docs.title: Welcome
docs.text:
Step-by-Step Introduction to the [Flutter] Mobile Framework

created by Anthropic’s AI Claude at the request of Serge Tahé - September 2026

This document is a translation of the original French version, generated using an automated tool. Some expressions or technical terms may not fully reflect the original meaning.

This course shows, step by step, how to write a mobile application with the Flutter framework and the Dart language: an Android application whose screens are built on the phone from the JSON data of a server. The same code also produces a web application.

After setting up the working environment, it relies on 25 small examples, each focused on a single concept: StatelessWidget and StatefulWidget, setState, the widget tree, input fields, validation with Form and FormField; widget composition, the widget life cycle, InheritedWidget, animations; routing with go_router and its guards; asynchronous code and shared state (Future, Stream, FutureBuilder, provider, shared_preferences); internationalization; and finally talking to the server.

The server is treated as a black box: it is the JSON server of the RdvMedecins application, written with NestJS. You install it, study its API and query it with 48 curl examples, without having to read its code.

Then comes a complete case study: the Flutter client of RdvMedecins, an appointment-booking application for a medical practice, in which every file is commented, followed by its deployment.

Prerequisites: the basics of the Dart language, presented in the course Introduction to the Dart Language Through Examples. The 25 examples have the same numbers as those of the React course; the same screens are also written with Vue.js and Angular.

All courses by Serge Tahé

docs.title: 14.1. Installing Flutter
docs.text:
The SDK and [Flutter] files can be downloaded from docs.flutter.dev (select [Windows], then [Android]). It is a simple compressed folder, which you extract into a folder named SANS (no spaces or accented characters, e.g., [C:\dev\flutter]), then add its subfolder [bin] to the user’s environment variable [Path]. The SDK and [Dart] files are included. Verify the installation in a new console:

flutter --version
flutter doctor

[flutter doctor] checks everything that [Flutter] requires: SDK, [Android], and its licenses, [Chrome], [Visual Studio] (for [Windows] applications), connected devices, and network access. Each line is preceded by a checkmark [√] if everything is okay, an X [X] or an exclamation point [!] otherwise, with instructions on what to do listed below. [flutter doctor -v] provides details (versions, paths).

The “Visual Studio” line applies only to [Windows] applications (the [windows/] examples folder): it may remain in error if you’re targeting only mobile and web.

In [Windows], projects that use native code packages ([shared_preferences]...) require the system’s “developer mode”: [flutter pub get] indicates this (“Building with plugins requires symlink support”). You can enable it in Settings / System / Developer Space (command [start ms-settings:developers]).

docs.title: 14.2. Installing Android Studio and an emulator
docs.text:
[Android Studio] can be downloaded from developer.android.com/studio. It is not used to write code, but to install the SDK [Android] and create an emulator:

  • Upon first launch, the wizard installs SDK and [Android];
  • More Actions menu / SDK Manager, SDK Tools tab: check “Android SDK Command-line Tools,” which [Flutter] requires;
  • in a console: [flutter doctor --android-licenses], and accept the licenses;
  • More Actions / Virtual Device Manager menu: create a virtual phone (for example, a “Pixel”) using a recent system image. Click the ▶ button to launch it; [flutter devices] will then detect it under the name [emulator-5554]. You can also launch it without opening [Android Studio]: [flutter emulators] lists the emulators, and [flutter emulators --launch <nom>] launches one.

For a real phone: In Settings / About Phone, tapping “Build Number” seven times brings up “Developer Options,” where you can enable “USB Debugging.” When connected to the computer, the phone will ask you to authorize the computer; [flutter devices] will then detect it.

docs.title: 14.3. Installing Visual Studio Code
docs.text:
[Visual Studio Code] is downloaded to code.visualstudio.com. In the Extensions panel (Ctrl-Shift-X), install the [Flutter] extension (from [Dart Code]), which also installs the [Dart] extension. They provide:

  • code completion, code validation as you type (using the rules from [analysis_options.yaml]), navigation to the definition of a widget or class, and renaming across the entire project;
  • code formatting upon saving ([dart format]);
  • device selection, in the lower-right corner of the window (or the “Flutter: Select Device” command);
  • launching via F5 (debugging: breakpoints, variables); each time a file is saved, the app is reloaded on the fly;
  • actions on widgets (Ctrl-. on a widget): “Wrap with Padding,” “Wrap with Column,” “Extract Widget,” etc.—very useful for reorganizing a widget tree.

To run an example using F5, open its file [main.dart] before pressing F5 (or create a file named [.vscode/launch.json]). Open a project via the File / Open Folder menu (the [exemples_flutter] folder, for example), and open a console via the Terminal / New Terminal menu.

docs.title: 14.4. The Flutter tool DevTools
docs.text:
[Flutter DevTools] is included with SDK. While the application is running, [flutter run] displays its address (“The Flutter DevTools debugger and profiler... is available at: http://127.0.0.1:9101... ”); in [VS Code], the “Flutter: Open DevTools” command opens it in the editor. Its most useful tabs:

  • “Flutter Inspector”: the widget tree for the screen, and the properties for each widget. “Select Widget Mode” lets you tap an element on the phone to find its widget in the tree; “Show Guidelines” draws the margins and alignment lines. This is the tool that answers the question, “Why isn’t this widget in the right place?”;
  • “Performance” and “CPU Profiler”: the time spent rendering and drawing each frame, to identify the cause of a choppy animation;
  • “Network”: the application’s HTTP requests, including their headers and bodies; here you can see the token cookie being sent and returned;
  • “Logging”: what the application displays ([debugPrint]).

docs.title: 14.5. Installation of Node.js
docs.text:
[Node.js] downloads to nodejs.org: select version LTS (long-term support). The [Windows] installer also installs [npm]. It is only required for the JSON server. Verify the installation in a console:

node --version
npm --version

docs.title: 14.6. Installing MySQL with Laragon
docs.text:
The JSON server requires [MySQL] (or [MariaDB]). [Laragon] (laragon.org) installs one under [Windows], ready to use, with the [HeidiSQL] administration tool. After installation:

  • the “Start All” button launches the [MySQL] server on port 3306;
  • the user [root] has no password: these are the default values from the server’s [.env.example] file;
  • in [HeidiSQL] (the “Database” button), the File / Run SQL File menu item runs the [database/dbrdvmedecins2.sql] script.

In [Linux] or [macOS], install [MySQL] or [MariaDB] using the system’s package manager, and run the script using the command-line client: [mysql -u root -p < database/dbrdvmedecins2.sql].

docs.title: 14.7. Installing curl
docs.text:
[curl] is included with [Windows] versions 10 and 11, [macOS], and most distributions of [Linux]. Check its version:

curl --version

The option [--json], used in this document, has been available since version 7.82 (2022). If you are using an older version, replace [--json @fichier] with [-H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @fichier], or install a recent version starting with curl.se.

In [PowerShell], you must enter [curl.exe], not [curl]: In [PowerShell], [curl] is an alias for another command ([Invoke-WebRequest]), which does not include the options from [curl]. The command prompt ([cmd]) does not have this issue.

docs.title: 6.1. Example 19: Future, Stream, and Timers
docs.text:
Many things happen “later”: timer ticks, keystrokes, a server’s response. [Dart] has two types for this, at the core of the language:

  • [Future<T>]: UNE value, later (a server’s response, a choice made in a window);
  • [Stream<T>]: a sequence of SUITE values over time (ticks, messages, GPS positions...).

[Flutter] has a widget to display each one, rebuilding it when a value arrives: [FutureBuilder] and [StreamBuilder]. And for what must happen after a delay: [Timer].

// =========================================================================
// lib/ex19_asynchrone/main.dart - Future, Stream, Timers
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Many things happen “later”: the ticks of a timer,
// keyboard keystrokes, a server’s response. Dart has two types for
// this, at the core of the language:
//    - Future<T>: a value, later (a server’s response);
//    - Stream<T>: a SUITE of values, over time (ticks,
//      messages...).
// Flutter has a widget to display each one, rebuilding it when a
// value arrives: FutureBuilder and StreamBuilder.
// And for what needs to happen after a delay: Timer (dart:async).
// =========================================================================

import 'dart:async';
import 'dart:math';

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

const medecins = ['Marie PELISSIER', 'Paul TATOU', 'Sophie DUPONT', 'Jacques DURAND', 'Martine PELLETIER'];
final _hasard = Random();

// A simulated “server”: the response (a Future) arrives after a random delay
Future<List<String>> rechercher(String texte) async {
  await Future<void>.delayed(Duration(milliseconds: 200 + _hasard.nextInt(600)));
  return medecins.where((m) => m.toLowerCase().contains(texte)).toList();
}

// 1. A Stream created by an “async*” function: each yield ENVOIE returns a
// value to those listening to the Stream
Stream<int> compteARebours(int depart) async* {
  for (var reste = depart; reste >= 0; reste--) {
    yield reste;
    if (reste > 0) await Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(seconds: 1));
  }
}

String heureCourante() => DateTime.now().toString().substring(11, 19);

void main() {
  runApp(
    MaterialApp(
      debugShowCheckedModeBanner: false,
      theme: ThemeData(colorSchemeSeed: Colors.indigo),
      home: const PageAsynchrone(),
    ),
  );
}

class PageAsynchrone extends StatefulWidget {
  const PageAsynchrone({super.key});

  @override
  State<PageAsynchrone> createState() => _PageAsynchroneState();
}

class _PageAsynchroneState extends State<PageAsynchrone> {
  final List<String> _journal = [];
   // The stream and the Future are created UNE times (and not on every build:
   // otherwise, every build call would restart the countdown!)
  final Stream<int> _rebours = compteARebours(20);
   // 3. A Future that completes after one second
  final Future<String> _message = Future.delayed(const Duration(seconds: 1), () => 'trois (une seconde plus tard)');

   // 2. search as you type
  Timer? _antiRebond;
  int _numeroRequete = 0; // the number of the DERNIÈRE search launched
  List<String> _resultats = [];

  void _tracer(String message) => setState(() => _journal.add('${heureCourante()} $message'));

   // called with each keystroke
  void _saisie(String texte) {
     // ANTI-REBOND: Each keystroke resets the timer for the
     // previous one; the search only starts after 400 ms without keystrokes
    _antiRebond?.cancel();
    _antiRebond = Timer(const Duration(milliseconds: 400), () => _lancer(texte.trim().toLowerCase()));
  }

  Future<void> _lancer(String texte) async {
     // fewer than two letters: no search, no results
    if (texte.length < 2) {
      _numeroRequete++; // a response still pending will be ignored
      setState(() => _resultats = []);
      return;
    }
     // "outdated": a response that arrives APRÈS after another search has been launched
     // search must be ignored (otherwise the slow response from an old
     // search would overwrite that of the new one)
    final numero = ++_numeroRequete;
    _tracer('recherche envoyée : « $texte »');
    final trouves = await rechercher(texte);
    if (!mounted) return;
    if (numero != _numeroRequete) {
      _tracer('réponse ignorée (périmée) : « $texte »');
      return;
    }
    setState(() => _resultats = trouves);
  }

  @override
  void dispose() {
    _antiRebond?.cancel();
    super.dispose();
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final styleTitre = Theme.of(context).textTheme.titleSmall;
    return Scaffold(
      appBar: AppBar(title: const Text("Exemple 19 - l'asynchrone")),
      body: ListView(
        padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16),
        children: [
          Card(
            child: Padding(
              padding: const EdgeInsets.all(12),
              child: Column(
                crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
                children: [
                  Text('Un compte à rebours (un Stream et StreamBuilder)', style: styleTitre),
                   // StreamBuilder: reconstructs its content with each value from the stream;
                   // etat.data: the last value received (null before the first)
                  StreamBuilder<int>(
                    stream: _rebours,
                    builder: (context, etat) =>
                        Text(etat.hasData ? '${etat.data}' : '...', style: Theme.of(context).textTheme.displaySmall),
                  ),
                ],
              ),
            ),
          ),
          Card(
            child: Padding(
              padding: const EdgeInsets.all(12),
              child: Column(
                crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
                children: [
                  Text('Une recherche au fil de la frappe (anti-rebond, réponses périmées)', style: styleTitre),
                  TextField(
                    decoration: const InputDecoration(hintText: 'au moins deux lettres : pel, dur...'),
                    onChanged: _saisie,
                  ),
                  for (final r in _resultats) Text('• $r'),
                  if (_resultats.isEmpty) const Text('aucun résultat', style: TextStyle(color: Colors.grey)),
                ],
              ),
            ),
          ),
          Card(
            child: Padding(
              padding: const EdgeInsets.all(12),
              child: Column(
                crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
                children: [
                  Text('Attendre un Future (FutureBuilder)', style: styleTitre),
                   // as long as the Future is not complete: the pending content
                  FutureBuilder<String>(
                    future: _message,
                    builder: (context, etat) => switch (etat.connectionState) {
                      ConnectionState.done => Text('reçu : ${etat.data}'),
                      _ => const Text('en attente...', style: TextStyle(color: Colors.grey)),
                    },
                  ),
                ],
              ),
            ),
          ),
          Text('Journal', style: styleTitre),
          for (final (i, ligne) in _journal.indexed) Text('${i + 1}. $ligne', style: const TextStyle(fontSize: 12)),
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}
  • lines 24–26: a simulated “server”: a function [async], whose response (a [Future]) arrives after a random delay. [await Future<void>.delayed(...)] waits for this delay without blocking the application;
  • lines 31–34: a [Stream] generated by a function [async*] (with an asterisk): an asynchronous generator. Each [yield] sends a value to those listening to [Stream]; between values, the function waits one second;
  • lines 61–63: the [Stream] and the [Future] are created UNE times, in fields of the [State] object, and not in [build]: Each rebuild would restart the countdown! This is the most common error with [FutureBuilder] and [StreamBuilder];
  • lines 66–68: the status of the search as the user types: a timer, the number of the last search initiated, and the results;
  • lines 73–77: debouncing: the program waits for the user to pause before querying the server, rather than sending a request with every keystroke. Each keystroke resets the timer from the previous keystroke ([cancel()]) and starts a new one: the search is only triggered after 400 milliseconds without a keystroke;
  • Lines 80–98: the search. An “out-of-date” response (one that arrives—APRÈS—after another search has been launched) must be ignored: otherwise, the slow response from an old search would override that of the new one. Each search is assigned a number ([++_numeroRequete]); when its response arrives, if it is no longer the number of the most recent search, it is ignored. [if (!mounted) return;]: the screen may have disappeared while waiting;
  • lines 102–104: the timer is stopped if the screen disappears;
  • lines 124–127: [StreamBuilder] listens for [Stream] and reconstructs its content with each new value. [builder] receives a snapshot ([etat], a [AsyncSnapshot]): [etat.hasData], [etat.data] (the last value received), [etat.hasError], [etat.connectionState]. When the widget disappears, [StreamBuilder] unsubscribes on its own;
  • lines 158–162: [FutureBuilder] waits for [Future]: until it is finished, the placeholder content; then, its value. [switch] on [etat.connectionState] chooses one or the other.

We type “p,” “pe,” “pel” quickly: only one search is sent. Then “du,” followed by “dup” before the response: the response to “du” arrives too late, and it is ignored if “dup” has already received its response:

In [JavaScript], the same thing is written using promises and timers; [Angular] adds the "observables" from [RxJS]. In [Dart], [Future] and [Stream] are in the base library, and [async], [await], [async*], [yield], and [await for] are in the language: this is why [Flutter] does not require a library for asynchronous operations.

docs.title: 6.2. Example 20: A Shared State
docs.text:
Same question as in previous lessons: what are the “scopes” for an application’s data?

  • A widget’s local state disappears when the widget is removed;
  • the state of a “store” is shared by all widgets and survives their removal… but not the application’s shutdown;
  • State stored on the device survives when the application is shut down.

docs.title: 6.2.1. The shopping cart
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex20_etat_partage/stores/panier.dart - a ÉTAT PARTAGÉ, with a provider
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A “store” is a state that consists of HORS screens, in a single
// instance, shared by everyone who reads it. Example 14 did this
// manually (InheritedNotifier); the provider package, the most commonly used
// with Flutter (and recommended by its documentation), does the same thing
// in a single line:
//
//      ChangeNotifierProvider(create: (_) => Cart(), child: ...)
//
// The store is a regular ChangeNotifier. Standard structure:
//    - the ÉTAT: PRIVÉES data (_articles);
//    - ACTIONS: methods that modify the state and end with
//      with notifyListeners();
//    - calculated values: getters.
// A widget accesses it through its context:
//    - context.watch<Shopping  Cart>() : read ET, subscribe (rebuilt with every change);
//    - context.read<Shopping   Cart>() : read without subscribing (to call an action);
//    - context.select<Cart, int>((p) => p.nombre): subscribe to the value of UNE:
//      reconstructed only if the value of CETTE changes.
// The store lives as long as its supplier lives: it survives the removal of a
// screen... but not when the application stops.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';

typedef Article = ({String libelle, double prix});

class Panier extends ChangeNotifier {
  final List<Article> _articles = [];

   // A view NON MODIFIABLE of the list: only actions change it
  List<Article> get articles => List.unmodifiable(_articles);
  int get nombre => _articles.length;
  double get total => _articles.fold(0, (s, a) => s + a.prix);

  void ajouter(Article article) {
    _articles.add(article);
    notifyListeners();
  }

  void vider() {
    _articles.clear();
    notifyListeners();
  }
}

A store is a state that spans multiple screens, existing as a single instance shared by all who access it. Example 14 implemented this manually. The [provider] package, the most commonly used one along with [Flutter] (and the one recommended in its documentation), does the same thing in a single line: [ChangeNotifierProvider(create: (_) => Panier(), child: ...)].

  • Line 31: the state: private data;
  • lines 34–36: calculated values: getters. [List.unmodifiable]: a read-only view of the list; only actions can modify it;
  • lines 38–45: the actions: methods—the only ones that modify the state—which end with [notifyListeners()].

docs.title: 6.2.2. Preferences
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex20_etat_partage/stores/preferences.dart - a state that survives shutdown
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// For data to survive a shutdown of the application, it must be saved
// SUR The APPAREIL. The shared_preferences package provides a small dictionary
// key -> value (bool, int, double, String), specific to the app and
// stored on the device (on the web: in the browser's localStorage).
//    - at startup, the stored values are read (main.dart);
//    - they are rewritten with every change.
// No sensitive data (passwords, tokens) is stored here: they
// are stored in plain text.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';
import 'package:shared_preferences/shared_preferences.dart';

class Preferences extends ChangeNotifier {
  static const _cleSombre = 'exemple20.sombre';
  static const _cleTaille = 'exemple20.taille';

  final SharedPreferences _stockage;
  bool _sombre;
  double _taille; // text size

   // the initial state: what the device has stored; otherwise, the default values
  Preferences(this._stockage)
    : _sombre = _stockage.getBool(_cleSombre) ?? false,
      _taille = _stockage.getDouble(_cleTaille) ?? 16;

  bool get sombre => _sombre;
  double get taille => _taille;

   // a parameter designated as optional by preference: only the provided value is changed
  void modifier({bool? sombre, double? taille}) {
    if (sombre != null) {
      _sombre = sombre;
      _stockage.setBool(_cleSombre, sombre); // text on the device
    }
    if (taille != null) {
      _taille = taille;
      _stockage.setDouble(_cleTaille, taille);
    }
    notifyListeners();
  }
}

For data to survive after the application is shut down, it must be stored on the device. The [shared_preferences] package provides a small key->value dictionary ([bool], [int], [double], [String]), specific to the application and stored on the device (on the web: in the browser’s [localStorage]).

  • Line 21: the storage data, received upon creation;
  • lines 26–28: the initial state: what the device has stored, or default values otherwise. The fields are initialized by the manufacturer’s “initialization list” (after the colon), before the body;
  • Lines 34–43: a single action, with optional named parameters: only the provided values are changed, and they are immediately written to the device ([setBool], [setDouble]).

Do not store any sensitive data (passwords, tokens) such as JAMAIS there: such data is written in plain text. For this purpose, there is the [flutter_secure_storage] package, which uses the system’s vault ([Keystore] from [Android], [Keychain] from [iOS]).

docs.title: 6.2.3. The widgets
docs.text:
// lib/ex20_etat_partage/components/boutique.dart - AJOUTE to the shared cart
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:provider/provider.dart';

import '../magasins/panier.dart';

const produits = <Article>[(libelle: 'Consultation', prix: 30), (libelle: 'Vaccin', prix: 12.5)];

class Boutique extends StatelessWidget {
  const Boutique({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
     // Note: Only one action is performed; the shopping cart is not
     // rebuilt when the cart changes
    final panier = context.read<Panier>();
    return Card(
      child: Padding(
        padding: const EdgeInsets.all(12),
        child: Column(
          crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
          children: [
            Text('Boutique', style: Theme.of(context).textTheme.titleSmall),
            for (final p in produits)
              TextButton.icon(
                icon: const Icon(Icons.add),
                label: Text('${p.libelle} (${p.prix} €)'),
                onPressed: () => panier.ajouter(p),
              ),
          ],
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}
  • Line 16: [context.read<Panier>()] reads the shopping cart provided above; SANS subscribes: the store simply calls an action; it does not need to be rebuilt when the shopping cart changes. 
// lib/ex20_etat_partage/components/resume_panier.dart - LIT: same shopping cart
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:provider/provider.dart';

import '../magasins/panier.dart';

class ResumePanier extends StatelessWidget {
  const ResumePanier({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
     // select: rebuilds SEULEMENT if the quantity or total changes
    final nombre = context.select<Panier, int>((p) => p.nombre);
    final total = context.select<Panier, double>((p) => p.total);
    return Card(
      child: Padding(
        padding: const EdgeInsets.all(12),
        child: Row(
          children: [
            const Icon(Icons.shopping_cart),
            const SizedBox(width: 8),
            Expanded(child: Text('$nombre article(s), $total €')),
            TextButton(
              onPressed: nombre == 0 ? null : () => context.read<Panier>().vider(),
              child: const Text('Vider'),
            ),
          ],
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}
  • Lines 13–14: [context.select] reads the shopping cart value from UNE and subscribes the widget to the value from CETTE: it is rebuilt only if that value changes. [context.watch<Panier>()] would read and subscribe to the entire shopping cart. 
// lib/ex20_etat_partage/components/compteur_local.dart - a LOCAL state, which disappears with the widget
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

class CompteurLocal extends StatefulWidget {
  final String titre;

  const CompteurLocal({super.key, required this.titre});

  @override
  State<CompteurLocal> createState() => _CompteurLocalState();
}

class _CompteurLocalState extends State<CompteurLocal> {
  int _clics = 0;

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Card(
      child: ListTile(
        title: Text(widget.titre),
        trailing: OutlinedButton(onPressed: () => setState(() => _clics++), child: Text('$_clics clic(s)')),
      ),
    );
  }
}

A local state that disappears with the widget.

docs.title: 6.2.4. The application
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex20_etat_partage/main.dart - three "ranges" of data
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
//    - the state LOCAL of a widget (CompteurLocal) disappears along with it;
//    - the state of a MAGASIN (the shopping cart) is shared by all widgets
//      and survives their removal—but not when the application is shut down;
//    - the state stored on the device (preferences) survives shutdown.
// And Visibility(maintainState: true): the content is CACHÉ, but not
// removed; its local state is preserved.
// Uncheck and then recheck "Show Field," then stop and restart
// the app: compare the results.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:provider/provider.dart';
import 'package:shared_preferences/shared_preferences.dart';

import 'composants/boutique.dart';
import 'composants/compteur_local.dart';
import 'composants/resume_panier.dart';
import 'magasins/panier.dart';
import 'magasins/preferences.dart';

Future<void> main() async {
   // Essential before using a "plugin" (Android-specific code, iOS,
   // web...) such as shared_preferences, AVANT, runApp
  WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized();
  final stockage = await SharedPreferences.getInstance();
  runApp(
     // MultiProvider: multiple providers, nested within one another,
     // above the entire application
    MultiProvider(
      providers: [
        ChangeNotifierProvider(create: (_) => Panier()),
        ChangeNotifierProvider(create: (_) => Preferences(stockage)),
      ],
      child: const Application(),
    ),
  );
}

class Application extends StatelessWidget {
  const Application({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
     // watch: the app is rebuilt when preferences change
    final preferences = context.watch<Preferences>();
    return MaterialApp(
      debugShowCheckedModeBanner: false,
      theme: ThemeData(colorSchemeSeed: Colors.indigo),
       // dark theme, and the choice between the two
      darkTheme: ThemeData(colorSchemeSeed: Colors.indigo, brightness: Brightness.dark),
      themeMode: preferences.sombre ? ThemeMode.dark : ThemeMode.light,
       // builder: wraps TOUS around the screens; here, the text size
      builder: (context, child) => MediaQuery(
        data: MediaQuery.of(context).copyWith(textScaler: TextScaler.linear(preferences.taille / 16)),
        child: child!,
      ),
      home: const PageEtatPartage(),
    );
  }
}

class PageEtatPartage extends StatefulWidget {
  const PageEtatPartage({super.key});

  @override
  State<PageEtatPartage> createState() => _PageEtatPartageState();
}

class _PageEtatPartageState extends State<PageEtatPartage> {
  bool _zoneVisible = true;

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final preferences = context.watch<Preferences>();
    return Scaffold(
      appBar: AppBar(title: const Text('Exemple 20 - un état partagé')),
      body: ListView(
        padding: const EdgeInsets.all(12),
        children: [
          SwitchListTile(
            title: const Text('thème sombre'),
            value: preferences.sombre,
            onChanged: (v) => preferences.modifier(sombre: v),
          ),
          ListTile(
            title: Text('taille du texte : ${preferences.taille.round()}'),
            subtitle: Slider(
              value: preferences.taille,
              min: 12,
              max: 22,
              divisions: 10,
              onChanged: (v) => preferences.modifier(taille: v),
            ),
          ),
          CheckboxListTile(
            title: const Text('afficher la zone'),
            value: _zoneVisible,
            onChanged: (v) => setState(() => _zoneVisible = v!),
          ),
           // removed: these widgets disappear, along with their local state
          if (_zoneVisible) ...[const Boutique(), const ResumePanier(), const CompteurLocal(titre: 'État local')],
           // hidden: the widget remains in memory, and its state is preserved
          Visibility(
            visible: _zoneVisible,
            maintainState: true,
            child: const CompteurLocal(titre: 'État local, dans un Visibility'),
          ),
          const Padding(
            padding: EdgeInsets.symmetric(vertical: 8),
            child: Text('Hors de la zone, un second résumé du MÊME panier (il reste là quand la zone disparaît) :'),
          ),
          const ResumePanier(),
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}
  • Lines 27–28: [shared_preferences] is a "plugin": it uses platform-specific code ([Android], web...). To use AVANT and [runApp], you must first initialize [Flutter] ([ensureInitialized]). Reading from storage is asynchronous: [main] waits for it to complete;
  • lines 32–35: [MultiProvider] places multiple providers, one inside the other, at the top of the entire application. [ChangeNotifierProvider] creates [ChangeNotifier] ([create]), provides it to its descendants, rebuilds those that subscribe to it when it changes, and releases it when it disappears;
  • line 48: the application reads the preferences and subscribes to them; it is rebuilt when they change;
  • lines 53–54: two themes, light and dark, and the option to choose between them ([themeMode]);
  • lines 56–58: the [builder] from [MaterialApp] wraps the screens in TOUS. Here, the text size for the entire app is changed: [MediaQuery] describes the screen and the user’s settings (including [textScaler], the text magnification factor, which can also be adjusted in the phone’s accessibility settings);
  • line 104: removed; the area disappears, along with the local state of its widgets;
  • Lines 106–109: [Visibility] with [maintainState: true] and CACHE—its child—without removing it: its state is preserved. (This is what [<Activity mode="hidden">] does in the [React] course.)

We add two items, click once on each local counter (on the left); we remove the area and switch to dark mode (in the middle); we restore the area (on the right):

The shopping cart survived the removal of the section (as shown in the second summary); the removed counter reset to zero; the hidden counter retained its value. Stop the app and restart it: the dark theme and text size are preserved, and the shopping cart is empty.

Why [provider]? There are many state management libraries for [Flutter] ([Riverpod], [Bloc], [GetX], [MobX]...). [provider] is the simplest: it is simply a convenient way to write the [InheritedWidget] from Example 14, based on the [ChangeNotifier] from [Flutter]. This is the one used in the architecture guide for the [Flutter] documentation, and the one that will be used in the case study.

docs.title: 11. Case Study: The Flutter client for the RdvMedecins application
11.1. The Problem
docs.text:
The [RdvMedecins] app allows users to schedule appointments at a doctor's office. The [NestJS] course developed it as a HTML application, in which the server generated the pages; the [Vue.js], [Angular], and [React] wrote web clients for it, which generate the MÊMES pages in the browser, based on the JSON data from the server presented in the chapter “The RdvMedecins Server, a Black Box.” Here we describe the [Flutter] client: a mobile application ([Android]), which can also be compiled for the web.

The client must provide everything the others did:

  • a login screen, protected by a CAPTCHA, with the option to create a patient account;
  • a doctor’s schedule for a given day, with appointment booking (patient selection window) and cancellation;
  • for the administrator, management of doctors and clients (list, add, edit, delete);
  • for the patient, a personal dashboard (showing upcoming appointments, which they can cancel) and account management;
  • two languages: French and English;
  • the same addresses as the web clients ([/agenda?idMedecin=1&jour=...]). On the phone, they are invisible but organize the app; on the web, users can reload them, bookmark them, and navigate the app using the browser’s Back/Forward buttons.

A mobile app adds its own requirements: a narrow screen (no five-column tables), a keyboard that hides half the screen, a Back button, a password manager, and the absence of a browser to store the token cookie.

docs.title: 11.2. Installation and Execution
docs.text:
The JSON server must be installed and running (see the chapter “The RdvMedecins Server: A Black Box”). You do not need the CAPTCHA test mode: you can leave the [CAPTCHA_TEST] field blank in the [.env] file on the server.

In a console window open to the [rdvmedecins_flutter] folder:

flutter create --platforms=android,web --org fr.stahe --project-name rdvmedecins_flutter .
flutter pub get

The first command adds the platform-specific folders ([android/], [web/]) to the project, as in the examples; it does not modify any existing files, and the delivered [android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml] file (the one from Example 22) is retained. Then, choose one of the following:

flutter run -d emulator-5554
flutter run -d R58N12ABCDE --dart-define=SERVEUR=http://192.168.1.20:8080
flutter run -d chrome
  • The first line launches the application on the [Android] emulator (the [flutter devices] command lists the available devices). The emulator connects to the server at the address [10.0.2.2:8080] (see Example 22);
  • the second line runs the app on a real phone connected via USB (with “USB debugging” enabled in its developer options) or connected via Wi-Fi. The phone and computer must be on the same network; enter the computer’s address on this network ([ipconfig] under [Windows]). The firewall on [Windows] must allow incoming connections on port 8080;
  • the third, on [Chrome], at the address http://localhost:5173: the web development server in [Flutter] forwards /api requests to the server in JSON (file [web_dev_config.yaml]).

The demo accounts are listed on the login screen (password = login). While the application is running, the [r] key on the console performs a "hot reload" after a code change; [R] restarts it; [q] stops it.

docs.title: 11.4. Client Architecture
docs.text:
rdvmedecins_flutter/
├── pubspec.yaml               les bibliothèques, les ressources
├── analysis_options.yaml      les règles de l'analyseur de code
├── web_dev_config.yaml        le serveur de développement web (proxy /api)
├── android/                   le projet Android (dont AndroidManifest.xml)
├── web/                       la page HTML de la version web
├── assets/
│   ├── i18n/                  les dictionnaires fr.json, en.json
│   └── polices/               la police RobotoMono
├── test/                      tests unitaires ; fabrication des copies d'écran
└── lib/
    ├── main.dart              le démarrage
    ├── config.dart            l'adresse du serveur
    ├── routeur.dart           les écrans, leurs adresses, leurs droits
    ├── formatage.dart         la mise en forme des heures et des jours
    ├── api/                   la couche d'accès à l'API
    ├── i18n/                  les langues
    ├── etat/                  session, messages, cache (ChangeNotifier)
    ├── widgets/               le gabarit et les widgets réutilisables
    └── pages/                 les écrans

This is the architecture recommended by the [Flutter] guide (“App architecture”), explained more simply:

  • a data layer ([api/]): the only layer that knows the [http] package, the URLs, and the JSON;
  • a state layer ([etat/]): [ChangeNotifier] objects provided to the entire application ([provider]), which the screens monitor;
  • an interface layer ([pages/], [widgets/]): widgets that display the state and transmit user actions.

The following table compares the HTML application from the [NestJS] course, the [React] client, and this client:

Application HTML (NestJS)React clientFlutter clientThe server renders each page ([res.render])Components render the pages in the browserWidgets render the screens on the phone[views/layout.hbs] and its partial views[Gabarit.tsx] and the components[gabarit.dart] (a [ShellRoute]) and the widgetscontroller routes[React Router][go_router][JwtAuthGuard], [RolesGuard]router guards (middleware)The router's [redirect] functionthe token cookie, stored by the browsersame as aboveA HTTP client that manages cookies (on the phone)flash message in a cookiea store named [Zustand]a [ChangeNotifier], [Messages]dictionaries read by the server[i18next][Traductions] (example 21)language stored in a cookiein [localStorage]in [shared_preferences]data already read[TanStack Query][Cache] (a few lines)Form rejected: the server reloads the page400/409 response, errors below the fieldssame as above

All of the client’s files are presented below. They are extensively commented; their comments are part of the course.

docs.title: 11.6.1. lib/config.dart
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/config.dart - Is OÙ the server JSON?
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// This question does not arise for a web application served by the
// server itself: requests are sent to the origin that the page
// (a relative address, /api/...). But a MOBILE application does not
// origin: you must provide it with the full server address.
//    - The Android emulator sees the computer running it at
//      the address 10.0.2.2 (localhost, which, to the emulator, is the emulator itself);
//    - a real phone, connected to the same Wi-Fi network as the computer, must
//      use the computer’s address on that network (192.168.1.20...):
//      you provide it when launching the app:
//          flutter run --dart-define=SERVEUR=http://192.168.1.20:8080 ...
//    - in web development mode (flutter run -d chrome), the Flutter development server
//      Flutter development server forwards /api requests to the JSON server
//      (file web_dev_config.yaml): a relative address is sufficient;
//    - on a computer (Windows, macOS, Linux): localhost.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';

// the value specified by --dart-define=SERVEUR=..., default is '';
// String.fromEnvironment evaluates to COMPILATION: this is a constant
const _serveurImpose = String.fromEnvironment('SERVEUR');

class Config {
   // kIsWeb: true if the application is running in a browser;
   // defaultTargetPlatform: the system (Android, iOS, Windows...)
  static String urlServeur = _serveurImpose.isNotEmpty
      ? _serveurImpose
      : kIsWeb
      ? '' // same origin: relative addresses
      : defaultTargetPlatform == TargetPlatform.android
      ? 'http://10.0.2.2:8080'
      : 'http://localhost:8080';
}

The server address, depending on the platform (see Example 22):

  • line 24: the value provided at launch by [--dart-define=SERVEUR=...]. [String.fromEnvironment] is evaluated at compile time: the address is embedded in the built application;
  • lines 29–35: otherwise, a relative address on the web (the development server, then the JSON server itself in production, serve the page ET and API), [10.0.2.2] on [Android] (the computer, as seen from the emulator), [localhost] elsewhere. [static]: a class variable, not an object variable; not [final], so that the tests can modify it.

docs.title: 11.6.2. lib/main.dart
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/main.dart - application startup
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// We create, once and for all, the objects shared by the entire
// the application, then we pass them to all screens (provider):
//    - the HTTP client (which manages the token cookie on the phone) and the
//      access layer to the API;
//    - the session (who is logged in?), messages, and data cache;
//    - translations (French, English);
//    - the router, which displays the screen showing the current address.
// Two mechanisms link these objects together:
//    1. the 401 response to a protected request (session expired): the user is logged out
//       the user and prepare the message; the router, which is listening for the
//       session, then redirects to the login screen (see api/client_api.dart);
//    2. “Flash” messages: at the end of CHAQUE navigation, the messages
//       from the previous screen disappear, and the following messages
//       appear (see status/messages.dart).
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:flutter_localizations/flutter_localizations.dart';
import 'package:flutter_web_plugins/url_strategy.dart';
import 'package:go_router/go_router.dart';
import 'package:intl/date_symbol_data_local.dart';
import 'package:provider/provider.dart';
import 'package:shared_preferences/shared_preferences.dart';

import 'api/client_api.dart';
import 'api/client_http.dart';
import 'api/rdvmedecins_api.dart';
import 'etat/cache.dart';
import 'etat/messages.dart';
import 'etat/session.dart';
import 'i18n/traductions.dart';
import 'routeur.dart';

Future<void> main() async {
  WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized();
  usePathUrlStrategy(); // on the web: /agenda rather than /#/agenda
  await initializeDateFormatting();
  final stockage = await SharedPreferences.getInstance();
  final traductions = Traductions(stockage);
  await traductions.demarrer();
  runApp(Application(stockage: stockage, traductions: traductions));
}

class Application extends StatefulWidget {
  final SharedPreferences stockage;
  final Traductions traductions;

  const Application({super.key, required this.stockage, required this.traductions});

  @override
  State<Application> createState() => _ApplicationState();
}

class _ApplicationState extends State<Application> {
  late final ClientApi _client = ClientApi(ClientAvecCookies(widget.stockage));
  late final RdvMedecinsApi _api = RdvMedecinsApi(_client);
  late final Session _session = Session(_api);
  final Messages _messages = Messages();
  final Cache _cache = Cache();
  late final GoRouter _routeur = creerRouteur(_session, _messages, _api);
  String? _adresse;

  @override
  void initState() {
    super.initState();
     // 1. Session expired
    _client.onSessionExpiree = () {
      _session.oublier();
      _cache.vider();
      _messages.flash(succes: false, cle: 'ERRORS.SESSION_EXPIRED');
       // no _routeur.go('/login'): the router handles this, and
       // saves the current screen (?redirect=...) to return to it
    };
     // the session changes (login, logout): the data read for
     // the previous user is no longer valid
    _session.addListener(_cache.vider);
     // 2. After each navigation is complete (the address has changed): new page
    _routeur.routerDelegate.addListener(() {
       // state: the DESSUS screen on the stack (including one screen pushed onto the stack)
      final adresse = _routeur.state.uri.toString();
      if (adresse != _adresse) {
        _adresse = adresse;
        _messages.nouvellePage();
      }
    });
  }

  @override
  void dispose() {
    _routeur.dispose();
    super.dispose();
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return MultiProvider(
      providers: [
         // ordinary objects...
        Provider.value(value: _api),
         // ... and objects that notify of their changes
        ChangeNotifierProvider.value(value: _cache),
        ChangeNotifierProvider.value(value: _session),
        ChangeNotifierProvider.value(value: _messages),
        ChangeNotifierProvider.value(value: widget.traductions),
      ],
      child: Consumer<Traductions>(
        builder: (context, traductions, _) => MaterialApp.router(
          debugShowCheckedModeBanner: false,
          onGenerateTitle: (context) => traductions.t('APP.TITLE'),
          theme: ThemeData(colorSchemeSeed: const Color(0xFF0D6EFD)),
           // Flutter’s own text (calendar...) in the selected language
          locale: Locale(traductions.langue),
          supportedLocales: [for (final l in langues) Locale(l)],
          localizationsDelegates: GlobalMaterialLocalizations.delegates,
          routerConfig: _routeur,
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}
  • lines 37–44: Before displaying anything, we prepare what needs to be prepared: web addresses without [#] (example 17), the names of days and months in all languages ([intl], example 09), the device’s storage, and the source language dictionary. [WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized()]: These operations require the [Flutter] engine, so we start it before [runApp];
  • lines 58–63: the shared objects, created UNE times, in the root widget’s state. Each receives the ones it needs upon creation: this is dependency injection, done manually. [late]: Initialization occurs upon first use, when [widget] already exists;
  • lines 70–76: 1. the expired session. The access layer for API is unaware of either the session or the messages; it is entrusted with this function, which it will call upon every 401 response. The user is forgotten, the cache is cleared, and the message for the next screen is prepared. The screen transition itself is handled by the router, which monitors the session;
  • line 79: every time the user changes, the cache is cleared: the data read for the previous user is of no use to the next one (a patient should not see the calendar viewed by the administrator);
  • Lines 81–88: 2. Flash messages. The router’s [routerDelegate] alerts its listeners with each transmission; the address is compared to the previous one ([_routeur.state]: the screen state of the stack’s DESSUS, including a screen stacked by [push], such as the reservation window), and, if it has changed, the system moves to a “new page”: the messages from the previous screen disappear, and those placed on this one appear (see [messages.dart]);
  • lines 99–107: shared objects are provided to all screens (Example 20). [.value]: the object already exists; the provider does not create it (and will not destroy it);
  • lines 109–118: the application itself, rebuilt with every language change ([Consumer], see Example 20): the title ([onGenerateTitle]), and the language of the text in [Flutter] itself (the calendar, tooltips). [colorSchemeSeed]: a color from which [Material] derives the entire palette; this is the blue of [Bootstrap], the color used by web clients.

docs.title: 11.7. The access layer to the API
11.7.1. lib/api/client_http.dart
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/api/client_http.dart - a HTTP client that handles COOKIES
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The RdvMedecins server places the JWT token in a COOKIE (httpOnly).
// In a browser, it is the browser that stores cookies and
// sends them back with every request: the application code has nothing to do with it.
// On a phone, there is no PAS browser: it’s up to the app to
// take on that role, which means:
//    1. read the "Set-Cookie" header in each response and store the cookies;
//    2. send them back in the “Cookie” header of each request.
// This client (HTTP) does this; in ENVELOPPANT, the client in the HTTP package
// (http.BaseClient: simply call the `send` method). The cookies are
// also stored on the device (shared_preferences): you remain logged in
// even when you close and then reopen the app.
// On the web, it does nothing more than a regular client: the
// browser prevents the app from reading or writing these headers.
// =========================================================================

import 'dart:convert';

import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';
import 'package:http/http.dart' as http;
import 'package:shared_preferences/shared_preferences.dart';

class ClientAvecCookies extends http.BaseClient {
  static const _cle = 'rdvmedecins.cookies';

  final http.Client _interne = http.Client();
  final SharedPreferences? _stockage;
   // cookie name -> its value
  final Map<String, String> _cookies = {};

  ClientAvecCookies([this._stockage]) {
     // cookies stored from a previous session
    final memorises = _stockage?.getString(_cle);
    if (memorises != null) {
      _cookies.addAll((jsonDecode(memorises) as Map<String, Object?>).cast<String, String>());
    }
  }

  @override
  Future<http.StreamedResponse> send(http.BaseRequest requete) async {
    if (!kIsWeb && _cookies.isNotEmpty) {
       // "rdvmedecins_jwt=eyJhbGci...; other=value"
      requete.headers['cookie'] = [for (final MapEntry(:key, :value) in _cookies.entries) '$key=$value'].join('; ');
    }
    final reponse = await _interne.send(requete);
    final setCookie = reponse.headers['set-cookie'];
    if (!kIsWeb && setCookie != null) {
      _memoriser(setCookie);
    }
    return reponse;
  }

   // Set-Cookie: rdvmedecins_jwt=eyJ...; Max-Age=7200; Path=/api; Expires=Tue, Sep 29, 2026 ...; HttpOnly
   // (multiple cookies are separated by commas). We only keep the
   // name and value of each cookie; an empty value (logout) deletes it
  void _memoriser(String setCookie) {
     // a name followed by "=", at the beginning of the header or after a comma
    for (final m in RegExp(r'(?:^|,)\s*([^=;,\s]+)=([^;]*)').allMatches(setCookie)) {
      final nom = m[1]!;
      final valeur = m[2]!.trim();
      if (valeur.isEmpty) {
        _cookies.remove(nom);
      } else {
        _cookies[nom] = valeur;
      }
    }
    _stockage?.setString(_cle, jsonEncode(_cookies));
  }

  @override
  void close() => _interne.close();
}

The HTTP client from Example 23, unchanged: it stores the received cookies ([Set-Cookie] header) and sends them back ([Cookie] header) to the phone; on the web, it lets the browser handle it.

docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/api/client_api.dart - TOUTES requests to API go through here
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Taken from the examples in commun/api.dart, with a new feature: centralized handling
// centralized handling of the 401 response.
//
// A 401 can occur at any time: the token has expired (2 hours), the
// account has been deleted, or the server has restarted with a different key
// is hidden... Rather than handling this case on every screen, it is handled
// ICI, just once. But this file knows neither the router nor the messages
// (it is independent of anything else): it calls a function that was assigned to it at
// startup (onSessionExpiree, see main.dart), which ignores the user and
// redirects to the login page.
//
// Some requests handle their own 401 responses (login, GET
// /api/auth/me...): these are "public" (see rdvmedecins_api.dart).
// =========================================================================

import 'dart:convert';

import 'package:http/http.dart' as http;

import '../config.dart';
import 'erreur_api.dart';

class ClientApi {
  final http.Client _client;
   // What to do when the server returns a 401 response to a protected request
  void Function() onSessionExpiree = () {};

  ClientApi(this._client);

   // public: true for routes that handle the 401 themselves
  Future<Object?> requete(String methode, String url, {Object? corps, bool publique = false}) async {
    final requete = http.Request(methode, Uri.parse('${Config.urlServeur}/api$url'));
    if (corps != null) {
      requete.headers['content-type'] = 'application/json';
      requete.body = jsonEncode(corps);
    }
    final http.Response reponse;
    try {
      reponse = await http.Response.fromStream(await _client.send(requete));
    } catch (_) {
       // No response: network down, server stopped, incorrect address
      throw const ErreurApi(0, 'ERRORS.SERVER_UNREACHABLE');
    }
    if (reponse.statusCode >= 400) {
      final erreur = ErreurApi.depuisReponse(reponse);
      if (erreur.statusCode == 401 && !publique) {
        onSessionExpiree();
         // The screen that was waiting for the response will also display the CE message
        throw const ErreurApi(401, 'ERRORS.SESSION_EXPIRED');
      }
      throw erreur;
    }
    return reponse.bodyBytes.isEmpty ? null : jsonDecode(utf8.decode(reponse.bodyBytes));
  }
}

The [commun/api.dart] file from the examples, with a new feature: the 401 response.

  • Line 29: a function to call in the event of a 401 error, specified at startup (see [main.dart]). By default, it does nothing;
  • line 34: [publique] is a named, optional parameter (enclosed in curly braces): [requete('GET', '/captcha', publique: true)];
  • lines 35–38: the request, built piece by piece: method, address, header, and body JSON;
  • lines 40–45: the request is sent. An exception here means that no response was received (network down, server down, incorrect address). [final http.Response reponse;]: a variable [final] declared without a value; [Dart] checks that it receives a value—only once—before being read;
  • lines 47–54: an error response becomes a [ErreurApi]. A 401 on a protected request means the session has expired: [onSessionExpiree] is called, then an error is triggered anyway (the screen that was waiting for the response must know that it did not arrive), using the key [ERRORS.SESSION_EXPIRED]: if this screen displays the error, it is the same message;
  • line 56: a response with no body (204) yields [null]. We decode the bytes to UTF-8: without the header [charset], the packet [http] would decode to [reponse.body] in Latin-1, and the accents would be corrupted.

docs.title: 11.7.3. lib/api/erreur_api.dart
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/api/erreur_api.dart - UNE class for all API errors
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// All error responses from the RdvMedecins server have the same format:
//    { "statusCode": 409, "key": "ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN", "params": {...}, "fields": {...} }
// But a request can also fail (AUTREMENT): no response at all
// (network down, server down, incorrect address), or a response that
// doesn’t come from our server (an error page from a proxy). We convert
// all of this into the UNE class, ErreurApi, which carries the translation key
// sent by the server (and, if any, its parameters and the error for
// for each field).
// =========================================================================

import 'dart:convert';

import 'package:http/http.dart' as http;

// "implements Exception": an object that can be thrown and caught
class ErreurApi implements Exception {
  final int statusCode; // 0: the server did not respond
  final String cle; // e.g., 'ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN'
  final Map<String, String> params;
  final Map<String, String> champs;

  const ErreurApi(this.statusCode, this.cle, {this.params = const {}, this.champs = const {}});

   // an error response (4xx, 5xx) -> a ErreurApi
  factory ErreurApi.depuisReponse(http.Response reponse) {
    Object? corps;
    try {
      corps = jsonDecode(utf8.decode(reponse.bodyBytes));
    } on FormatException {
      corps = null; // not JSON: this response did not come from our server
    }
     // "filtering" (pattern matching) of a Map: if the body has a key
     // "key" of type String, it is stored in the variable key
    if (corps case {'cle': final String cle}) {
      final json = corps as Map<String, Object?>;
      return ErreurApi(reponse.statusCode, cle, params: _chaines(json['params']), champs: _chaines(json['champs']));
    }
     // No key: the proxy or the network responded instead
    return ErreurApi(
      reponse.statusCode,
      reponse.statusCode >= 500 ? 'ERRORS.SERVER_UNREACHABLE' : 'ERRORS.SERVER_ERROR',
    );
  }

   // an object JSON { "name": "ERRORS..." } -> Map<String, String> (empty otherwise)
  static Map<String, String> _chaines(Object? json) =>
      json is Map<String, Object?> ? {for (final e in json.entries) e.key: '${e.value}'} : const {};

  @override
  String toString() => '$statusCode $cle';
}

The one from Example 24: any request that fails ends with a [ErreurApi], which contains the message’s translation key, its parameters, and the error for each field.

docs.title: 11.7.4. lib/api/types.dart
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/api/types.dart - JSON objects exchanged with the server
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The translation, into Dart classes, of the API described in the chapter "The
// server, a black box" (see the examples in `commun/types.dart`). Each
// class processes its JSON using Dart 3 filtering: a response that does not
// the expected format is detected as soon as it is received.
// =========================================================================

enum Role { admin, doctor, user }

Role _role(String nom) => Role.values.byName(nom.toLowerCase());

Never _inattendu(String quoi, Object? json) => throw FormatException('$quoi inattendu : $json');

// POST /api/auth/login, GET /api/auth/me, PUT /api/my-account
class Utilisateur {
  final String login;
  final String nom; // display name: "Marie PELISSIER"
  final Role role;

  const Utilisateur(this.login, this.nom, this.role);

  factory Utilisateur.depuisJson(Object? json) => switch (json) {
    {'login': final String login, 'nom': final String nom, 'role': final String role} => Utilisateur(
      login,
      nom,
      _role(role),
    ),
    _ => _inattendu('Utilisateur', json),
  };
}

// GET /api/captcha
class Captcha {
  final String id;
  final String svg;

  const Captcha(this.id, this.svg);

  factory Captcha.depuisJson(Object? json) => switch (json) {
    {'id': final String id, 'svg': final String svg} => Captcha(id, svg),
    _ => _inattendu('Captcha', json),
  };
}

// a title, a first name, a last name
class Identite {
  final String titre;
  final String prenom;
  final String nom;

  const Identite(this.titre, this.prenom, this.nom);

  factory Identite.depuisJson(Object? json) => switch (json) {
    {'titre': final String titre, 'prenom': final String prenom, 'nom': final String nom} => Identite(
      titre,
      prenom,
      nom,
    ),
    _ => _inattendu('Identité', json),
  };

   // "Ms. Alice DURAND"
  String get libelle => '$titre $prenom $nom';
}

// a doctor or a client: GET /api/doctors, GET /api/clients/:id...
class Personne extends Identite {
  final int id;
  final int version; // optimistic lock: to be sent back with a modification
  final String? login; // only for ADMIN

  const Personne(this.id, this.version, super.titre, super.prenom, super.nom, [this.login]);

  factory Personne.depuisJson(Object? json) => switch (json) {
    {
      'id': final int id,
      'version': final int version,
      'titre': final String titre,
      'prenom': final String prenom,
      'nom': final String nom,
    } =>
      Personne(id, version, titre, prenom, nom, (json as Map<String, Object?>)['login'] as String?),
    _ => _inattendu('Personne', json),
  };

  static List<Personne> liste(Object? json) => [for (final p in json as List<Object?>) Personne.depuisJson(p)];
}

// a time slot
class Creneau {
  final int id;
  final int hdebut;
  final int mdebut;
  final int hfin;
  final int mfin;

  const Creneau(this.id, this.hdebut, this.mdebut, this.hfin, this.mfin);

  factory Creneau.depuisJson(Object? json) => switch (json) {
    {'id': final int id, 'hdebut': final int hd, 'mdebut': final int md, 'hfin': final int hf, 'mfin': final int mf} =>
      Creneau(id, hd, md, hf, mf),
    _ => _inattendu('Créneau', json),
  };
}

// a calendar entry, with the DROITS of the logged-in user
class CreneauAgenda extends Creneau {
  final bool libre;
  final Identite? patient; // null: available, or booked by another patient
  final bool moi; // the logged-in patient’s appointment
  final bool reservable;
  final int? idRv; // specified if the user can cancel

  const CreneauAgenda(
    super.id,
    super.hdebut,
    super.mdebut,
    super.hfin,
    super.mfin,
    this.libre,
    this.patient,
    this.moi,
    this.reservable,
    this.idRv,
  );

  factory CreneauAgenda.depuisJson(Object? json) {
    final c = Creneau.depuisJson(json);
    return switch (json) {
      {
        'libre': final bool libre,
        'patient': final Object? patient,
        'moi': final bool moi,
        'reservable': final bool reservable,
        'idRv': final int? idRv,
      } =>
        CreneauAgenda(
          c.id,
          c.hdebut,
          c.mdebut,
          c.hfin,
          c.mfin,
          libre,
          patient == null ? null : Identite.depuisJson(patient),
          moi,
          reservable,
          idRv,
        ),
      _ => _inattendu('Créneau', json),
    };
  }
}

// GET /api/agenda?idMedecin=...&day=...
class Agenda {
  final Personne medecin;
  final String jour; // "yyyy-MM-dd"
  final List<CreneauAgenda> creneaux;
  final String? info; // translation key (patient who already has an appointment)

  const Agenda(this.medecin, this.jour, this.creneaux, this.info);

  factory Agenda.depuisJson(Object? json) => switch (json) {
    {
      'medecin': final Object medecin,
      'jour': final String jour,
      'creneaux': final List<Object?> creneaux,
      'info': final String? info,
    } =>
      Agenda(Personne.depuisJson(medecin), jour, [for (final c in creneaux) CreneauAgenda.depuisJson(c)], info),
    _ => _inattendu('Agenda', json),
  };
}

// an appointment from GET /api/my-space
class RendezVous {
  final int id;
  final String jour;
  final Creneau creneau;
  final Personne medecin;

  const RendezVous(this.id, this.jour, this.creneau, this.medecin);

  factory RendezVous.depuisJson(Object? json) => switch (json) {
    {'id': final int id, 'jour': final String jour, 'creneau': final Object creneau, 'medecin': final Object medecin} =>
      RendezVous(id, jour, Creneau.depuisJson(creneau), Personne.depuisJson(medecin)),
    _ => _inattendu('Rendez-vous', json),
  };
}

// GET /api/my-space
class MonEspace {
  final Identite patient;
  final List<RendezVous> rendezVous;

  const MonEspace(this.patient, this.rendezVous);

  factory MonEspace.depuisJson(Object? json) => switch (json) {
    {'patient': final Object patient, 'rendezVous': final List<Object?> rv} => MonEspace(Identite.depuisJson(patient), [
      for (final r in rv) RendezVous.depuisJson(r),
    ]),
    _ => _inattendu('Espace', json),
  };
}

// GET /api/my-account
class MonCompte extends Identite {
  final String login;
  final int version;

  const MonCompte(super.titre, super.prenom, super.nom, this.login, this.version);

  factory MonCompte.depuisJson(Object? json) {
    final i = Identite.depuisJson(json);
    return switch (json) {
      {'login': final String login, 'version': final int version} => MonCompte(
        i.titre,
        i.prenom,
        i.nom,
        login,
        version,
      ),
      _ => _inattendu('Compte', json),
    };
  }
}

The JSON objects from API, in [Dart] classes (see Example 24):

  • line 14: a function that never terminates normally (it throws an exception): its return type is [Never]. It can therefore serve as the final case for a [switch] of any type;
  • lines 24–30: filtering a [Map]: this case applies if the JSON has (at least) these three keys, with values of these types, which are stored in variables along the way;
  • lines 69–88: a doctor or a client: a [Identite], plus an identifier, a version (the optimistic lock: it will be released upon a modification), and a login, which only the ADMIN receives (hence the optional parameter in square brackets);
  • Lines 109–114: An entry in the calendar, showing the DROITS for the logged-in user, calculated by the server: [patient] is only shown to those who have permission to view it, [reservable] indicates whether the user can make a reservation; [idRv] is only provided to those who can cancel;
  • lines 129–151: first, the time slot itself ([Creneau.depuisJson]) is read, followed by its specific fields;
  • lines 209–213: the logged-in patient’s account: their identity, login, and version. [super.titre]: the parameter is passed as-is to the parent class constructor.

docs.title: 11.7.5. lib/api/rdvmedecins_api.dart
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/api/rdvmedecins_api.dart - a method per route from API
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The client’s “data access layer” (a “repository,” in the
// terminology of the Flutter architecture guide): the screens call
// these typed methods without knowing anything about URL, the http package, or the
// JSON. If the API changes, only this file changes.
// Each method returns a Future; if it fails, it ends with a
// ErreurApi (see client_api.dart).
// The data sent (forms) are simple Map<String, Object>?> :
// Their keys are the names of the fields expected by the server—and those
// of the errors it returns (ErreurApi.champs).
// =========================================================================

import 'client_api.dart';
import 'types.dart';

// /api/doctors or /api/clients: both are handled the same way
enum TypePersonnes { medecins, clients }

typedef Donnees = Map<String, Object?>;

class RdvMedecinsApi {
  final ClientApi _client;

  RdvMedecinsApi(this._client);

  Future<Object?> _get(String url, {bool publique = false}) => _client.requete('GET', url, publique: publique);
  Future<Object?> _post(String url, Object corps, {bool publique = false}) =>
      _client.requete('POST', url, corps: corps, publique: publique);

   // ------------------------------------------------ login (public routes)
  Future<Captcha> captcha() async => Captcha.depuisJson(await _get('/captcha', publique: true));

  Future<Utilisateur> moi() async => Utilisateur.depuisJson(await _get('/auth/moi', publique: true));

  Future<Utilisateur> connecter(String login, String password, String captchaId, String captcha) async =>
      Utilisateur.depuisJson(
        await _post('/auth/login', {
          'login': login,
          'password': password,
          'captchaId': captchaId,
          'captcha': captcha,
        }, publique: true),
      );

  Future<void> deconnecter() => _post('/auth/logout', {}, publique: true);

   // ------------------------------------------------ account creation (public)
  Future<void> accesInscription(String captchaId, String captcha) =>
      _post('/inscription/acces', {'captchaId': captchaId, 'captcha': captcha}, publique: true);

  Future<bool> etatAccesInscription() async => switch (await _get('/inscription/acces', publique: true)) {
    {'valide': true} => true,
    _ => false,
  };

  Future<String> inscrire(Donnees donnees) async => switch (await _post('/inscription', donnees, publique: true)) {
    {'login': final String login} => login,
    final autre => throw FormatException('Réponse inattendue : $autre'),
  };

   // ------------------------------------------------ calendar and appointments
   // idMedecin null: for a logged-in doctor, SON calendar
  Future<Agenda> agenda(int? idMedecin, String jour) async {
    final parametres = Uri(queryParameters: {'jour': jour, 'idMedecin': ?idMedecin?.toString()}).query;
    return Agenda.depuisJson(await _get('/agenda?$parametres'));
  }

  Future<void> reserver(String jour, int idCreneau, int? idClient) =>
      _post('/rendez-vous', {'jour': jour, 'idCreneau': idCreneau, 'idClient': ?idClient});

  Future<void> annulerRv(int idRv) => _client.requete('DELETE', '/rendez-vous/$idRv');

   // ------------------------------------------------ doctors and clients
  Future<List<Personne>> lister(TypePersonnes type) async => Personne.liste(await _get('/${type.name}'));

  Future<Personne> lire(TypePersonnes type, int id) async => Personne.depuisJson(await _get('/${type.name}/$id'));

  Future<Personne> ajouter(TypePersonnes type, Donnees donnees) async =>
      Personne.depuisJson(await _post('/${type.name}', donnees));

  Future<Personne> modifier(TypePersonnes type, int id, Donnees donnees) async =>
      Personne.depuisJson(await _client.requete('PUT', '/${type.name}/$id', corps: donnees));

  Future<void> supprimer(TypePersonnes type, int id) => _client.requete('DELETE', '/${type.name}/$id');

   // ------------------------------------------------ Patient Area
  Future<MonEspace> monEspace() async => MonEspace.depuisJson(await _get('/mon-espace'));

  Future<MonCompte> monCompte() async => MonCompte.depuisJson(await _get('/mon-compte'));

  Future<Utilisateur> modifierMonCompte(Donnees donnees) async =>
      Utilisateur.depuisJson(await _client.requete('PUT', '/mon-compte', corps: donnees));

  Future<void> supprimerMonCompte(String motDePasseActuel) =>
      _client.requete('DELETE', '/mon-compte', corps: {'motDePasseActuel': motDePasseActuel});
}

A method per route for API: this is the [RdvMedecins] class from Example 24, expanded.

  • Line 19: [/api/medecins] and [/api/clients] are handled the same way: an enumeration, where the name of each value ([TypePersonnes.medecins.name], “doctors”) is that of the route;
  • Line 21: A type alias: a more descriptive name for an existing type;
  • lines 33–47: the connection routes, which are public: a 401 has its own specific meaning (“no one is logged in,” “incorrect password”) and does not mean that the session has expired;
  • line 53: Is the account creation token valid? A [switch] expression in the response: [true] only for [{"valide": true}];
  • Lines 65–67: The address parameters, constructed by [Uri] (which encodes them). ['idMedecin': ?idMedecin?.toString()]: an optional element of [Map] ([Dart] 3.8): the key is added only if the value is not [null]. A logged-in doctor requests the calendar without [idMedecin]: the server returns the doctor’s own calendar;
  • line 71: similarly, [idClient] is sent only if it is known (a patient is making a reservation for themselves);
  • lines 76–86: the five operations involving doctors or clients: [/api/${type.name}];
  • lines 89–97: the patient’s space. Deleting the account sends a message body with a [DELETE] request (the current password): this is permitted by HTTP, and the [http] package also allows it, via a manually constructed [http.Request] (see [client_api.dart]).

docs.title: 11.8.1. lib/i18n/traductions.dart
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/i18n/traductions.dart - dictionaries, current language
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Taken from Example 21. The dictionaries (assets/i18n/fr.json, en.json)
// are those for the Vue.js, Angular, and React clients: same keys, same
// conventions ({{param}}, plurals _one / _other). The server does not return
// only CLÉS ("ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN"): this is where they become
// text in the language selected by the user.
//    - t('CLE', {'param': value}) : the text in the current language;
//    - changerLangue('en'        ) : loads the other dictionary, notifies
//                                    the screens (ChangeNotifier), saves
//                                    the selection on the device.
// =========================================================================

import 'dart:convert';

import 'package:flutter/services.dart';
import 'package:flutter/widgets.dart';
import 'package:intl/intl.dart';
import 'package:shared_preferences/shared_preferences.dart';

const langues = ['fr', 'en'];

class Traductions extends ChangeNotifier {
  final SharedPreferences? _stockage;
  String _langue = 'fr';
  Map<String, Object?> _dictionnaire = {};

  Traductions([this._stockage]);

  String get langue => _langue;

   // the source language: the one stored on the device, otherwise the language of the
   // phone (if known), otherwise French
  Future<void> demarrer() async {
    final memorisee = _stockage?.getString('rdvmedecins.langue');
    final appareil = WidgetsBinding.instance.platformDispatcher.locale.languageCode;
    await changerLangue(memorisee ?? (langues.contains(appareil) ? appareil : 'fr'));
  }

  Future<void> changerLangue(String langue) async {
     // rootBundle: the files included with the application (the "assets" section of the pubspec)
    final json = await rootBundle.loadString('assets/i18n/$langue.json');
    _dictionnaire = jsonDecode(json) as Map<String, Object?>;
    _langue = langue;
    await _stockage?.setString('rdvmedecins.langue', langue);
    notifyListeners();
  }

   // "ACCUEIL.BONJOUR" -> dictionaryQZXW2HTMLBWydBQ0NVRUlMJ10ZQXQZXW2HTMLBWydCT05KT1VSJ10ZQX; null if absent
  String? _chercher(String cle) {
    Object? noeud = _dictionnaire;
    for (final partie in cle.split('.')) {
      noeud = noeud is Map<String, Object?> ? noeud[partie] : null;
    }
    return noeud is String ? noeud : null;
  }

  String t(String cle, [Map<String, Object?> params = const {}]) {
    String? texte;
    final count = params['count'];
    if (count is int) {
       // Intl.pluralLogic: the plural form, according to the rules of the language
      texte = Intl.pluralLogic(
        count,
        locale: _langue,
        zero: _chercher('${cle}_zero'),
        one: _chercher('${cle}_one'),
        other: _chercher('${cle}_other'),
      );
    }
    texte ??= _chercher(cle);
     // an unknown key is displayed as-is: you can immediately see what’s missing
    if (texte == null) return cle;
     // {{name}} -> the value of the “name” parameter
    return texte.replaceAllMapped(RegExp(r'\{\{(\w+)\}\}'), (m) => '${params[m[1]] ?? m[0]}');
  }
}

The [Traductions] class from Example 21, simplified: the dictionaries always have the same name ([assets/i18n/fr.json]).
