Also try: a username that’s already taken ([martin]), an invalid username (“Jean M”), and the same record edited on two devices (or in the app and with [curl]).

The principle is the same as for all forms in the case study: the rules reside in UN one place—the server; the app displays the results in the user’s language.

docs.title: 13. Conclusion
docs.text:
We have developed the [Flutter] client for the [RdvMedecins] application. For the user, it offers the same screens as the HTML application from the [NestJS] course and as the [Vue.js], [Angular] and [React] from previous courses; however, this is a mobile app installed on the phone, and the same code also generates a web app.

The server, on the other hand, hasn’t changed. Its API and JSON—whose contract (routes, body, codes, and error keys) was sufficient to write the client without ever reading its code—serves both a browser and a phone equally well. There is only one difference: on the phone, there is no browser to store the token cookie, so the app took on that role with just a few lines of code ([ClientAvecCookies]). Security remains unchanged: it is still the server that authenticates users, verifies roles and management rules, and decides what a patient is authorized to view.

Readers who have taken the [React] course can compare:

  • both are based on the same idea: the interface is a function of the state. A [React] component is a function that returns JSX; a [Flutter] widget has a [build()] method that returns a widget tree. When the state changes ([useState] / [setState]), the interface is rebuilt and then compared to the previous one;
  • [React] generates HTML, which the browser renders; [Flutter] renders each pixel itself, using its own engine, on both the phone and in the browser. This results in identical screens across all platforms, but a web application that takes longer to load;
  • [Flutter] provides much more than [React]: the widgets from [Material], forms, lists, windows, animations, the theme, and tests. Fewer libraries were required: [go_router] for addresses, [provider] for shared state, and [http] for queries. No CSS: the layout is built using widgets ([Column], [Row], [Padding], [Expanded]...);
  • [Dart] is a typed, compiled language with non-nullable types: many errors that [TypeScript] overlooks (a missing [null] value, a misread JSON) are detected at compile time, or as soon as the response is received thanks to [Dart] 3 filtering;
  • the trade-off: more verbose screens (the widget tree is deep), and a lifecycle to be familiar with ([initState], [didUpdateWidget], [dispose], [mounted]).

Concepts covered in this course (stateless and stateful widgets, lifecycle, keys, [InheritedWidget] and [provider], [ChangeNotifier], [Future], and [Stream], router and guards, forms, internationalization) are common to any [Flutter] application. For further reading:

  • the official documentation, docs.flutter.dev, its tutorials, and its architecture guide (“App architecture”);
  • tests: widget tests ([flutter_test]), which interact with a screen without a phone (the screenshots in this document were created using these tests), and integration tests ([integration_test]), which run the actual application on an emulator;
  • other widely used state managers: [Riverpod] (the successor to [provider], by the same author), [Bloc];
  • Code generation: [json_serializable] and [freezed] generate the methods [depuisJson], [copyWith], [==]... from simple declarations;
  • secure token storage ([flutter_secure_storage]), notifications, the camera, geolocation: one package per need, on pub.dev;
  • iPhone: the same code generates an application [iOS], to be built on a [Mac] using [Xcode].

docs.title: 12. Deployment
docs.text: During development, the application runs under the control of [flutter run]: in “debug” mode, which is slower, with hot reloading and checks ([assert]) performed by [Flutter]. To deploy it, we build it in “release” mode: optimized code, without development tools. We build one version per platform.

docs.title: 12.1. The web version
docs.text:
1. Build the client. In the [rdvmedecins_flutter] folder:
flutter build web --no-web-resources-cdn

The console displays:

Compiling lib\main.dart for the Web...
Wasm dry run succeeded. Consider building and testing your application with the `--wasm` flag. See docs for more info: https://docs.flutter.dev/platform-integration/web/wasm
Use --no-wasm-dry-run to disable these warnings.
Expected to find fonts for (MaterialIcons, packages/cupertino_icons/CupertinoIcons), but found (MaterialIcons). This usually means you are referring to font families in an IconData class but not including them in the assets section of your pubspec.yaml, are missing the package that would include them, or are missing "uses-material-design: true".
Font asset "MaterialIcons-Regular.otf" was tree-shaken, reducing it from 1645184 to 9004 bytes (99.5% reduction). Tree-shaking can be disabled by providing the --no-tree-shake-icons flag when building your app.
Compiling lib\main.dart for the Web...                             70,5s
√ Built build\web

Two warnings, with no consequences: compilation into [WebAssembly] would be possible (see below); a library in [Flutter] references icons from the [iOS] ([CupertinoIcons]) style, which the application does not use.

The [dart2js] compiler has compiled the entire application ([Dart], [Flutter], and the packages) into [JavaScript], in the [build/web/] folder:

  • [index.html]: LA application page, which loads [flutter_bootstrap.js], then [main.dart.js] (3.5 MB, approximately 1 MB once compressed by the server): NOTRE code, along with all the code from [Flutter] and the packets, optimized. [Flutter] does not generate HTML: the application draws each pixel itself on a canvas, using the same engine as on the phone;
  • [canvaskit/]: this rendering engine ([Skia], compiled into [WebAssembly]: [canvaskit.wasm], 7 MB). Without the [--no-web-resources-cdn] option, it would be downloaded from a [Google] server; with it, it is included with the application, which no longer depends on any external site;
  • [assets/]: the resources from [pubspec.yaml] (dictionaries, fonts). The icons are “tree-shaken”: only those used by the application are kept in the icon font;
  • Upon first load, the browser downloads a few megabytes (primarily the rendering engine) and then caches them. This is the main weakness of [Flutter] for the web: it is better suited for applications (which are opened and used for extended periods) than for websites (which are browsed briefly).

The [--wasm] option compiles the application as [WebAssembly] rather than [JavaScript]: it is faster in browsers that support it (recent versions of [Chrome], [Edge], and [Firefox]); other browsers automatically receive the [JavaScript] version.

  1. Place it on the server. Copy the CONTENU file from the [build/web/] folder to a folder named [client/] at the root of the JSON server ([rdvmedecins-nestjs-json/client/index.html], [rdvmedecins-nestjs-json/client/main.dart.js]...), then restart the server. It displays:
[Nest] LOG [RdvMedecins] client web servi depuis .../rdvmedecins-nestjs-json/client
[Nest] LOG [RdvMedecins] serveur JSON démarré : http://localhost:8080/api

The complete application is now available at http://localhost:8080. The server serves the client’s files and returns [index.html] for any other address outside of /api: reloading the /agenda page works (it is the client’s browser that displays it). The server’s [src/web/client-spa.ts] file handles this task. The application is served by the API server: the relative address of [config.dart] ([''], or [/api/...]) is correct.

You can also try the version built without the JSON server, using any file server, but the /api requests will fail.

docs.title: 12.2. The Android version
docs.text:
1. Build the app, specifying the server address:
flutter build apk --dart-define=SERVEUR=http://192.168.1.20:8080

The console displays (for a APK built without [--dart-define]):

Running Gradle task 'assembleRelease'...
Font asset "MaterialIcons-Regular.otf" was tree-shaken, reducing it from 1645184 to 3400 bytes (99.8% reduction). Tree-shaking can be disabled by providing the --no-tree-shake-icons flag when building your app.
Running Gradle task 'assembleRelease'...                          193,4s
√ Built build\app\outputs\flutter-apk\app-release.apk (53.5MB)

(A few warnings regarding [Gradle] and [Java], which had no impact, have been removed.) The first build takes a long time: [Gradle] downloads its own tools and libraries; subsequent builds are much faster.

The [Dart] compiler translated the application into machine code for the three processor families of [Android] phones (ARM 32-bit, ARM 64-bit, x86 64-bit), and the [Android] build tool ([Gradle]) packaged it, along with the [Flutter] engine, into a APK file: the [Android] application installation format. It contains three copies of the application and its engine—one per processor family—which explains its size. [--split-per-abi] would generate three smaller APK files, one per processor family; an “App Bundle” (see below) allows the store to deliver only what each phone needs.

  1. Install it. With the phone connected to the computer (USB cable, USB debugging enabled):
flutter install

You can also copy the APK file to the phone and open it: [Android] will then ask you to allow the installation of apps “from unknown sources.”

  1. For a real release:
  • the app must be signed with a developer-specific key: the project generated by [flutter create] signs the “release” version with the debug key, which is sufficient for testing but not for a store. The [Flutter] documentation (“Build and release an Android app”) describes how to create the key and configure [Gradle];
  • [Google Play Store] expects an “Android App Bundle” rather than a APK: [flutter build appbundle];
  • The app name and icon are configured in [android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml] ([android:label]) and [android/app/src/main/res/mipmap-*/];
  • The server must be set to HTTPS (passwords are shared), and the line [android:usesCleartextTraffic="true"] is removed from the manifest.

docs.title: 12.3. The production server
docs.text:
In actual production, don’t forget the [.env] file on the server:

  • a long, random [JWT_SECRET];
  • an empty [CAPTCHA_TEST];
  • [COOKIE_SECURE=true] if the site is served via HTTPS (it must be). The mobile client sends the cookie regardless of this option: it is the browser that enforces it;
  • [TRUST_PROXY=true] if the server is located behind a proxy ([nginx]...), so that the attempt limit sees the clients’ actual IP address.

We then launch the compiled server: [npm run build], followed by [npm run start:prod].

docs.title: 3.1. Example 01: The Structure of a Flutter Application
3.1.1. The Project
docs.text:
A [Flutter] project is created using the [flutter create] command:

flutter create --org fr.stahe --platforms=android,web,windows mon_application
  • [--org fr.stahe]: the prefix of the app ID, reversed like a domain name. The app [Android] will be named [fr.stahe.mon_application]; two apps installed on the same phone must have different IDs;
  • [--platforms=...]: the target platforms. For each one, [flutter create] creates a folder ([android/], [web/], [windows/], and also [ios/], [macos/], [linux/] if requested): a small, platform-specific project that simply launches the [Flutter] engine and loads the application into it. We rarely make changes to it (the application’s name, icon, and permissions);
  • [mon_application]: the project name, which is also the package name [Dart]: lowercase letters, numbers, and underscores.

The command generates a complete, ready-to-run application (a counter). The example project was created in the same way, and then its [lib/] folder was filled in manually to combine twenty-five applications into a single project: this way, they share the same packages, which are downloaded only once.

docs.title: 3.1.2. The pubspec.yaml file
docs.text:
The [pubspec.yaml] file describes the project: its name, the required version of [Dart], the packages used, and the files included with the application. The one for the examples:

# ==========================================================================
# pubspec.yaml - Project description for the examples
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A single Flutter project for all 25 examples: each has its own folder in
# the `lib/` directory and its own entry point (main.dart), which is specified with the command
# `flutter run` command with the `-t` (target) option:
#
#      flutter run -t lib/ex05_champs_controles/main.dart
#
# The libraries (the "packages") are downloaded from pub.dev by
# the `flutter pub get` command (launched automatically by `flutter run`).
# ==========================================================================

name: exemples_flutter
description: Les 25 petits exemples du cours Introduction étape par étape au framework Flutter.
# No publication on pub.dev: this is an application, not a library
publish_to: none
version: 1.0.0

environment:
   # the required Dart version
  sdk: ^3.12.0

dependencies:
  flutter:
    sdk: flutter
   # "clean" web addresses (example 17)
  flutter_web_plugins:
    sdk: flutter
   # text from Flutter itself (window buttons, calendar, etc.)
   # in French and English (examples 05, 21)
  flutter_localizations:
    sdk: flutter
   # dates and numbers formatted according to the language (examples 09, 21)
  intl: any
   # the router (examples 17, 18)
  go_router: ^16.2.0
   # a state shared by the entire application (examples 20, 24, 25)
  provider: ^6.1.5
   # a small key-value dictionary stored on the device (examples 20, 21, 23)
  shared_preferences: ^2.5.3
   # the HTTP requests (examples 22 through 25)
  http: ^1.5.0
   # image display SVG (example 03, CAPTCHA for examples 22 through 25)
  flutter_svg: ^2.2.1

dev_dependencies:
   # tests (and screenshots from the course; see test/screenshots)
  flutter_test:
    sdk: flutter
   # style guidelines recommended by the Flutter team (see analysis_options.yaml)
  flutter_lints: ^6.0.0

flutter:
   # Material Design icons (Icons.add, Icons.delete...)
  uses-material-design: true
   # files included with the app (AVEC): they are accessed via their path
  assets:
    - assets/
    - assets/i18n/
   # a monospaced font (to display JSON), included with the application
  fonts:
    - family: RobotoMono
      fonts:
        - asset: assets/polices/RobotoMono-Regular.ttf
        - asset: assets/polices/RobotoMono-Bold.ttf
          weight: 700
  • Lines 14–18: the project name (which is also the package name—the project files are imported via [package:exemples_flutter/...]), its description, and its version. [publish_to: none]: This project is not a library; it will never be published on [pub.dev];
  • lines 20–22: the required version of the [Dart] language. The prefix [^] accepts any newer version within the same major version (3.12, 3.13… but not 4.0);
  • lines 24–45: the packages required by the application. Some are derived from SDK, which itself is derived from [Flutter] ([sdk: flutter]): [flutter] (the framework), [flutter_localizations] (the texts from [Flutter] translated into each language), [flutter_web_plugins] (a web-specific configuration). The others are downloaded from pub.dev, the repository for the [Dart] packages: their purpose is explained in the comments, and each will be demonstrated in the example that uses it. [intl: any]: any version ([flutter_localizations] dictates its own);
  • lines 47–52: packages used only for development and not included in the shipped application: [flutter_test] (tests) and [flutter_lints] (parser style rules);
  • lines 54–67: the configuration specific to [Flutter]:
    • [uses-material-design: true]: the application uses the icon font from [Material Design] ([Icons.add], [Icons.delete]...) ;
    • [assets]: the files included with the application (images, dictionaries, etc.), which are read by their path. Specifying a folder ([assets/]) delivers all the files it contains directly;
    • [fonts]: a font included with the application; [Roboto Mono], a monospaced font, is used to display JSON. The standard font for [Material Design], [Roboto], is the system font [Android]: there is no need to include it.

Package versions follow the same convention as [npm]: [^16.2.0] accepts any version of 16.x.y starting from 16.2.0. The command [flutter pub get] downloads the packages and writes the exact selected versions to the file [pubspec.lock]. It is launched automatically by [flutter run] when [pubspec.yaml] has changed; [VS Code] also runs it as soon as this file is saved. To add a package, rather than editing the file manually, you can type [flutter pub add go_router]: the command adds the line with the latest version of the package.

docs.title: 3.1.3. The analysis_options.yaml file
docs.text:
The [Dart] parser checks the code as you type: [VS Code] underlines errors in red and warnings in yellow or blue. You can also run it for the entire project with [flutter analyze]. Its rules:

# ==========================================================================
# analysis_options.yaml - the rules for the Dart code analyzer
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The parser checks the code as you type it (VS Code highlights
# errors) and via the `flutter analyze` command. It is based on the rules
# recommended by the Flutter team (package flutter_lints)...
# ==========================================================================

include: package:flutter_lints/flutter.yaml

analyzer:
  language:
     # ... making them stricter: no implicit conversion of a `dynamic` type
    strict-casts: true
    strict-raw-types: true

linter:
  rules:
     # single quotes everywhere, as in the examples from the course
    prefer_single_quotes: true
     # "final" for a local variable that is never reassigned
    prefer_final_locals: true
     # Excessively long strings are allowed (French text)
    lines_longer_than_80_chars: false
  • line 9: the rules recommended by the [Flutter] team ([flutter_lints] package): a widget must have a constructor [const] if possible, a controller must be released, etc.;
  • Lines 14–15: stricter typing. [Dart] is a statically typed language, but it has a type [dynamic] (“anything”): the decoded JSON, for example, is made up of [dynamic]. [strict-casts] prohibits implicit conversion to another type: you must write it explicitly ([json['nom'] as String]), and any error occurs there and is visible;
  • Lines 20–24: a few style rules: use single quotes for strings (double quotes if the string contains an apostrophe: ["l'état"]), and [final] for variables that are never reassigned.

docs.title: 3.1.4. The entry point: main.dart
docs.text:
For example, there is a file named [main.dart], which contains the function [main]—the entry point for any program named [Dart]. The one from Example 01:

// =========================================================================
// lib/ex01_premiere_application/main.dart - a first application
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Everything in a Flutter app is a WIDGET: an object that describes
// a part of the screen (text, a button, a margin, a column...).
// Widgets nest inside one another and form a ARBRE.
// A widget has a build() method, which RENVOIE assembles the widgets that
// compose it. Flutter calls `build()` to render the screen; it
// RAPPELLE every time the widget’s state changes (setState), and updates
// the screen with the new result.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

// "Regular" data, outside of widgets: it never changes
const titre = 'Bienvenue dans Flutter';
const langages = ['Dart', 'Flutter', 'Material Design'];

// "12:05:09": the current time, displayed as two digits
String heureCourante() {
  final d = DateTime.now();
  String deuxChiffres(int n) => n.toString().padLeft(2, '0');
  return '${deuxChiffres(d.hour)}:${deuxChiffres(d.minute)}:${deuxChiffres(d.second)}';
}

// the entry point of any Dart program
void main() {
   // runApp: Flutter takes control of the screen and displays the RACINE widget
  runApp(const Application());
}

// the root widget: it configures the app (title, theme, first screen).
// StatelessWidget: a SANS state widget, fully described by its parameters
class Application extends StatelessWidget {
  const Application({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
     // MaterialApp: an app with the colors and behavior of
     // Material Design, Google’s visual language
    return MaterialApp(
      title: 'Exemple 01',
       // no "DEBUG" banner in the corner of the screen
      debugShowCheckedModeBanner: false,
       // the colors of the entire app, derived from a base color
      theme: ThemeData(colorSchemeSeed: Colors.indigo),
      home: const PageAccueil(),
    );
  }
}

// A AVEC state widget: it consists of two parts—the widget itself (which
// ever changes) and a State object (which contains the data that changes)
class PageAccueil extends StatefulWidget {
  const PageAccueil({super.key});

  @override
  State<PageAccueil> createState() => _PageAccueilState();
}

// the "_": this class is PRIVÉE, invisible outside this file
class _PageAccueilState extends State<PageAccueil> {
   // ÉTAT: simple fields of the State object
  int _compteur = 0;
  String _heure = heureCourante();

   // the function called by the button
  void _incrementer() {
     // setState: the state is modified DANS the function passed to setState;
     // Flutter then calls build() to update the screen. We
     // never modify the screen ourselves
    setState(() {
      _compteur++;
      _heure = heureCourante();
    });
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
     // Scaffold: the structure of a Material screen (top bar, body, etc.)
    return Scaffold(
      appBar: AppBar(title: const Text('Exemple 01 - une première application')),
       // Padding: a margin around its child
      body: Padding(
        padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16),
         // Column: children placed one below the other
        child: Column(
          crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
          children: [
            Text(titre, style: Theme.of(context).textTheme.headlineSmall),
            const SizedBox(height: 12),
            const Text(
               'This screen is built using Flutter, starting with the `main` function
              'et des widgets Application et PageAccueil.',
            ),
            const SizedBox(height: 8),
             // ${expression} inserts the value of an expression into a string
            Text('On y écrit du ${langages.join(', ')} (${langages.length} langages).'),
            const SizedBox(height: 16),
             // onPressed: the function to call when tapped (see example 04)
            FilledButton(onPressed: _incrementer, child: const Text('Cliquez-moi')),
            const SizedBox(height: 16),
            Text(
              'Vous avez cliqué $_compteur fois (dernier clic : $_heure).',
              style: const TextStyle(fontWeight: FontWeight.bold, color: Color(0xFF087EA4)),
            ),
          ],
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}

Let’s start at the end: the program.

  • Line 13: the [Material] library from [Flutter]: all the widgets from [Material Design], the visual language of [Google] (buttons, input fields, bars, windows, etc.). It imports the rest of [Flutter] itself;
  • lines 16–17: two ordinary data values, declared outside the widgets: they never change. [const]: a constant known at compile time;
  • lines 20–23: an ordinary function that returns the current time in the format “12:05:09.” It contains a small function of its own, [deuxChiffres], written on a single line with [=>];
  • lines 27–29: the function [main], called at launch. [runApp] starts [Flutter]: it takes control of the screen and displays the widget provided to it—the root of the application.

The root widget, [Application]:

  • Line 34: A widget is a class. This class inherits from [StatelessWidget], a stateless widget: what it displays depends solely on its parameters and never changes on its own;
  • Line 29: its constructor. [{super.key}]: an optional named parameter passed to the parent class. Every widget has one: the “key” that identifies it (see Example 04). The constructor is [const]: [Application()] can be a constant that [Flutter] never needs to reconstruct;
  • Lines 38–47: the [build] method, the core of a widget. It returns the widgets that make it up. [@override]: it overrides the [build] method of the parent class. The parameter [context] is the widget’s position in the widget tree: it is used to retrieve what its ancestors provide (the theme, for example, line 90);
  • lines 41–47: [MaterialApp] is the widget that turns a widget tree into an application [Material]: a title ([title], the application’s name in the phone’s recent apps list or the browser tab), a theme ([theme]), and a home screen ([home]). [debugShowCheckedModeBanner: false] removes the “DEBUG” banner that a development app displays in a corner. [ThemeData(colorSchemeSeed: Colors.indigo)]: All colors in the application (buttons, bars, fields, etc.) are derived from a single base color, according to the rules in [Material Design] 3.

The first screen, [PageAccueil], has data that changes: it is a stateful widget.

  • Lines 54–58: A [StatefulWidget] consists of two parts. The widget itself, like any widget, never changes (its fields would be [final]); its sole task is to create, via [createState], a [State] object, which in turn contains the data that changes. [Flutter] creates this object once and retains it as long as the widget remains in the same place in the tree;
  • line 62: the object [State]. Its name begins with an underscore: in [Dart], everything beginning with [_] is private and invisible outside the file;
  • lines 64–65: the state: simple fields of the [State] object;
  • lines 68–75: the method called by the button. It does not affect the screen: it changes the state within the function passed to [setState]. [setState] executes this function, then notifies [Flutter] that the state has changed: [Flutter] will call [build], compare the new widget tree to the old one, and redraw what has changed;
  • lines 79–105: the [build] for the screen:
    • [Scaffold] (“scaffolding”) is the structure of a screen [Material]: a top bar ([appBar]), a body ([body]), and, if requested, a bottom bar, a floating button, and a side menu;
    • [AppBar]: the top bar; its title is a widget ([Text]), as is almost everything in [Flutter];
    • [Padding]: a margin around its single child, [child]. [EdgeInsets.all(16)]: 16 points on each side (a logical “point,” independent of screen density: approximately 2.6 pixels on the phone shown in the screenshots);
    • [Column]: its children, [children], arranged one below the other. [crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start]: left-aligned (the “transverse” axis of a column is the horizontal axis);
    • [Text]: text. Its style may be derived from the theme: [Theme.of(context).textTheme.headlineSmall] is the style for “small headings”;
    • [SizedBox]: an empty box with a specified height—a space between two widgets;
    • line 98: [${expression}] inserts the value of an expression into a string; [$nom] is sufficient for a simple variable (line 104);
    • line 101: a button. [onPressed] takes the function to be called when the button is pressed. We specify the function itself, without parentheses: [onPressed: _incrementer()] would call it immediately, during screen construction;
    • lines 104–105: text that depends on the state. When the state changes, [build] is called, and this text changes.

Two notes regarding [Dart]:

  • almost all widget arguments are named parameters ([title: ...], [child: ...]): the widget tree reads like a description, and the order of the arguments does not matter. A named parameter is optional, unless it is declared as [required];
  • the keyword [const] preceding a widget ([const SizedBox(height: 12)]) creates it once and for all at compile time. [Flutter] then knows that it never changes and doesn’t waste time comparing it. The parser flags any [const] that have been omitted; [VS Code] knows how to add them on its own.

The screen’s widget tree, as shown by the [Flutter DevTools] tool (widget inspector):

Application
└── MaterialApp
    └── PageAccueil
        └── Scaffold
            ├── AppBar
            │   └── Text
            └── Padding
                └── Column
                    ├── Text          (le titre)
                    ├── SizedBox
                    ├── Text
                    ├── SizedBox
                    ├── Text
                    ├── SizedBox
                    ├── FilledButton
                    │   └── Text
                    ├── SizedBox
                    └── Text          (le compteur)

In a [Flutter] application, you write very little “implementation” code and a lot of “descriptive” code: the screen is a tree of widgets, each configured by its parameters. This is the same concept as JSX from [React], but without a template language: the tree is written in [Dart].

docs.title: 3.1.5. Execution
docs.text:
In the console open to the [exemples_flutter] folder, with the [Android] emulator running:

flutter run -d emulator-5554 -t lib/ex01_premiere_application/main.dart

The console displays:

Launching lib/ex01_premiere_application/main.dart on sdk gphone16k x86 64 in debug mode...
Running Gradle task 'assembleDebug'...                             24,1s
√ Built build\app\outputs\flutter-apk\app-debug.apk
Installing build\app\outputs\flutter-apk\app-debug.apk...          1 523ms
Syncing files to device sdk gphone16k x86 64...                       88ms

Flutter run key commands.
r Hot reload.
R Hot restart.
h List all available interactive commands.
d Detach (terminate "flutter run" but leave application running).
c Clear the screen
q Quit (terminate the application on the device).

A Dart VM Service on sdk gphone16k x86 64 is available at: http://127.0.0.1:54321/...
The Flutter DevTools debugger and profiler on sdk gphone16k x86 64 is available at: http://127.0.0.1:9101?uri=...

The first time, building the [Android] application (using the [Gradle] tool) takes one or two minutes; subsequent builds take just a few seconds. The application installs on the emulator and starts. On the left, the startup screen; on the right, after pressing the button twice:

Two experiments to try:

  • Change the title text in [main.dart], save the file, and type `r` in the console (or simply save the file in [VS Code]): the screen updates in one second, and the counter retains its value. This is a “hot reload”: the new code is injected into the running application; [Flutter] calls [build], but the [State] objects are preserved. R (“hot restart”) restarts the application from [main]: the counter resets to 0;
  • Launch the same application in the browser: [flutter run -d chrome -t lib/ex01_premiere_application/main.dart]. It is the same screen, rendered by the same engine; only the window size changes. With [-d windows], it is an application [Windows].

docs.title: 3.2. Example 02: The state and calculated values
docs.text:
The status is the core of [Flutter], just as it is for [React]. This example calculates the price TTC of an item:

// =========================================================================
// lib/ex02_etat/main.dart - the state and calculated values
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A small price calculator TTC:
//    - ÉTAT: the fields of the State object; change them DANS setState()
//      calls build(), which renders the screen with the new values;
//    - a value CALCULÉE derived from the state is not PAS a state: it is a
//      "getter" (or a local variable of build()), recalculated on every call
//      of build(). It is always up to date, with nothing to synchronize;
//    - data that depends on the state’s values (the history
//      of totals) is updated wherever the report changes: in setState;
//    - the app title (browser tab, list of
//      recent apps on the phone) is also a widget, Title:
//      it updates based on the state, just like the rest of the screen.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:intl/intl.dart';

// a euro amount formatter, in the French style (1,234.50 €), see example 09
final euros = NumberFormat.currency(locale: 'fr_FR', symbol: '€');

void main() {
  runApp(
    MaterialApp(
      debugShowCheckedModeBanner: false,
      theme: ThemeData(colorSchemeSeed: Colors.indigo),
      home: const PageCalculateur(),
    ),
  );
}

class PageCalculateur extends StatefulWidget {
  const PageCalculateur({super.key});

  @override
  State<PageCalculateur> createState() => _PageCalculateurState();
}

class _PageCalculateurState extends State<PageCalculateur> {
   // the status
  String _libelle = 'Stylo';
  double _prixHT = 2.5;
  int _quantite = 1;
  double _tauxTVA = 20; // as a percentage
   // the history of the last 5 changes to the total TTC
  final List<String> _historique = [];

   // A controller provides access to the TEXTE of an input field: we need it
   // here to reset it to its initial value (Reset). Example 05
   // examines them in detail
  final _champLibelle = TextEditingController(text: 'Stylo');
  final _champPrix = TextEditingController(text: '2.5');

   // of the CALCULÉES values: getters, recalculated with each read
  double get _totalHT => _quantite * _prixHT;
  double get _montantTVA => _totalHT * _tauxTVA / 100;
  double get _totalTTC => _totalHT + _montantTVA;

   // TOUS state changes go through this method: it records the
   // total TTC before the change, applies the change, and updates
   // the history if the total has changed
  void _changer(void Function() changement) {
    final ancienTTC = _totalTTC;
    setState(() {
      changement();
      if (_totalTTC != ancienTTC) {
        _historique.insert(0, '${euros.format(ancienTTC)} -> ${euros.format(_totalTTC)}');
        if (_historique.length > 5) {
          _historique.removeLast();
        }
      }
    });
  }

   // Changing the item resets the quantity to 1: this is done wherever we know
   // POURQUOI the status changes
  void _changerLibelle(String nouveau) {
    _changer(() {
      _libelle = nouveau;
      _quantite = 1;
    });
  }

  void _reinitialiser() {
    _changer(() {
      _libelle = 'Stylo';
      _prixHT = 2.5;
      _quantite = 1;
      _tauxTVA = 20;
    });
    _champLibelle.text = 'Stylo';
    _champPrix.text = '2.5';
  }

   // The State object disappears (we exit the screen): we release the controls
  @override
  void dispose() {
    _champLibelle.dispose();
    _champPrix.dispose();
    super.dispose();
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final styleTotal = Theme.of(context).textTheme.titleMedium!.copyWith(fontWeight: FontWeight.bold);

     // Title: the application title SUIT the state, like everything else
    return Title(
      title: 'TTC : ${euros.format(_totalTTC)}',
      color: Colors.indigo,
      child: Scaffold(
        appBar: AppBar(title: const Text("Exemple 02 - l'état")),
         // ListView: a column that scrolls if it exceeds the screen height
        body: ListView(
          padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16),
          children: [
            Card(
              child: Padding(
                padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16),
                child: Column(
                  children: [
                     // onChanged: called every time a key is pressed, with the new text
                    TextField(
                      controller: _champLibelle,
                      decoration: const InputDecoration(labelText: 'Article'),
                      onChanged: _changerLibelle,
                    ),
                    TextField(
                      controller: _champPrix,
                      decoration: const InputDecoration(labelText: 'Prix unitaire HT'),
                       // the phone’s numeric keypad, including the comma
                      keyboardType: const TextInputType.numberWithOptions(decimal: true),
                       // tryParse: null if the text is not a number; the comma is accepted
                      onChanged: (texte) => _changer(() => _prixHT = double.tryParse(texte.replaceAll(',', '.')) ?? 0),
                    ),
                    const SizedBox(height: 12),
                    Row(
                      children: [
                        const Expanded(child: Text("Quantité (revient à 1 si l'article change)")),
                        IconButton(
                          icon: const Icon(Icons.remove),
                           // null: the button is disabled
                          onPressed: _quantite > 0 ? () => _changer(() => _quantite--) : null,
                        ),
                        Text('$_quantite', style: styleTotal),
                        IconButton(icon: const Icon(Icons.add), onPressed: () => _changer(() => _quantite++)),
                      ],
                    ),
                    const SizedBox(height: 8),
                     // buttons, of which only UN is selected: the rate of TVA
                    SegmentedButton<double>(
                      segments: const [
                        ButtonSegment(value: 5.5, label: Text('5,5 %')),
                        ButtonSegment(value: 10, label: Text('10 %')),
                        ButtonSegment(value: 20, label: Text('20 %')),
                      ],
                      selected: {_tauxTVA},
                      onSelectionChanged: (choix) => _changer(() => _tauxTVA = choix.first),
                    ),
                    const SizedBox(height: 12),
                    OutlinedButton(onPressed: _reinitialiser, child: const Text('Réinitialiser')),
                  ],
                ),
              ),
            ),
            Card(
              child: Padding(
                padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16),
                child: Column(
                  crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
                  children: [
                    Text('$_quantite x $_libelle', style: Theme.of(context).textTheme.titleLarge),
                    const Divider(),
                    _ligne('Total HT', euros.format(_totalHT)),
                    _ligne('TVA (${_tauxTVA.toString().replaceAll('.', ',')} %)', euros.format(_montantTVA)),
                    _ligne('Total TTC', euros.format(_totalTTC), style: styleTotal),
                  ],
                ),
              ),
            ),
            Card(
              child: Padding(
                padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16),
                child: Column(
                  crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
                  children: [
                    Text('Historique du total TTC', style: Theme.of(context).textTheme.titleSmall),
                     // one line of text per history entry (see example 03)
                    for (final ligne in _historique) Text('• $ligne'),
                  ],
                ),
              ),
            ),
          ],
        ),
      ),
    );
  }

   // one line "label ....... amount": a method that creates widgets
  Widget _ligne(String libelle, String montant, {TextStyle? style}) {
    return Padding(
      padding: const EdgeInsets.symmetric(vertical: 4),
      child: Row(
        children: [
          Expanded(child: Text(libelle, style: style)),
          Text(montant, style: style),
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}
  • Line 21: A French-style amount formatter (€1,234.50), created once and for all outside the widgets, using the [intl] package (see Example 09). [final]: a variable that is assigned only once, but whose value is not known until runtime (unlike [const]);
  • lines 23–28: the program; this time, [MaterialApp] is written directly into [main]. This is how most examples will begin;
  • lines 42–45: four state data items, simple fields, typed as: [String], [double], [int]. In [Dart], [int], and [double], there are two distinct types of numbers;
  • line 47: the history of the last five changes to the total, a list. The field is [final]: the list will never be replaced; it will be modified (additions, removals);
  • Lines 52–53: two input field controllers. An input field [Flutter] stores its text in a controller, which is created and assigned to it: the text can then be read or changed from within the code (Reset button). Example 05 covers these in detail;
  • lines 56–58: three values calculated from the report. These are not report fields (PAS); they are getters—methods without parentheses that are used like fields ([_totalTTC]). They are recalculated each time they are read, so they are always up to date. This is the same rule we’ve already seen with [React]: we only store in the report what we cannot calculate; everything else is calculated;
  • Lines 63–73: The history of the totals in TTC depends on successive values of the total, which a getter cannot express. Therefore, TOUS passes state changes through the [_changer] method, which receives the change to be made as a parameter (a function with no parameters or return value, of type [void Function()]): it records the total before the change, applies the change in `[setState]`, compares it with the total after the change, and updates the history if it has changed. This is the natural place for this calculation: where the state changes, and not in `[build]` (which should only describe the screen);
  • lines 78–81: Changing the item resets the quantity to 1. This is done in the method that handles the field change, where we know why the state is changing;
  • lines 85–93: multiple state changes within a single [setState]: [build] will be called only once. Then the controllers receive their initial text: the fields display it immediately;
  • lines 98–101: [dispose] is called when the [State] object disappears permanently (the screen is exited). Here, the created objects—in this case, the controls—are released. Example 13 will illustrate the lifecycle of an object [State].

The [build] method:

  • line 106: a text style, calculated based on the theme—the medium-sized heading style ([titleMedium]), in bold. [copyWith] creates a copy of an object whose properties are modified: this is a convention of [Flutter] that we’ll see often. [!] tells [Dart] that the value is not [null] (the type of [titleMedium] is [TextStyle?], a style, or [null]);
  • Lines 109–111: The [Title] widget provides the application’s title: on the web, this is the browser tab title; on [Android], it is the name displayed in the list of recent applications. Whereas [React] used an effect ([useEffect]) to modify [document.title] after it was displayed, [Flutter] doesn’t require anything special: the title is a widget, described by [build] just like the rest of the screen, and it updates its state automatically;
  • line 115: [ListView] is a column that scrolls when it exceeds the screen height. On a phone, this is almost always what’s needed: a [Column] that’s too tall would be cut off (and [Flutter] would display a yellow and black band, indicating an “overflow”);
  • lines 124–127: an input field ([TextField]): its controller, its label ([decoration: InputDecoration(labelText: ...)]), and [onChanged], the function called with each keystroke, along with the new text;
  • lines 130–135: the price. [keyboardType] selects the phone’s keyboard: in this case, the numeric keypad, including the comma. The entered text is converted to a number by [double.tryParse], which returns [null] if the text is not a number ([?? 0]: in this case, 0). The French comma is accepted by replacing it with a period;
  • lines 138–147: the quantity, with two buttons, “–” and “+.” [Row] places its children side by side; [Expanded] gives its child the entire remaining width. [IconButton]: a button that is just an icon. [onPressed: null] disables a button: the value cannot go below 0;
  • lines 152–159: the rate of TVA, three “segmented” buttons, only one of which is selected. [selected] receives a set of values ([{_tauxTVA}]: a [Set] for an element), [onSelectionChanged] the new selected set;
  • lines 173–177: the results: three lines generated by the [_ligne] method;
  • line 190: one line of text per element in the history, generated by a [for] loop written in the list of children (see Example 03);
  • lines 202–208: a method that creates widgets. [{TextStyle? style}]: an optional named parameter that defaults to [null] if not provided. Breaking down a [build] into methods makes it more readable; Example 10 will show that it is often better to turn them into actual widgets.

We modify the price, quantity, and rate, then the item:

Each time the total TTC changes, a line is added to the history. Changing the item resets the quantity to 1 (on the right).

The difference from [React] lies in one detail: [React] reflects the component’s behavior, which recreates its variables each time; the report must therefore be stored separately, via [useState]. In [Flutter], the state resides in an object ([State]), created once and retained: these are its fields, and [build] is just one of its methods. Therefore, we need neither hooks nor their rules (such as not calling them within a condition or managing their dependencies). The golden rule remains the same: we modify the state only in [setState], and [build] simply describes the screen based on the state.

docs.title: 3.3. Example 03: Writing a Widget Tree
docs.text:
There is no template language in [Flutter]: the screen is written in [Dart]. For conditions and loops, [Dart] provides tools for creating lists of children. This example displays a list of doctors, which can be filtered:

// =========================================================================
// lib/ex03_widgets/main.dart - write a widget tree
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Flutter has no template language (no HTML, no JSX): the
// screens are written in Dart, using nested widget constructors.
// For conditions and loops, Dart provides tools designed to
// create LISTES children (children: [...]):
//    - if (condition) widge         t : a child that is created only if the
//                                       condition is true (“if collection”);
//    - if (c) widgetA else widget   B : one or the other;
//    - condition? widgetA : widgetB  : same as above, in an expression;
//    - for (final x in list) widget  : one child per element in the list
//                                       ("collection for");
//    - ...autreList                 e : the elements of another list,
//                                       inserted here ("spread");
//    - switch (value) { pattern => ... }: one value among several.
// And everything before the `return` in `build()` is ordinary code.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:flutter_svg/flutter_svg.dart';

// an “enumeration”: the only possible values for a specialty
enum Specialite { generaliste, pediatre, cardiologue }

// a data class: its fields are final; a `Medecin` object never changes
// . The "const" constructor allows you to make them constants
class Medecin {
  final int id;
  final String titre;
  final String prenom;
  final String nom;
  final Specialite specialite;
  final bool disponible;

  const Medecin(this.id, this.titre, this.prenom, this.nom, this.specialite, this.disponible);
}

const medecins = [
  Medecin(1, 'Mme', 'Marie', 'PELISSIER', Specialite.generaliste, true),
  Medecin(2, 'Mr', 'Paul', 'TATOU', Specialite.pediatre, false),
  Medecin(3, 'Melle', 'Sophie', 'DUPONT', Specialite.cardiologue, true),
];

// "one value among several, depending on a value": a EXPRESSION switch.
// The compiler verifies that all cases in the enumeration are handled
String libelle(Specialite s) => switch (s) {
  Specialite.generaliste => 'généraliste',
  Specialite.pediatre => 'pédiatre',
  Specialite.cardiologue => 'cardiologue',
};

Icon icone(Specialite s) => switch (s) {
  Specialite.pediatre => const Icon(Icons.child_care, color: Colors.orange),
  Specialite.cardiologue => const Icon(Icons.favorite, color: Colors.red),
  _ => const Icon(Icons.medical_services, color: Colors.teal), // "_": all other cases
};

void main() {
  runApp(
    MaterialApp(
      debugShowCheckedModeBanner: false,
      theme: ThemeData(colorSchemeSeed: Colors.indigo),
      home: const PageMedecins(),
    ),
  );
}

class PageMedecins extends StatefulWidget {
  const PageMedecins({super.key});

  @override
  State<PageMedecins> createState() => _PageMedecinsState();
}

class _PageMedecinsState extends State<PageMedecins> {
  String _filtre = ''; // the search text
  bool _seulementDisponibles = false;
  bool _afficherAide = true;

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
     // the displayed list: a regular variable, recalculated on every build()
    final texte = _filtre.trim().toLowerCase();
    final affiches = medecins
        .where(
          (m) =>
              (!_seulementDisponibles || m.disponible) &&
               '${m.prenom} ${m.nom} ${libelle(m.specialite)}'.toLowerCase().contains(text),
        )
        .toList();

     // "one of the three blocks": we calculate it as AVANT and return it, using if statements
    final Widget contenu;
    if (medecins.isEmpty) {
      contenu = const Text('Aucun médecin.');
    } else if (affiches.isEmpty) {
      contenu = Text('Aucun médecin ne correspond à « $_filtre ».', style: const TextStyle(color: Colors.deepOrange));
    } else {
      contenu = Column(
        children: [
           // one child per doctor: "collection for," with its rank (indexed)
          for (final (i, m) in affiches.indexed)
             // Opacity: Unavailable doctors are grayed out
            Opacity(
              opacity: m.disponible ? 1 : 0.5,
               // ListTile: a Material list row (icon, title, subtitle, end)
              child: ListTile(
                leading: CircleAvatar(child: Text('${i + 1}')),
                title: Text('${m.titre} ${m.prenom} ${m.nom}'),
                 // Wrap: like a Row, but wraps to the next line if there isn’t enough space
                subtitle: Wrap(
                  spacing: 6,
                  crossAxisAlignment: WrapCrossAlignment.center,
                  children: [icone(m.specialite), Text(libelle(m.specialite))],
                ),
                trailing: Chip(
                  label: Text(m.disponible ? 'disponible' : 'indisponible'),
                   // a color selected by a conditional expression
                  backgroundColor: m.disponible ? Colors.green.shade100 : Colors.grey.shade300,
                ),
              ),
            ),
        ],
      );
    }

    return Scaffold(
      appBar: AppBar(
         // an image SVG included with the application (assets/ folder, see pubspec.yaml)
        leading: Padding(padding: const EdgeInsets.all(12), child: SvgPicture.asset('assets/medecin.svg')),
        title: const Text('Exemple 03 - les widgets'),
      ),
      body: ListView(
        padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16),
        children: [
          TextField(
            decoration: const InputDecoration(hintText: 'rechercher...', prefixIcon: Icon(Icons.search)),
            onChanged: (valeur) => setState(() => _filtre = valeur),
          ),
           // SwitchListTile: a toggle switch, with its label
          SwitchListTile(
            title: const Text('disponibles seulement'),
            value: _seulementDisponibles,
            onChanged: (valeur) => setState(() => _seulementDisponibles = valeur),
          ),
          Align(
            alignment: Alignment.centerLeft,
            child: TextButton(
              onPressed: () => setState(() => _afficherAide = !_afficherAide),
              child: Text(_afficherAide ? "Cacher l'aide" : "Montrer l'aide"),
            ),
          ),
           // "collection if": this widget only EXISTE if _afficherAide is true
          if (_afficherAide)
            Card(
              color: Colors.lightBlue.shade50,
              child: const Padding(
                padding: EdgeInsets.all(12),
                child: Text('Tapez un nom ou une spécialité. Les médecins indisponibles sont grisés.'),
              ),
            ),
          contenu,
          const SizedBox(height: 12),
           // a style CALCULÉ: the text size depends on the number of doctors displayed
          Text(
             '${affiches.length} doctor(s) displayed—the size of this text depends on that.',
            style: TextStyle(fontSize: 12 + affiches.length * 2.0),
          ),
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}
  • line 24: an enumeration: the only three possible values for a specialty ([Specialite.pediatre]...);
  • lines 28–36: a data class. Its fields are [final]: a [Medecin] never changes. The constructor [Medecin(this.id, this.titre, ...)] directly assigns its arguments to the fields of the same name. It is [const]: constant doctors can be created (line 39);
  • lines 47–50: “one value among several, depending on a value”: a [switch] expression (not an instruction), which has a value. Each case is written as [motif => valeur]. For an enumeration, the compiler verifies that all cases are handled: adding a specialty without completing this [switch] would result in a compilation error;
  • lines 53–56: the same principle applies when selecting an icon; the pattern [_] means “all other cases.” The icons in [Material Design] are constants of the class [Icons];
  • lines 77–79: the screen state.

The method [build]:

  • lines 84–91: the displayed list: a variable recalculated with each call to [build]. [where] retains the elements that satisfy a condition; [toList()] converts the result into a list;
  • lines 94–100: one of three possible values, selected using [if] before [return]. A widget is a value like any other: it can be stored in a variable. [final Widget contenu;] declares the variable without initializing it: the compiler verifies that each branch assigns a value to it exactly once;
  • lines 103–117: the list. A `[for]` written to a literal list (`[children: [ ... ]]`) adds an element to it on each loop iteration: this is a “collection for.” [affiches.indexed] returns tuples (rank, doctor), which [(i, m)] “unpacks” into two variables;
  • line 106: [Opacity] makes its child partially transparent: unavailable doctors are grayed out. The value is calculated by the operator [? :];
  • lines 108–112: [ListTile] is the list entry for [Material Design]: a header element ([leading], here a disk showing the rank), a title, a subtitle, and an end element ([trailing]). All of these are widgets: any widgets. The subtitle is a [Wrap]: a [Row] that wraps to the next line when there isn’t enough space (on a phone, the icon and specialty wouldn’t always fit next to the “available” label);
  • Lines 117–120: a “bullet” ([Chip]), whose text and color depend on the doctor. [Colors.green.shade100]: a light shade of green.

[return]:

  • line 131: an image SVG, included with the application (folder [assets/], declared in [pubspec.yaml]). [Flutter] cannot render SVG on its own: the [flutter_svg] package provides the [SvgPicture] widget. For an image PNG or JPEG, [Flutter] has the widget [Image.asset];
  • Lines 138–139: the search field. [hintText] is the grayed-out text displayed as long as the field is empty; [prefixIcon] is an icon on the left. This time, no controller: we only need the entered value, received by [onChanged];
  • lines 142–145: a toggle switch, with its label: a list item that you tap to toggle;
  • line 150: an anonymous function, written directly within the parameter: it toggles the state;
  • lines 155–160: an “if collection”: the help card exists only if [_afficherAide] is true. There is no “hidden” widget: when the condition is false, the list of children has one fewer item;
  • line 163: the content selected earlier;
  • lines 167–168: a computed style: the text size depends on the number of doctors displayed.

To summarize the tools in [Dart] that replace, within a list of children, what other frameworks write in their templates:

In DartRoleif (condition) widgeta child that exists only if the condition is trueif (c) widgetA else widgetBone or the othercondition? widgetA : widgetBeither one, in an expressionfor (final x in list) widgetone child per element in the list...autreListethe elements of another list, inserted at this location...[widgetA, widgetB]multiple children at once (often after an `if` statement)switch (value) { pattern => widget }one child among several, based on a value

At startup, then after typing “gen” and hiding the help, then with “xyz”:

docs.title: 3.4. Example 04: Events
docs.text:
An interactive widget receives functions as parameters to be called when something happens; these are often called “callbacks.” This example manages a to-do list:

// =========================================================================
// lib/ex04_evenements/main.dart - respond to user actions
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// An interactive widget receives as parameters the FONCTIONS to be called when
// something happens ("callbacks"):
//    - onPressed:                  f : f is called when a button is pressed;
//    - onPressed: () => delete(t): an anonymous function, to pass its
//                                      own arguments;
//    - onChanged, onSubmitted..    . : the function receives data (the
//                                      text, the checked box...);
//    - GestureDetecto              r : adds gestures (tap, long press,
//                                      double-tap, swipe...) to
//                                      N'IMPORTE QUEL widget;
//    - Dismissibl                  e : drag a line to remove it,
//                                      the typical gesture on a mobile device.
// To interact with an input field from within the code (read or clear its
//text, or give it focus), you associate it with a CONTRÔLEUR and a FocusNode.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:flutter/services.dart';

class Tache {
  final int id;
  final String libelle;
  bool faite;

  Tache(this.id, this.libelle, {this.faite = false});
}

void main() {
  runApp(
    MaterialApp(
      debugShowCheckedModeBanner: false,
      theme: ThemeData(colorSchemeSeed: Colors.indigo),
      home: const PageTaches(),
    ),
  );
}

class PageTaches extends StatefulWidget {
  const PageTaches({super.key});

  @override
  State<PageTaches> createState() => _PageTachesState();
}

class _PageTachesState extends State<PageTaches> {
  final List<Tache> _taches = [
    Tache(1, 'Installer Flutter', faite: true),
    Tache(2, 'Lire le chapitre sur les événements'),
  ];
  final List<String> _journal = [];
   // the field controller: its text (read, write);
   // the FocusNode: its focus (the phone’s cursor and keyboard)
  final _champ = TextEditingController();
  final _focus = FocusNode();
   // a field of the State object that is not displayed: modifying it
   // requires any setState
  int _prochainId = 3;

  @override
  void dispose() {
    _champ.dispose();
    _focus.dispose();
    super.dispose();
  }

  void _tracer(String message) {
    final t = TimeOfDay.now();
    _journal.insert(0, '${t.format(context)} $message');
  }

   // triggered by the ET button or the Enter key on the keyboard (onSubmitted)
  void _ajouter() {
    final libelle = _champ.text.trim();
    if (libelle.isEmpty) {
      return;
    }
    setState(() {
      _taches.add(Tache(_prochainId++, libelle));
      _tracer('ajout de « $libelle »');
    });
    _champ.clear();
     // focus returns to the field: you can type the next task
    _focus.requestFocus();
  }

  void _basculer(Tache tache, bool faite) {
    setState(() {
      tache.faite = faite;
      _tracer('« ${tache.libelle} » : ${faite ? 'faite' : 'à faire'}');
    });
  }

  void _supprimer(Tache tache, String comment) {
    setState(() {
      _taches.remove(tache);
      _tracer('suppression de « ${tache.libelle} » ($comment)');
    });
  }

   // the details of a tap: its position relative to the widget tapped
  void _position(TapDownDetails details) {
    final p = details.localPosition;
    setState(() => _tracer('appui en (${p.dx.round()}, ${p.dy.round()})'));
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Scaffold(
      appBar: AppBar(title: const Text('Exemple 04 - les événements')),
      body: ListView(
        padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16),
        children: [
          Row(
            children: [
              Expanded(
                 // CallbackShortcuts: keyboard shortcuts (a keyboard
                 // — computer, emulator, tablet); Esc clears the field
                child: CallbackShortcuts(
                  bindings: {const SingleActivator(LogicalKeyboardKey.escape): _champ.clear},
                  child: TextField(
                    controller: _champ,
                    focusNode: _focus,
                    decoration: const InputDecoration(hintText: 'nouvelle tâche (Échap pour vider)'),
                     // the "Enter" key on the phone's keyboard
                    textInputAction: TextInputAction.done,
                    onSubmitted: (_) => _ajouter(),
                  ),
                ),
              ),
              const SizedBox(width: 8),
              FilledButton(onPressed: _ajouter, child: const Text('Ajouter')),
            ],
          ),
          const SizedBox(height: 12),
          for (final t in _taches)
             // Dismissible: Swiping the line to the left removes it.
             // key: the IDENTITÉ of the line, so that Flutter knows which one
             // has disappeared (see the course explanation)
            Dismissible(
              key: ValueKey(t.id),
              direction: DismissDirection.endToStart,
              background: Container(
                color: Colors.red.shade100,
                alignment: Alignment.centerRight,
                padding: const EdgeInsets.only(right: 16),
                child: const Icon(Icons.delete),
              ),
              onDismissed: (_) => _supprimer(t, 'glissement'),
              child: CheckboxListTile(
                 // The checkbox is set to GAUCHE, like on a to-do list
                controlAffinity: ListTileControlAffinity.leading,
                value: t.faite,
                 // the checkbox passes its new value (bool?, hence the "!")
                onChanged: (coche) => _basculer(t, coche!),
                title: Text(
                  t.libelle,
                  style: t.faite ? const TextStyle(decoration: TextDecoration.lineThrough, color: Colors.grey) : null,
                ),
                 // an anonymous function: the task at CETTE is passed as an argument
                secondary: IconButton(
                  icon: const Icon(Icons.delete_outline, color: Colors.red),
                  onPressed: () => _supprimer(t, 'bouton'),
                ),
              ),
            ),
          const SizedBox(height: 12),
           // GestureDetector: any widget becomes gesture-responsive
          GestureDetector(
            onTapDown: _position,
            onDoubleTap: () => setState(() => _tracer('double appui')),
            onLongPress: () => setState(() => _tracer('appui long')),
            child: Container(
              height: 80,
              alignment: Alignment.center,
              decoration: BoxDecoration(color: const Color(0xFFE7F5FF), borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(8)),
              child: const Text('Touchez cette zone (appui, double appui, appui long)'),
            ),
          ),
          const SizedBox(height: 16),
          Text('Journal', style: Theme.of(context).textTheme.titleSmall),
          for (final ligne in _journal) Text(ligne, style: const TextStyle(fontSize: 12)),
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}
  • lines 23–28: a task. [faite] is not [final]: we’ll modify it. [{this.faite = false}]: an optional named parameter, with its default value;
  • lines 49–53: the report: the list of tasks and an event log;
  • lines 56–57: to manipulate the input field from within the code, two objects are associated with it: a controller ([TextEditingController]), which provides access to its text, and a [FocusNode], which provides access to its focus (the blinking cursor and the phone’s keyboard, which opens when a field has focus);
  • Line 60: A field of the [State] object that is not displayed: modifying it does not require a [setState]. This is what [React] calls a “reference” ([useRef]); in [Flutter], it is an ordinary field;
  • lines 63–66: the controller and the [FocusNode] are released when the screen disappears;
  • lines 69–71: one additional line at the top of the log. [TimeOfDay] is the time of day from [Flutter]; [format(context)] formats it according to the conventions of the application’s language;
  • lines 75–86: adding a task, triggered by the ET button or by pressing the Enter key on the keyboard. We read the text in the control ([_champ.text]), add the task (in [setState]), clear the field ([_champ.clear()]), and return focus to it ([_focus.requestFocus()]): you can now type the next task;
  • Lines 89–92: Check or uncheck a task: We modify the [Tache] object itself, in [setState]. Unlike [React], there is no need to create a new list: [setState] notifies [Flutter] that the status has changed, regardless of how it changed;
  • lines 96–99: deletion, either via the button or by swiping (see below);
  • Lines 104–106: The function called when the bottom area is tapped. It receives the event details: in this case, [localPosition], the finger's position relative to the tapped widget.

The [build] method:

  • Lines 121–122: [CallbackShortcuts] associates keyboard shortcuts with functions for a physical keyboard (computer, emulator, tablet with keyboard): the Esc key clears the field. [{ touche: fonction }] is a literal [Map];
  • Lines 124–129: The input field, linked to its controller and its [FocusNode]. [textInputAction] selects the “Enter” key on the phone’s keyboard; [onSubmitted] is called when it is pressed, along with the text (which is not used: the parameter is named [_], by convention);
  • line 134: the button calls the same method;
  • lines 138–151: one line per task, in a [Dismissible]: a widget that you swipe with your finger to remove, the typical gesture for a list on a phone. [direction]: only to the left; [background]: what appears below the row during the swipe (a trash can icon on a red background); [onDismissed]: the function called when the row is swiped off the screen;
  • line 143: the key for [Dismissible]. When a list of widgets changes, [Flutter] compares the old list to the new one to determine which widgets to keep: without a key, it pairs them by their rank (the first to the first, the second to the second, and so on). If the first task disappears, the second would take its place… with the state of the first. A key gives each widget an identity: [Flutter] then matches the widgets by their keys. The key must be unique among siblings and stable: the task’s identifier, not its rank. A [Dismissible] requires a key;
  • lines 152–157: a list item with a checkbox. [controlAffinity] places the checkbox on the left. [onChanged] receives the new value of the checkbox, of type [bool?] (a checkbox can have a third state, “undetermined”): [!] indicates that it is not [null];
  • line 160: the label’s style depends on the task: struck through and gray if it’s done, the default style ([null]) otherwise;
  • lines 163–165: a “trash can” button. The anonymous function [() => _supprimer(t, 'bouton')] allows arguments to be passed: the task on this line;
  • Lines 171–174: [GestureDetector] makes any widget responsive to gestures: tap ([onTap], [onTapDown]...), double-tap, long press, swipe, pinch... Here, a simple colored box ([Container]) responds to three gestures;
  • lines 175–178: [Container] is a box, specifying margin, background, border, size, and alignment. [decoration] describes its background: a color, rounded corners. [Color(0xFFE7F5FF)]: a color specified by its code ARGB (opacity FF, then red, green, blue);
  • line 184: the log.

Add a task, check the second one, tap the bottom area; then drag the first task to the left (to the middle while dragging; to the right once the line is removed):

In [React], the browser events ([click], [keydown]...) are the same for all elements; in [Flutter], each interactive widget declares its own, with typed parameters ([onPressed], [onChanged], [onSubmitted]...), and [GestureDetector] adds gestures to those that do not have any. The editor, which knows the parameters for each widget, suggests them as you type.

docs.title: 3.5. Example 05: All Field Types
docs.text:
This example uses the form from Example 05 of course [React], with the input fields from [Flutter]: text boxes, radio buttons, checkboxes, drop-down lists, bulleted lists, sliders, and calendars.

// =========================================================================
// lib/ex05_champs_controles/main.dart - all field types
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A CONTRÔLÉ field displays a value from the state and notifies the widget of
// every change (onChanged), which updates the state: the state is the
// sole source of truth. Modifying the state (via code) modifies the field.
// What onChanged transmits depends on the field:
//    - TextField (with a controller)   -> the text (String);
//    - Checkbox, Switc                h -> bool? / bool;
//    - Radio button (in a RadioG      roup) -> the value of the selected button;
//    - DropdownButto                  n -> the value of the selected element;
//    - FilterChi                      p -> bool: Is the bullet point selected?
//    - Slide                          r -> double;
//    - showDatePicker (a window)      -> a Future<DateTime?>.
// TextField is a special case: it stores its text in a
// TextEditingController, which is created, read (controller.text),
// modify... and then release (dispose of).
// Same form as Example 05 from the React course; everything happens on the
// phone, without a server.
// =========================================================================

import 'dart:convert';

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:flutter_localizations/flutter_localizations.dart';

const titres = ['Mr', 'Mme', 'Melle'];
const loisirs = ['sport', 'musique', 'lecture', 'cinéma'];
const pays = {'fr': 'France', 'be': 'Belgique', 'ch': 'Suisse'};
const langues = {'fr': 'français', 'en': 'anglais', 'es': 'espagnol'};

void main() {
  runApp(
    MaterialApp(
      debugShowCheckedModeBanner: false,
      theme: ThemeData(colorSchemeSeed: Colors.indigo),
       // Flutter’s own text (calendar, buttons OK / ANNULER) in
       // French (see Example 21)
      locale: const Locale('fr'),
      supportedLocales: const [Locale('fr'), Locale('en')],
      localizationsDelegates: GlobalMaterialLocalizations.delegates,
      home: const PageFormulaire(),
    ),
  );
}

class PageFormulaire extends StatefulWidget {
  const PageFormulaire({super.key});

  @override
  State<PageFormulaire> createState() => _PageFormulaireState();
}

class _PageFormulaireState extends State<PageFormulaire> {
   // a status for each form field
  String _titre = 'Mme';
  final _nom = TextEditingController();
  final _age = TextEditingController(text: '30');
  String _presentation = '';
  bool _newsletter = false;
  final Set<String> _loisirs = {'lecture'}; // a ENSEMBLE: no duplicates
  String _pays = 'fr';
  final Set<String> _langues = {};
  DateTime? _naissance; // null: not yet selected
  double _satisfaction = 3;
  String? _envoye;

  @override
  void initState() {
    super.initState();
     // a controller PRÉVIENT its headphones every time the text changes:
     // the screen is redrawn (the model displayed in real time)
    _nom.addListener(_redessiner);
    _age.addListener(_redessiner);
  }

  void _redessiner() => setState(() {});

  @override
  void dispose() {
    _nom.dispose();
    _age.dispose();
    super.dispose();
  }

   // "2026-10-05": the date format of the API RdvMedecins
  String? get _naissanceTexte => _naissance?.toIso8601String().substring(0, 10);

   // all values, combined into a single object (what would be sent to a server)
  Map<String, Object?> get _modele => {
    'titre': _titre,
    'nom': _nom.text.trim(),
    'age': int.tryParse(_age.text), // null if the field is empty
    'presentation': _presentation,
    'newsletter': _newsletter,
    'loisirs': _loisirs.toList(),
    'pays': _pays,
    'langues': _langues.toList(),
    'naissance': _naissanceTexte,
    'satisfaction': _satisfaction.round(),
  };

   // date of birth: a calendar pop-up. showDatePicker returns
   // a Future, the selected date (or null: window closed without a selection)
  Future<void> _choisirNaissance() async {
    final choix = await showDatePicker(
      context: context,
      initialDate: _naissance ?? DateTime(2000, 1, 1),
      firstDate: DateTime(1900),
      lastDate: DateTime.now(),
    );
    if (choix != null) {
      setState(() => _naissance = choix);
    }
  }

   // the modified status PAR LE CODE: the fields follow
  void _exemple() {
    setState(() {
      _titre = 'Mr';
      _nom.text = 'MARTIN';
      _age.text = '42';
      _loisirs
        ..clear()
        ..addAll(['sport', 'cinéma']);
      _pays = 'be';
    });
  }

  void _envoyer() {
     // JsonEncoder.withIndent: indented from JSON; jsonEncode: on a single line
    setState(() => _envoye = jsonEncode(_modele));
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final styleTitre = Theme.of(context).textTheme.titleSmall;
    return Scaffold(
      appBar: AppBar(title: const Text('Exemple 05 - les champs contrôlés')),
      body: ListView(
        padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16),
        children: [
          Text('Titre', style: styleTitre),
           // RadioGroup: the selected value (groupValue) and the called function
           // when one of the radio buttons it contains is selected
          RadioGroup<String>(
            groupValue: _titre,
            onChanged: (valeur) => setState(() => _titre = valeur!),
            child: Row(
              children: [
                for (final t in titres) ...[Radio<String>(value: t), Text(t), const SizedBox(width: 12)],
              ],
            ),
          ),
          Row(
            children: [
              Expanded(
                flex: 2,
                child: TextField(
                  controller: _nom,
                  decoration: const InputDecoration(labelText: 'Nom'),
                ),
              ),
              const SizedBox(width: 12),
              Expanded(
                child: TextField(
                  controller: _age,
                  decoration: const InputDecoration(labelText: 'Âge'),
                  keyboardType: TextInputType.number,
                ),
              ),
            ],
          ),
          const SizedBox(height: 8),
           // Focus: notifies when its child GAGNE or PERD gains focus. The field
           // is not linked to the "on-key" event: its text is read only when
           // the field is exited (such as onBlur in HTML)
          Focus(
            onFocusChange: (aLeFocus) {
              if (!aLeFocus) setState(() {});
            },
            child: TextFormField(
              initialValue: _presentation,
              maxLines: 2,
              decoration: const InputDecoration(labelText: 'Présentation (mise à jour à la sortie du champ)'),
              onChanged: (texte) => _presentation = texte, // SANS setState: nothing is redrawn
            ),
          ),
           // a single checkbox: true / false
          CheckboxListTile(
            contentPadding: EdgeInsets.zero,
            controlAffinity: ListTileControlAffinity.leading,
            title: const Text("Recevoir la lettre d'information"),
            value: _newsletter,
            onChanged: (coche) => setState(() => _newsletter = coche!),
          ),
          Text('Loisirs', style: styleTitre),
           // multiple bullets for UN as a group: the value is added or removed
          Wrap(
            spacing: 8,
            children: [
              for (final l in loisirs)
                FilterChip(
                  label: Text(l),
                  selected: _loisirs.contains(l),
                  onSelected: (choisi) => setState(() => choisi ? _loisirs.add(l) : _loisirs.remove(l)),
                ),
            ],
          ),
          const SizedBox(height: 8),
          Row(
            children: [
              Text('Pays', style: styleTitre),
              const SizedBox(width: 16),
               // a drop-down list: "value" specifies which item is selected
              DropdownButton<String>(
                value: _pays,
                items: [
                  for (final MapEntry(key: code, value: nom) in pays.entries)
                    DropdownMenuItem(value: code, child: Text(nom)),
                ],
                onChanged: (code) => setState(() => _pays = code!),
              ),
            ],
          ),
          Text('Langues parlées', style: styleTitre),
          Wrap(
            spacing: 8,
            children: [
              for (final MapEntry(key: code, value: nom) in langues.entries)
                FilterChip(
                  label: Text(nom),
                  selected: _langues.contains(code),
                  onSelected: (choisi) => setState(() => choisi ? _langues.add(code) : _langues.remove(code)),
                ),
            ],
          ),
          const SizedBox(height: 8),
          Row(
            children: [
              Text('Satisfaction : ${_satisfaction.round()} / 5', style: styleTitre),
              Expanded(
                 // a slider: 5 steps, from 1 to 5
                child: Slider(
                  value: _satisfaction,
                  min: 1,
                  max: 5,
                  divisions: 4,
                  onChanged: (v) => setState(() => _satisfaction = v),
                ),
              ),
            ],
          ),
          ListTile(
            contentPadding: EdgeInsets.zero,
            leading: const Icon(Icons.cake),
            title: const Text('Date de naissance'),
            subtitle: Text(_naissanceTexte ?? 'non choisie'),
            trailing: OutlinedButton(onPressed: _choisirNaissance, child: const Text('Choisir')),
          ),
          const SizedBox(height: 8),
           // Wrap: the buttons wrap to the next line on a narrow screen
          Wrap(
            spacing: 8,
            runSpacing: 8,
            children: [
              FilledButton(onPressed: _envoyer, child: const Text('Envoyer')),
              OutlinedButton(onPressed: _exemple, child: const Text('Remplir par le code')),
            ],
          ),
