          const SizedBox(height: 16),
          Text('Le modèle, en direct', style: styleTitre),
          Container(
            padding: const EdgeInsets.all(8),
            color: Colors.grey.shade100,
             // JsonEncoder.w ithIndent(' ') : the JSON, indented by 2 spaces
            child: Text(
              const JsonEncoder.withIndent('  ').convert(_modele),
              style: const TextStyle(fontFamily: 'RobotoMono', fontSize: 12),
            ),
          ),
           // a block that only exists after a submission; ...[ ] inserts PLUSIEURS widgets
          if (_envoye != null) ...[
            const SizedBox(height: 8),
            Text('Dernier envoi', style: styleTitre),
            Container(
              padding: const EdgeInsets.all(8),
              color: Colors.green.shade50,
              child: Text(_envoye!, style: const TextStyle(fontFamily: 'RobotoMono', fontSize: 12)),
            ),
          ],
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}

A controlled field displays a value from the report and notifies the widget of any changes ([onChanged]), which updates the report: the report is the single source of truth. This is true for all fields in [Flutter]... except for text boxes, which store their text in a controller.

  • Lines 39–41: The text in [Flutter] itself (the days and months of the calendar, the “OK” and “ANNULER” buttons in its windows) is in English by default. We declare the application’s languages ([supportedLocales]), the selected language ([locale]), and the “delegates” that provide translations for [Flutter], in the [flutter_localizations] package. Example 21 will revisit this;
  • lines 56–66: one state per field. [final _nom = TextEditingController()]: for a text field, the state is the control itself; [Set<String>]: a set (without duplicates) of hobbies and languages; [DateTime? _naissance]: a date, or [null] until one is selected;
  • lines 69–74: [initState] is called once, when the object [State] is created (see Example 13). A controller notifies its listeners ([addListener]) of every change to its text: the screen is redrawn so that the template displayed at the bottom keeps up with the input. [setState(() {})]: nothing needs to be changed, only redrawn;
  • line 87: the date in the format of API [RdvMedecins], “2026-10-05.” [_naissance?.toIso8601String()]: the [?.] operator calls the method only if [_naissance] is not [null] (otherwise, the result is [null]);
  • lines 90–100: all values, combined into a [Map] (which would be sent to a server). [int.tryParse(_age.text)]: the age, or [null] if the field is not a number;
  • lines 105–113: the date of birth is selected from a calendar window. [showDatePicker] opens the window and returns a [Future]: the selected date, later, when the user has closed the window (or [null] if they closed it without making a selection). The method is [async]: [await] waits for [Future] to finish without blocking the application. This mechanism is used wherever there is a need to wait (for a window, a server);
  • lines 118–126: the state modified by the code: the fields follow. For a text box, we write to its controller. [..clear()..addAll([...])]: the “cascade” of [Dart], multiple method calls on the same object;
  • line 132: [jsonEncode] (from [dart:convert]) creates the JSON from a [Map].

The fields in [build]:

  • lines 146–151: radio buttons. [RadioGroup] contains the selected value ([groupValue]) and the function called when another value is selected ([onChanged]); it contains the buttons [Radio], each with its own value. [...[a, b, c]] inserts multiple widgets at once: for each title, a button, its label, and a space;
  • lines 160–169: two text fields side by side, in a [Row]. [Expanded(flex: 2, ...)]: the name takes up twice as much space as the age. The age field’s keyboard is numeric;
  • Lines 178–186: An uncontrolled field: [TextFormField] can receive an initial value ([initialValue]) instead of a controller, and manage its own text. The text is updated with each keystroke, SANS [setState]: nothing is redrawn. The [Focus] widget notifies when its child gains or loses focus ([onFocusChange]): redrawing only occurs when the field is exited. This is equivalent to the [blur] event of the HTML;
  • lines 190–195: a single checkbox and its label;
  • lines 199–206: multiple choices for UN as a group: checkboxes to select ([FilterChip]). Each bullet is selected if the set contains its value; tapping it adds or removes the value. [Wrap] places its children side by side and wraps to the next line when there is no more space;
  • lines 216–222: a drop-down list. [value] specifies which item is selected; [items] lists the items, each with its value and widget. [for (final MapEntry(key: code, value: nom) in pays.entries)] iterates through the entries in [Map] and [pays] by “unpacking” each one into two variables, [code] and [nom];
  • lines 230–234: spoken languages, also listed with bullets. (In [Flutter], there is no multiple-choice list: bullets or checkboxes serve this purpose);
  • lines 244–249: a slider, from 1 to 5, in four intervals ([divisions]). Its value is a [double];
  • lines 254–259: the date of birth and the button that opens the calendar;
  • lines 278–279: the template, displayed directly: its JSON, indented by two spaces, in the monospaced font included with the application;
  • lines 283–289: a block that only appears after a message is sent: [if] followed by [...[ ]] inserts several widgets, or none at all.

You choose the title, a name, hobbies, and a language; then you open the calendar; then you send:

The following table summarizes what each field transmits to its corresponding function, [onChanged]:

FieldValue TransmittedTextField, TextFormFieldString (text); or the checkbox is readCheckbox, CheckboxListTilebool? (checked, unchecked, or undetermined)Switch, SwitchListTileboolRadio (in a RadioGroup)the value of the selected button (T?)DropdownButton<T>the value of the selected element (T?)FilterChipbool: Is the bullet point selected?SegmentedButton<T>Set<T>: the selected valuesSliderdoubleshowDatePickerFuture<DateTime?>: the selected date, at a later time

docs.title: 3.6. Example 06: A form, an object, a reducer
docs.text:
Example 05 had a state field for each form field. For a real form, we prefer an object that contains all the values—the model—and we describe its changes in a single function, the reducer: [reducteur(etatActuel, action) -> nouvelEtat]. This is what the hook [useReducer] does for [React]; in [Flutter], there is nothing to import: [Dart] provides everything needed.

// =========================================================================
// lib/ex06_reducteur/main.dart - a form, an object, a reducer
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Example 05 had one status field per form field. For a real
// form, we prefer UN an object that contains all the values, the
// MODÈLE (here, a Profile object, which cannot be modified), and we describe its
// changes in a single function, the RÉDUCTEUR:
//
//      reducer(etatActuel, action) -> nouvelEtat
//
// The widget no longer modifies the state: it DÉCRIT what happened, via a
// object ActionProfil (Edit(Champ.nom, 'Dupont'), Exit(Champ.nom)...), and
// the reducer infers the new state from it. All the logic is contained in a
// place, in a PURE function (same input, same output, no effect
// edge effects), which is easy to test.
// Dart lends itself well to this: a "sealed" class enumerates all possible actions
// possible actions, and a switch statement on an action is checked by the compiler
// (a missed case is an error).
//
// The state also keeps track, for each field, of whether it has been “touched” (exited
// at least once); from this, it is determined whether it has been “modified” (its value differs from
// the initial value) and whether it is disabled.
// =========================================================================

import 'dart:convert';

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

// the name of each field in the form
enum Champ { titre, prenom, nom, age, newsletter, email, pays, naissance, presentation }

// the form data: a NON MODIFIABLE object (all its fields are
// final). To “modify” it, we create a new one (copyWith)
class Profil {
  final String titre;
  final String prenom;
  final String nom;
  final int age;
  final bool newsletter;
  final String email;
  final String pays;
  final String naissance;
  final String presentation;

  const Profil({
    required this.titre,
    required this.prenom,
    required this.nom,
    required this.age,
    required this.newsletter,
    required this.email,
    required this.pays,
    required this.naissance,
    required this.presentation,
  });

   // a copy, in which we change a few fields (the others are retained);
   // "??": the new value if provided, otherwise the old one
  Profil copyWith({
    String? titre,
    String? prenom,
    String? nom,
    int? age,
    bool? newsletter,
    String? email,
    String? pays,
    String? naissance,
    String? presentation,
  }) {
    return Profil(
      titre: titre ?? this.titre,
      prenom: prenom ?? this.prenom,
      nom: nom ?? this.nom,
      age: age ?? this.age,
      newsletter: newsletter ?? this.newsletter,
      email: email ?? this.email,
      pays: pays ?? this.pays,
      naissance: naissance ?? this.naissance,
      presentation: presentation ?? this.presentation,
    );
  }

   // the value of a field, identified by its name
  Object valeur(Champ c) => switch (c) {
    Champ.titre => titre,
    Champ.prenom => prenom,
    Champ.nom => nom,
    Champ.age => age,
    Champ.newsletter => newsletter,
    Champ.email => email,
    Champ.pays => pays,
    Champ.naissance => naissance,
    Champ.presentation => presentation,
  };

   // a copy in which the field UN, identified by its name, has a new value
  Profil avec(Champ c, Object v) => switch (c) {
    Champ.titre => copyWith(titre: v as String),
    Champ.prenom => copyWith(prenom: v as String),
    Champ.nom => copyWith(nom: v as String),
    Champ.age => copyWith(age: v as int),
    Champ.newsletter => copyWith(newsletter: v as bool),
    Champ.email => copyWith(email: v as String),
    Champ.pays => copyWith(pays: v as String),
    Champ.naissance => copyWith(naissance: v as String),
    Champ.presentation => copyWith(presentation: v as String),
  };

  Map<String, Object> versJson() => {for (final c in Champ.values) c.name: valeur(c)};
}

const depart = Profil(
  titre: 'Mme',
  prenom: 'Marie',
  nom: 'PELISSIER',
  age: 30,
  newsletter: false,
  email: '',
  pays: 'fr',
  naissance: '',
  presentation: '',
);

// the complete state: the values and the fields that have already been exited
class Etat {
  final Profil valeurs;
  final Set<Champ> touches;

  const Etat(this.valeurs, this.touches);
}

// possible actions. "sealed": there are no others besides those in
// this file; the compiler knows this
sealed class ActionProfil {
  const ActionProfil();
}

class Modifier extends ActionProfil {
  final Champ champ;
  final Object valeur;
  const Modifier(this.champ, this.valeur);
}

class Quitter extends ActionProfil {
  final Champ champ;
  const Quitter(this.champ);
}

class Majuscules extends ActionProfil {
  const Majuscules();
}

class Reinitialiser extends ActionProfil {
  const Reinitialiser();
}

// the reducer: it never MODIFIE uses the received state; it returns a new one.
// The switch “unpacks” each action: Modify(:final field, ...) reads
// its fields into variables of the same name
Etat reducteur(Etat etat, ActionProfil action) => switch (action) {
  Modifier(:final champ, :final valeur) => Etat(etat.valeurs.avec(champ, valeur), etat.touches),
  Quitter(:final champ) => Etat(etat.valeurs, {...etat.touches, champ}),
  Majuscules() => Etat(
    etat.valeurs.copyWith(prenom: etat.valeurs.prenom.toUpperCase(), nom: etat.valeurs.nom.toUpperCase()),
    etat.touches,
  ),
  Reinitialiser() => const Etat(depart, {}),
};

const titres = ['Mr', 'Mme', 'Melle'];
const champsSuivis = [Champ.prenom, Champ.nom, Champ.age, Champ.email];
// text fields: each will have its own controller
const champsTexte = [Champ.prenom, Champ.nom, Champ.email, Champ.presentation];

void main() {
  runApp(
    MaterialApp(
      debugShowCheckedModeBanner: false,
      theme: ThemeData(colorSchemeSeed: Colors.indigo),
      home: const PageProfil(),
    ),
  );
}

class PageProfil extends StatefulWidget {
  const PageProfil({super.key});

  @override
  State<PageProfil> createState() => _PageProfilState();
}

class _PageProfilState extends State<PageProfil> {
  Etat _etat = const Etat(depart, {});
   // one controller per text field; a “map”: Field -> controller
  final _controleurs = {for (final c in champsTexte) c: TextEditingController(text: depart.valeur(c) as String)};

  @override
  void dispose() {
    for (final c in _controleurs.values) {
      c.dispose();
    }
    super.dispose();
  }

   // LA the only way to change the state: describe what happened
  void _dispatch(ActionProfil action) {
    setState(() => _etat = reducteur(_etat, action));
     // the reducer may have changed some text (capitalization, reset): the
     // input fields must reflect this
    for (final MapEntry(key: champ, value: controleur) in _controleurs.entries) {
      final valeur = _etat.valeurs.valeur(champ) as String;
      if (controleur.text != valeur) {
        controleur.text = valeur;
      }
    }
  }

  Profil get _v => _etat.valeurs;

   // values DÉDUITES from the report
  bool _modifie(Champ c) => _v.valeur(c) != depart.valeur(c);
  bool _desactive(Champ c) => c == Champ.email && !_v.newsletter; // The email requires a letter
  bool get _formulaireModifie => Champ.values.any(_modifie);

   // a text field linked to the template: a method that creates it
  Widget _champ(Champ champ, String libelle, {int lignes = 1}) {
     // Focus: we know when the field is QUITTÉ (it loses focus)
    return Focus(
      onFocusChange: (aLeFocus) {
        if (!aLeFocus) _dispatch(Quitter(champ));
      },
      child: TextField(
        controller: _controleurs[champ],
        enabled: !_desactive(champ),
        maxLines: lignes,
        decoration: InputDecoration(labelText: libelle),
        onChanged: (texte) => _dispatch(Modifier(champ, texte)),
      ),
    );
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final styleTitre = Theme.of(context).textTheme.titleSmall;
    return Scaffold(
      appBar: AppBar(title: const Text('Exemple 06 - un réducteur')),
      body: ListView(
        padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16),
        children: [
          RadioGroup<String>(
            groupValue: _v.titre,
            onChanged: (t) => _dispatch(Modifier(Champ.titre, t!)),
            child: Row(
              children: [
                for (final t in titres) ...[Radio<String>(value: t), Text(t), const SizedBox(width: 12)],
              ],
            ),
          ),
          Row(
            children: [
              Expanded(child: _champ(Champ.prenom, 'Prénom')),
              const SizedBox(width: 12),
              Expanded(child: _champ(Champ.nom, 'Nom')),
            ],
          ),
          Row(
            children: [
              Text('Âge : ${_v.age}', style: styleTitre),
              Expanded(
                child: Slider(
                  value: _v.age.toDouble(),
                  max: 120,
                  divisions: 120,
                  onChanged: (a) => _dispatch(Modifier(Champ.age, a.round())),
                   // The cursor is released: the field has been "exited"
                  onChangeEnd: (_) => _dispatch(const Quitter(Champ.age)),
                ),
              ),
            ],
          ),
          SwitchListTile(
            contentPadding: EdgeInsets.zero,
            title: const Text("Recevoir la lettre d'information"),
            value: _v.newsletter,
            onChanged: (oui) => _dispatch(Modifier(Champ.newsletter, oui)),
          ),
          _champ(Champ.email, "E-mail (si lettre d'information)"),
          const SizedBox(height: 8),
          DropdownButton<String>(
            value: _v.pays,
            items: const [
              DropdownMenuItem(value: 'fr', child: Text('France')),
              DropdownMenuItem(value: 'be', child: Text('Belgique')),
              DropdownMenuItem(value: 'ch', child: Text('Suisse')),
            ],
            onChanged: (p) => _dispatch(Modifier(Champ.pays, p!)),
          ),
          _champ(Champ.presentation, 'Présentation', lignes: 2),
          const SizedBox(height: 12),
          Wrap(
            spacing: 8,
            children: [
              OutlinedButton(onPressed: () => _dispatch(const Majuscules()), child: const Text('Nom en majuscules')),
              OutlinedButton(onPressed: () => _dispatch(const Reinitialiser()), child: const Text('Réinitialiser')),
            ],
          ),
          const SizedBox(height: 16),
          Text('Le modèle, en direct', style: styleTitre),
          Container(
            padding: const EdgeInsets.all(8),
            color: Colors.grey.shade100,
            child: Text(
              const JsonEncoder.withIndent('  ').convert(_v.versJson()),
              style: const TextStyle(fontFamily: 'RobotoMono', fontSize: 12),
            ),
          ),
          const SizedBox(height: 16),
          Text("L'état des champs", style: styleTitre),
           // DataTable: a table, with its columns and rows
          DataTable(
            columnSpacing: 16,
            headingRowHeight: 36,
            dataRowMinHeight: 28,
            dataRowMaxHeight: 32,
            columns: const [
              DataColumn(label: Text('champ')),
              DataColumn(label: Text('touché')),
              DataColumn(label: Text('modifié')),
              DataColumn(label: Text('désactivé')),
            ],
            rows: [
              for (final c in champsSuivis)
                DataRow(
                  cells: [
                    DataCell(Text(c.name)),
                    DataCell(Text('${_etat.touches.contains(c)}')),
                    DataCell(Text('${_modifie(c)}')),
                    DataCell(Text('${_desactive(c)}')),
                  ],
                ),
            ],
          ),
          const SizedBox(height: 8),
          Text.rich(
            TextSpan(
              children: [
                const TextSpan(text: 'formulaire modifié : '),
                TextSpan(
                  text: '$_formulaireModifie',
                  style: const TextStyle(fontWeight: FontWeight.bold),
                ),
              ],
            ),
          ),
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}

The template:

  • line 30: the name of each field in the form;
  • lines 34–43: the form data: a non-editable object, all of whose fields are [final];
  • lines 45–54: a constructor with named parameters, all of which are required ([required]);
  • lines 59–79: To “modify” a non-editable object, a copy is created in which some fields are changed: this is the method [copyWith], a variation of [Flutter] (which we encountered with [TextStyle]). Each parameter is optional ([String? titre]: a string or [null]); [titre ?? this.titre]: the new value if provided, otherwise the old one;
  • lines 84–93: the value of a field designated by its name: an expression [switch] on the enumeration;
  • lines 97–106: a copy in which the field UN, designated by its name, has a new value. [v as String]: the received value (of type [Object], which can be anything) is converted to a string; if it were not a string, it would result in a runtime error;
  • line 109: a [Map] “field name -> value,” created by a [for] within a literal [Map]. [c.name]: the name of an enumeration value (“first name”);
  • lines 112–121: the initial values;
  • lines 125–129: the complete state: the values, and all fields that have already been processed (“touched”).

Actions and the reducer:

  • lines 134–154: the possible actions: a sealed class ([sealed]) and its four subclasses. [sealed] tells the compiler that there are no subclasses other than those in this file. An action describes what happened: [Modifier(Champ.nom, 'Dupont')], [Quitter(Champ.nom)]...;
  • lines 160–167: the reducer. It is a pure function: same input, same output, no side effects; it never modifies the received state, but returns a new one. The [switch] applies to the action, and each case is a pattern that tests its type: [Modifier(:final champ, :final valeur)] verifies that the action is a [Modifier], and stores its [champ] and [valeur] fields in variables of the same name. Since the class is sealed, the compiler verifies that all four actions are handled; adding a fifth one without completing the reducer would result in a compilation error;
  • line 162: a new set, composed of elements from the old set ([...etat.touches]) and the field being exited.

The screen:

  • line 193: the screen state: UN field, the object [Etat];
  • line 195: a text field control, in a [Map] created by a [for];
  • Lines 206–213: the SEULE method for changing the state: describe what happened. [_dispatch] (“ship,” the name given to it by [React]) calculates the new state using the reducer, in [setState]. Then, since the reducer may have modified some text (Uppercase, Reset), the values are copied to the controllers that do not already have them;
  • lines 221–223: values derived from the state: a field is modified if its value differs from the initial value; email is disabled without the newsletter; the form is modified if any of its fields are modified ([any]). [Champ.values]: the list of enumeration values;
  • lines 226–237: a method that creates a text field linked to the template: its controller, its disabled state ([enabled]), and two actions: [Modifier] on each keystroke, [Quitter] when it loses focus;
  • In [build], each field describes its changes using an action: [_dispatch(Modifier(Champ.titre, t!))], [_dispatch(const Majuscules())]...;
  • lines 320–338: a table ([DataTable]), with its columns and rows: the status of each field being tracked;
  • lines 344–349: a text composed of several sections with different styles: [Text.rich] and its [TextSpan].

We change the name, exit the field, and subscribe to the newsletter; then we capitalize the name:

All the form’s logic is contained in the reducer—a function of just a few lines, without any widgets—which can be tested on its own. The widgets now simply display the status and describe what is happening.

docs.title: 3.7. Example 07: Validating a form manually
docs.text:
A pure function, [valider(compte)], returns field errors; it is called each time [build] is executed, so the errors are always up to date. They are not displayed immediately (an empty form covered in red is unpleasant), only for a field that has already been left. Submitting the form displays all errors.

// =========================================================================
// lib/ex07_validation/main.dart - submit a form manually
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A function, PURE, validate(account), returns field errors; we
// It is called every time `build()` is executed, so the errors are always up to date.
// We don’t display them right away (an empty form covered in red is
// unpleasant): only for a field that has already been exited (“touched”). The submission
//marks all fields as affected, then takes action only if the form
// is valid. A TextField displays an error below the field in red,
// when provided with an error message: InputDecoration(errorText: ...).
//
// Same rules as the server RdvMedecins ("Create an Account" form).
// ATTENTION: This validation is simply a CONFORT for the user (a
// an immediate response, without any back-and-forth with the server). It does not protect
// anything: anyone can send the server a request fabricated by
// (curl...). The server therefore revalidates TOUJOURS everything (see example 25).
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

enum Champ { titre, prenom, nom, login, password, confirmation }

// a “record”: a small group of named values, with no class to write
typedef Compte = ({String titre, String prenom, String nom, String login, String password, String confirmation});

const titres = ['Mr', 'Mme', 'Melle'];
final formatLogin = RegExp(r'^[a-z0-9._-]{1,30}$');
const motDePasseMin = 6;

// the rules: a pure function that depends only on its argument.
// For each field with an error, it returns its error message
Map<Champ, String> valider(Compte c) {
  final erreurs = <Champ, String>{};
  if (!titres.contains(c.titre)) erreurs[Champ.titre] = 'Choisissez un titre dans la liste.';
  if (c.prenom.trim().isEmpty) {
    erreurs[Champ.prenom] = 'Le prénom est obligatoire.';
  } else if (c.prenom.length > 20) {
    erreurs[Champ.prenom] = 'Le prénom ne doit pas dépasser 20 caractères.';
  }
  if (c.nom.trim().isEmpty) {
    erreurs[Champ.nom] = 'Le nom est obligatoire.';
  } else if (c.nom.length > 20) {
    erreurs[Champ.nom] = 'Le nom ne doit pas dépasser 20 caractères.';
  }
  if (c.login.isEmpty) {
    erreurs[Champ.login] = 'Le login est obligatoire.';
  } else if (!formatLogin.hasMatch(c.login)) {
    erreurs[Champ.login] = 'Lettres minuscules non accentuées, chiffres, point, tiret, souligné.';
  }
  if (c.password.isEmpty) {
    erreurs[Champ.password] = 'Le mot de passe est obligatoire.';
  } else if (c.password.length < motDePasseMin) {
    erreurs[Champ.password] = 'Au moins $motDePasseMin caractères.';
  }
   // a rule that compares DEUX fields
  if (c.confirmation != c.password) {
    erreurs[Champ.confirmation] = 'La confirmation ne correspond pas au mot de passe.';
  }
  return erreurs;
}

void main() {
  runApp(
    MaterialApp(
      debugShowCheckedModeBanner: false,
      theme: ThemeData(colorSchemeSeed: Colors.indigo),
      home: const PageCompte(),
    ),
  );
}

class PageCompte extends StatefulWidget {
  const PageCompte({super.key});

  @override
  State<PageCompte> createState() => _PageCompteState();
}

class _PageCompteState extends State<PageCompte> {
  String _titre = 'Mr';
   // one validator per text field
  final _textes = {
    for (final c in [Champ.prenom, Champ.nom, Champ.login, Champ.password, Champ.confirmation])
      c: TextEditingController(),
  };
  final Set<Champ> _touches = {};
  bool _envoiTente = false;
  bool _succes = false;

  @override
  void dispose() {
    for (final c in _textes.values) {
      c.dispose();
    }
    super.dispose();
  }

   // the account, as entered: a record generated on demand
  Compte get _compte => (
    titre: _titre,
    prenom: _textes[Champ.prenom]!.text,
    nom: _textes[Champ.nom]!.text,
    login: _textes[Champ.login]!.text,
    password: _textes[Champ.password]!.text,
    confirmation: _textes[Champ.confirmation]!.text,
  );

  void _envoyer() {
    setState(() {
      _envoiTente = true;
      _touches.addAll(Champ.values); // all errors appear
       // Here, the bill would be sent to the server (see Example 25)
      _succes = valider(_compte).isEmpty;
    });
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
     // Errors: recalculated with each `build()`, never saved in the state
    final erreurs = valider(_compte);

     // the error at AFFICHER for a field: only if it has been modified
    String? erreur(Champ c) => _touches.contains(c) ? erreurs[c] : null;

     // a text field: label, error, and a green checkmark if it has been entered and is valid
    Widget champ(Champ c, String libelle, {bool secret = false}) {
      final valide = _touches.contains(c) && !erreurs.containsKey(c);
      return Focus(
        onFocusChange: (aLeFocus) {
          if (!aLeFocus) setState(() => _touches.add(c));
        },
        child: TextField(
          controller: _textes[c],
          obscureText: secret, // characters are hidden
          decoration: InputDecoration(
            labelText: libelle,
            errorText: erreur(c),
             // the error may span two lines
            errorMaxLines: 2,
            suffixIcon: valide ? const Icon(Icons.check_circle, color: Colors.green) : null,
          ),
          onChanged: (_) => setState(() => _succes = false),
        ),
      );
    }

    return Scaffold(
      appBar: AppBar(title: const Text('Exemple 07 - la validation')),
      body: ListView(
        padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16),
        children: [
          DropdownButton<String>(
            value: _titre,
            items: [for (final t in titres) DropdownMenuItem(value: t, child: Text(t))],
            onChanged: (t) => setState(() => _titre = t!),
          ),
          champ(Champ.prenom, 'Prénom'),
          champ(Champ.nom, 'Nom'),
          champ(Champ.login, 'Login'),
          champ(Champ.password, 'Mot de passe', secret: true),
          champ(Champ.confirmation, 'Confirmation', secret: true),
          const SizedBox(height: 16),
          FilledButton(onPressed: _envoyer, child: const Text('Créer le compte')),
          const SizedBox(height: 12),
          if (_envoiTente && erreurs.isNotEmpty)
            _Message('Le formulaire contient ${erreurs.length} erreur(s).', couleur: Colors.red.shade50),
          if (_succes)
            _Message('Formulaire valide : il pourrait être envoyé au serveur.', couleur: Colors.green.shade50),
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}

// a small private widget: a message on a colored background
class _Message extends StatelessWidget {
  final String texte;
  final Color couleur;

  const _Message(this.texte, {required this.couleur});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Container(
      padding: const EdgeInsets.all(12),
      decoration: BoxDecoration(color: couleur, borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(8)),
      child: Text(texte),
    );
  }
}
  • line 24: the account entered is a record: a small group of named values, with no class to write. [typedef] assigns it a name. A record is written as [(titre: 'Mr', prenom: 'Marie', ...)] and read as [compte.prenom];
  • lines 27–28: a regular expression (the format of a login) and a constant: the same rules as the server [RdvMedecins];
  • lines 32–59: the rules: a pure function that depends only on its argument and returns a [Map] “error field → message.” The last rule compares DEUX fields: the confirmation and the password;
  • lines 82–84: one validator per text field;
  • line 86: fields that have already been exited;
  • lines 99–105: the account, as entered: a record generated on demand based on the validators. [_textes[Champ.prenom]!]: Accessing a [Map] returns a value or [null] (the key may be missing); the [!] confirms that it is present;
  • lines 108–113: the submission marks all fields as affected (errors appear), then takes action only if the form is valid;
  • line 120: in [build], errors are recalculated each time; they are never stored in the report;
  • line 123: a local function: the error to display for a field, only if it has been modified;
  • Lines 126–142: a local function that creates a field. [InputDecoration] knows how to display an error: [errorText]. When it is not [null], the field is outlined in red and the message is displayed below it (on no more than two lines: [errorMaxLines]). [suffixIcon]: an icon to the right of the field—in this case, a green checkmark for a filled-in and valid field. [obscureText] masks the characters of a password;
  • lines 165–168: end-of-form messages;
  • lines 176–187: a small private widget, to avoid repeating the same colored box twice.

Fill in a few fields, then submit; then correct everything, and resubmit:

ATTENTION: This validation is merely a convenience for the user—an immediate response without back-and-forth communication with the server. It doesn’t protect anything: anyone can send a manually crafted request to the server ([curl]…), and the code of a mobile app can be modified. The server therefore always revalidates everything (see Example 25).

docs.title: 3.8. Example 08: Flutter Forms, Form, and FormField
docs.text:
The form from Example 07, written using the tools provided by [Flutter] itself. Whereas [React] requires a library ([React Hook Form]), [Flutter] has its own form widgets:

// =========================================================================
// lib/ex08_form/main.dart - Flutter forms: Form and FormField
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The form from Example 07, written using the form tools that
// Flutter itself provides:
//    - Form: a widget that REGROUPE form fields (FormField);
//      accessed via a “global key,” GlobalKey<FormState>;
//    - TextFormField, DropdownButtonFormField...: fields that can be
//      validate. Their `validator` parameter is a function:
//          (value) -> null if the value is correct, otherwise the error message;
//    - autovalidateMode: QUAND validate (here, as soon as the user has
//      modified the field, then with each keystroke);
//    - formulaire.validate(): validates TOUS the fields, displays their
//      errors, and returns true if everything is correct;
//    - formulaire.save(): calls the onSaved method for each field, which sets its
//      value wherever desired.
// The fields are not validated: each retains its value, and the form
// reads it only upon validation and saving.
// =========================================================================

import 'dart:convert';

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

const titres = ['Mr', 'Mme', 'Melle'];

void main() {
  runApp(
    MaterialApp(
      debugShowCheckedModeBanner: false,
      theme: ThemeData(colorSchemeSeed: Colors.indigo),
      home: const PageCompte(),
    ),
  );
}

class PageCompte extends StatefulWidget {
  const PageCompte({super.key});

  @override
  State<PageCompte> createState() => _PageCompteState();
}

class _PageCompteState extends State<PageCompte> {
   // The key that provides access to the form’s state (validate, save, reset)
  final _cleFormulaire = GlobalKey<FormState>();
   // the field key: to revalidate the confirmation when the password changes
  final _cleConfirmation = GlobalKey<FormFieldState<String>>();
   // The password is read from the confirmation rule: a validator
  final _password = TextEditingController();
   // values sorted by onSaved
  final Map<String, String> _compte = {};
   // null: not yet sent; '': sending rejected; otherwise, the JSON is sent
  String? _envoi;

  @override
  void dispose() {
    _password.dispose();
    super.dispose();
  }

  void _creer() {
    final formulaire = _cleFormulaire.currentState!;
    if (!formulaire.validate()) {
      setState(() => _envoi = '');
      return;
    }
    formulaire.save(); // each onSaved stores its value in _compte
    setState(() => _envoi = jsonEncode(_compte));
  }

   // FABRIQUES rules: each returns a validation function
  FormFieldValidator<String> _obligatoire(String message) =>
      (v) => (v == null || v.trim().isEmpty) ? message : null;

  FormFieldValidator<String> _maximum(int max, FormFieldValidator<String> autre) =>
      (v) => autre(v) ?? (v!.length > max ? '$max caractères au plus.' : null);

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Scaffold(
      appBar: AppBar(title: const Text('Exemple 08 - Form et FormField')),
      body: Form(
        key: _cleFormulaire,
        child: ListView(
          padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16),
          children: [
             // initialValue: the initial value; the field then manages its own
            DropdownButtonFormField<String>(
              initialValue: 'Mr',
              decoration: const InputDecoration(labelText: 'Titre'),
              items: [for (final t in titres) DropdownMenuItem(value: t, child: Text(t))],
              onChanged: (_) {},
              onSaved: (t) => _compte['titre'] = t!,
            ),
            TextFormField(
              decoration: const InputDecoration(labelText: 'Prénom'),
              autovalidateMode: AutovalidateMode.onUserInteraction,
              validator: _maximum(20, _obligatoire('Le prénom est obligatoire.')),
              onSaved: (v) => _compte['prenom'] = v!.trim(),
            ),
            TextFormField(
              decoration: const InputDecoration(labelText: 'Nom'),
              autovalidateMode: AutovalidateMode.onUserInteraction,
              validator: _maximum(20, _obligatoire('Le nom est obligatoire.')),
              onSaved: (v) => _compte['nom'] = v!.trim(),
            ),
            TextFormField(
              decoration: const InputDecoration(labelText: 'Login', errorMaxLines: 2),
              autovalidateMode: AutovalidateMode.onUserInteraction,
               // a rule written directly: an anonymous function
              validator: (v) {
                if (v == null || v.isEmpty) return 'Le login est obligatoire.';
                if (!RegExp(r'^[a-z0-9._-]{1,30}$').hasMatch(v)) {
                  return 'Lettres minuscules non accentuées, chiffres, point, tiret, souligné.';
                }
                return null;
              },
              onSaved: (v) => _compte['login'] = v!,
            ),
            TextFormField(
              controller: _password,
              obscureText: true,
              decoration: const InputDecoration(labelText: 'Mot de passe'),
              autovalidateMode: AutovalidateMode.onUserInteraction,
              validator: (v) {
                if (v == null || v.isEmpty) return 'Le mot de passe est obligatoire.';
                return v.length < 6 ? 'Au moins 6 caractères.' : null;
              },
               // the password changes: the confirmation is revalidated
               // (if it has already been entered)
              onChanged: (_) {
                final confirmation = _cleConfirmation.currentState!;
                if (confirmation.value?.isNotEmpty ?? false) confirmation.validate();
              },
              onSaved: (v) => _compte['password'] = v!,
            ),
            TextFormField(
              key: _cleConfirmation,
              obscureText: true,
              decoration: const InputDecoration(labelText: 'Confirmation', errorMaxLines: 2),
              autovalidateMode: AutovalidateMode.onUserInteraction,
               // a rule that reads a AUTRE field
              validator: (v) => v == _password.text ? null : 'La confirmation ne correspond pas au mot de passe.',
            ),
            const SizedBox(height: 16),
            FilledButton(onPressed: _creer, child: const Text('Créer le compte')),
            const SizedBox(height: 12),
            if (_envoi != null)
              Container(
                padding: const EdgeInsets.all(12),
                decoration: BoxDecoration(
                  color: _envoi!.isEmpty ? Colors.red.shade50 : Colors.green.shade50,
                  borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(8),
                ),
                child: Text(_envoi!.isEmpty ? 'Formulaire invalide.' : 'Formulaire valide : $_envoi'),
              ),
          ],
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}
  • Line 46: A form named [Form] contains form fields. To interact with it from the code (validate, save), we assign it a global key, [GlobalKey]: an object that provides access to the state of a widget in the tree ([_cleFormulaire.currentState]);
  • line 48: the key for the UN field, so it can be revalidated on its own;
  • line 50: a password validator: the confirmation rule must read it;
  • line 52: the values stored upon submission;
  • lines 62–69: [validate()] validates all form fields, displays any errors, and returns [true] if everything is correct. [save()] then calls the function [onSaved] for each field, which sets its value;
  • Lines 73–77: rule generators. A validation rule ([FormFieldValidator]) is a function that receives the field’s value and returns [null] if it is valid; otherwise, it returns the error message. [_obligatoire('...')] creates a rule; [_maximum(20, autre)] creates a rule that first applies the rule [autre], then its own ([??]: if the first one finds nothing);
  • line 83: the form and its key;
  • lines 89–94: a drop-down list that is also a form field. [initialValue]: its initial value; after that, the field manages its own value;
  • lines 96–100: a [TextFormField] is a [TextField] that is also a form field: it has a rule ([validator]), a save function ([onSaved]), and an automatic validation mode: [AutovalidateMode.onUserInteraction] validates the field as soon as the user modifies it, and then with every keystroke;
  • lines 112–117: a rule written directly, with two tests;
  • lines 132–134: when the password changes, the confirmation is revalidated using the field’s key, if it has already been entered;
  • line 144: a rule that reads a AUTRE field.

Enter some incorrect values and submit; then correct them:

Which of the two methods should you choose? [Form] and [TextFormField] are sufficient for a form whose rules are written in the application. But in this course, the server’s rules take precedence: the case study has no rules in the application and displays the error returned by the server beneath each field (Example 25). This is the method used in Example 07, which covers fields and their errors.

docs.title: 3.9. Example 09: Formatting Values
docs.text: Each row of the table shows a piece of code and what it displays.

docs.title: 3.9.1. Formatting functions
docs.text:
[Flutter] has no built-in formatting mechanism (the “pipes” from [Angular]): in [build], we call standard functions, stored in a file and testable separately:

// =========================================================================
// lib/ex09_mise_en_forme/formatage.dart - "custom" formatting functions
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Flutter does not have its own formatting mechanism (Angular has its
// "pipes"): in `build()`, we call regular FONCTIONS functions, organized
// in a file and testable separately:
//      schedule(time          slot) -> "8:00 - 8:20"
//      schedule (time slot, Partie.debut) -> "8:00"
// Dart also allows you to AJOUTER methods to an existing type, using a
// "extension": 'marie pelissier'.majusculeInitiale -> 'Marie Pelissier'.
// For dates, numbers, and amounts, the intl package follows the
// conventions for each language (see main.dart).
// =========================================================================

// a time slot, as described by API RdvMedecins
class Creneau {
  final int hdebut;
  final int mdebut;
  final int hfin;
  final int mfin;

  const Creneau(this.hdebut, this.mdebut, this.hfin, this.mfin);
}

enum Partie { tout, debut, fin }

// "8:05" rather than "8:5"
String _heure(int h, int m) => '$h:${m.toString().padLeft(2, '0')}';

// a FACULTATIF parameter, with its default value: [Partie partie = Partie.tout]
String horaire(Creneau c, [Partie partie = Partie.tout]) => switch (partie) {
  Partie.debut => _heure(c.hdebut, c.mdebut),
  Partie.fin => _heure(c.hfin, c.mfin),
  Partie.tout => '${_heure(c.hdebut, c.mdebut)} - ${_heure(c.hfin, c.mfin)}',
};

// a EXTENSION of type String: new methods for TOUTES strings
extension MiseEnForme on String {
   // "marie pelissier" -> "Marie Pelissier"; \p{L}: a letter, accented or unaccented
  String get majusculeInitiale => replaceAllMapped(
    RegExp(r'\p{L}+', unicode: true),
    (m) => m[0]![0].toUpperCase() + m[0]!.substring(1).toLowerCase(),
  );

   // "Marie PELISSIER" -> "MP"
  String get initiales =>
      split(RegExp(r'\s+')).where((mot) => mot.isNotEmpty).map((mot) => mot[0].toUpperCase()).join();
}

// "2026-10-05" (the format of API RdvMedecins) -> a date
DateTime versDate(String jour) => DateTime.parse(jour);
  • lines 16–22: a time slot, as described in API [RdvMedecins]: hours and minutes, as numbers;
  • line 28: “8:05” rather than “8:5”: [padLeft(2, '0')] pads with zeros on the left;
  • lines 31–34: a function with an optional positional parameter (in square brackets), along with its default value: [horaire(c)] or [horaire(c, Partie.debut)];
  • lines 38–47: an extension: it adds methods (in this case, getters) to the type [String], to TOUTES the strings: ['marie pelissier'.majusculeInitiale]. This is a special feature of [Dart], which is very useful for formatting. [replaceAllMapped] replaces each word (a sequence of letters, accented or unaccented: [\p{L}+] with [unicode: true]) with the function’s return value;
  • line 51: “2026-10-05” (the format of API) -> a date ([DateTime]).

docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex09_mise_en_forme/main.dart - format values
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Each row of the table shows a piece of code and what it displays.
// The formatters in the intl package (DateFormat, NumberFormat) are created
// once and for all, outside of widgets: creating them costs more than
// using them.
// The names of the days and months for each language are not loaded
// by default: initializeDateFormatting() loads them, AVANT runApp.
// =========================================================================

import 'dart:convert';

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:intl/date_symbol_data_local.dart';
import 'package:intl/intl.dart';

import 'formatage.dart';

// dates: “ready-made” formats (yMMMd, yMMMMEEEEd, Hms...), or a pattern
final dateCourte = DateFormat.yMMMd('fr_FR');
final dateComplete = DateFormat.yMMMMEEEEd('fr_FR');
final heureSeule = DateFormat.Hms('fr_FR');
final jourAnglais = DateFormat.yMMMMd('en_US');
final motif = DateFormat('dd/MM/yyyy HH:mm', 'fr_FR');
// numbers and amounts
final euros = NumberFormat.currency(locale: 'fr_FR', symbol: '€');
final entier = NumberFormat.decimalPattern('fr_FR');
final pourcent = NumberFormat.decimalPercentPattern(locale: 'fr_FR', decimalDigits: 1);

const jour = '2026-10-05'; // a date in the format of API RdvMedecins
const prix = 1234.5;
const taux = 0.055;
const nom = 'marie pelissier';
const medecin = {'titre': 'Mme', 'prenom': 'Marie', 'nom': 'PELISSIER'};
const langages = ['Dart', 'Flutter', 'Kotlin', 'Swift', 'SQL'];
const creneaux = [Creneau(8, 0, 8, 20), Creneau(8, 20, 8, 40), Creneau(14, 5, 14, 25)];

// the input can be ASYNCHRONE: waiting for languages to load
Future<void> main() async {
  await initializeDateFormatting('fr_FR');
  await initializeDateFormatting('en_US');
  runApp(
    MaterialApp(
      debugShowCheckedModeBanner: false,
      theme: ThemeData(colorSchemeSeed: Colors.indigo),
      home: const PageMiseEnForme(),
    ),
  );
}

class PageMiseEnForme extends StatefulWidget {
  const PageMiseEnForme({super.key});

  @override
  State<PageMiseEnForme> createState() => _PageMiseEnFormeState();
}

class _PageMiseEnFormeState extends State<PageMiseEnForme> {
  DateTime _maintenant = DateTime.now();

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
     // (displayed code, value): a row in the table, in the form of a "record"
    final lignes = <(String, String)>[
      ('dateCourte.format(maintenant)', dateCourte.format(_maintenant)),
      ('dateComplete.format(maintenant)', dateComplete.format(_maintenant)),
      ('heureSeule.format(maintenant)', heureSeule.format(_maintenant)),
      ('motif.format(maintenant)', motif.format(_maintenant)),
      ('dateComplete.format(versDate(jour))', dateComplete.format(versDate(jour))),
      ('jourAnglais.format(versDate(jour))', jourAnglais.format(versDate(jour))),
      ('maintenant.toString()', _maintenant.toString()),
      ('euros.format(prix)', euros.format(prix)),
      ('entier.format(prix)', entier.format(prix)),
      ('prix.toStringAsFixed(1)', prix.toStringAsFixed(1)),
      ('pourcent.format(taux)', pourcent.format(taux)),
      ('nom.toUpperCase()', nom.toUpperCase()),
      ('nom.majusculeInitiale', nom.majusculeInitiale),
      ("'RDV'.toLowerCase()", 'RDV'.toLowerCase()),
      ("langages.take(3).join(', ')", langages.take(3).join(', ')),
      ('jsonEncode(medecin)', jsonEncode(medecin)),
       // two transformations in a row: the result of the first is passed to the second
      ('nom.majusculeInitiale.initiales', nom.majusculeInitiale.initiales),
    ];

    const styleCode = TextStyle(fontFamily: 'RobotoMono', fontSize: 11, color: Color(0xFFC7254E));
    return Scaffold(
      appBar: AppBar(title: const Text('Exemple 09 - la mise en forme')),
      body: ListView(
        padding: const EdgeInsets.all(12),
        children: [
           // Table: a simple table; the first column takes up 55% of the width
          Table(
            columnWidths: const {0: FractionColumnWidth(0.55)},
            border: TableBorder(horizontalInside: BorderSide(color: Colors.grey.shade300)),
            children: [
              const TableRow(
                children: [
                  Padding(
                    padding: EdgeInsets.all(4),
                    child: Text('Dans le code', style: TextStyle(fontWeight: FontWeight.bold)),
                  ),
                  Padding(
                    padding: EdgeInsets.all(4),
                    child: Text('Affiché', style: TextStyle(fontWeight: FontWeight.bold)),
                  ),
                ],
              ),
               // a record is "unpacked": (code, value)
              for (final (code, valeur) in lignes)
                TableRow(
                  children: [
                    Padding(
                      padding: const EdgeInsets.all(4),
                      child: Text(code, style: styleCode),
                    ),
                    Padding(padding: const EdgeInsets.all(4), child: Text(valeur)),
                  ],
                ),
            ],
          ),
          const SizedBox(height: 16),
          Text("Parcourir les entrées d'une Map", style: Theme.of(context).textTheme.titleSmall),
          for (final MapEntry(:key, :value) in medecin.entries) Text('$key = $value'),
          const SizedBox(height: 16),
          Text('Une fonction maison : horaire', style: Theme.of(context).textTheme.titleSmall),
          for (final c in creneaux) Text('${horaire(c)} (début : ${horaire(c, Partie.debut)})'),
          const SizedBox(height: 16),
          Align(
            alignment: Alignment.centerLeft,
            child: OutlinedButton(
              onPressed: () => setState(() => _maintenant = DateTime.now()),
              child: const Text("Actualiser l'heure"),
            ),
          ),
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}
  • lines 21–25: date formatters from the [intl] package. [DateFormat] contains “predefined” formats, identified by the parts to be displayed: [yMMMd] (year, abbreviated month, day), [yMMMMEEEEd] (plus the full day of the week), [Hms] (hours, minutes, seconds)... You can also specify a pattern: ['dd/MM/yyyy HH:mm']. The second parameter is the language;
  • lines 27–29: number formatters: amounts, integers, percentages;
  • lines 40–42: the names of the days and months for each language are not loaded by default: [initializeDateFormatting] loads them, before [runApp]. [main] can be asynchronous;
  • lines 65–83: the table: a list of positional records [(code, valeur)], without field names;
  • lines 93–111: [Table] draws a simple table. [columnWidths]: the first column takes up 55% of the width; [border]: lines between rows. [for (final (code, valeur) in lignes)] breaks down each record;
  • line 124: iterate through the entries in a [Map]: [:key] is a shortcut for [key: key];
  • line 127: the custom function.

For dates, numbers, and amounts, [intl] serves the same purpose as API and [Intl] in web browsers: it understands the conventions of each language (separators, month names, order of components). Note that in French, a thin non-breaking space separates the thousands (1,234.50 €), and the order is “day, month, year.”

docs.title: 10. Interim Conclusion
docs.text:
We have seen, example after example, everything needed to write the [Flutter] client for [RdvMedecins]:

RequirementsIn Fluttera screena widget tree, described by `build()`data that changesthe state of a StatefulWidget (setState), or a ChangeNotifierformsTextField and its controllers, InputDecoration.errorTextmultiple screens, addresses, and guardsgo_router (GoRouter, GoRoute, ShellRoute, redirect)shared dataprovider (ChangeNotifierProvider, context.watch / read)waitFuture, Stream, async/await, FutureBuilderrequests HTTPthe HTTP package, a client that handles cookies, an access layer to the APItwo languagesdictionaries JSON, intl, flutter_localizationson-device storageshared_preferences

The [React] client relied on a library as needed; the [Flutter] client uses fewer of them: [Dart] provides asynchronous processing and types, and [Flutter] provides forms, animations, windows, lists, and the theme. All that remains is to put it all together.

docs.title: 7.1. Example 21: A Bilingual Application
docs.text:
A bilingual application has three types of text to translate:

  • application text: labels and messages. These are stored in dictionaries, one per language;
  • dates and amounts: the [intl] package (see Example 09), in the default language;
  • text from the [Flutter] package itself: the buttons on its windows, the days and months in its calendar. The [flutter_localizations] package provides these.

docs.title: 7.1.1. The dictionaries
docs.text:
{
  "APP": {
    "TITRE": "Exemple 21 - deux langues",
    "LANGUE": "Langue"
  },
  "ACCUEIL": {
    "BONJOUR": "Bonjour {{nom}} !",
    "AUJOURDHUI": "Nous sommes le {{date}}.",
    "PRIX": "Une consultation coûte {{prix}}.",
    "RENDEZ_VOUS_zero": "aucun rendez-vous",
    "RENDEZ_VOUS_one": "un rendez-vous",
    "RENDEZ_VOUS_other": "{{count}} rendez-vous",
    "AJOUTER": "Ajouter un rendez-vous",
    "RETIRER": "En retirer un",
    "CALENDRIER": "Ouvrir le calendrier"
  },
  "ERRORS": {
    "LOGIN_TAKEN": "Ce login est déjà utilisé par un autre compte.",
    "TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS": "Trop de tentatives infructueuses. Réessayez dans {{minutes}} minute(s)."
  },
  "SERVEUR": {
    "TITRE": "Traduire une réponse du serveur",
    "EXPLICATION": "Le serveur RdvMedecins ne renvoie que des clés. C'est le client qui les traduit :"
  }
}

Each text has a key ("ACCUEIL.BONJOUR"). The parameters are written as [{{nom}}]; a plural text has multiple keys, such as [_zero], [_one], and [_other]. These are the conventions of the [JavaScript] [i18next] library, used by the [React] and [Vue.js] clients of [RdvMedecins]: The case study will use their dictionaries as-is. The English dictionary has the same keys:

}

docs.title: 7.1.2. The translations
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex21_i18n/traductions.dart - dictionaries, a common language
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Each language has its own DICTIONNAIRE, a JSON file included with
// the application (assets/i18n/ex21_fr.json, ex21_en.json), where each text
// has a CLÉ ("ACCUEIL.BONJOUR"):
//    - t('ACCUEIL.BONJOUR', {'name': 'Marie'}): the text in the language
//      COURANTE, where the {{name}} parameters are replaced;
//    - t('ACCUEIL.RENDEZ_VOUS', {'count': n}): a plural text; it
//      chooses the key RENDEZ_VOUS_zero, _one, or _other depending on n and the rules
//      of the language (in French, 0 and 1 are singular; in English,
//      only 1);
//    - changerLangue('en'): loads the other dictionary and notifies the
//      screens (a ChangeNotifier), which are then re-translated.
// These are the conventions of the JavaScript i18next library: the
// dictionaries are those of the Vue.js, Angular, and React clients of
// RdvMedecins... and the server, which returns only CLÉS
// ("ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN"), also uses them.
// =========================================================================

import 'dart:convert';

import 'package:flutter/services.dart';
import 'package:flutter/widgets.dart';
import 'package:intl/intl.dart';
import 'package:shared_preferences/shared_preferences.dart';

const langues = ['fr', 'en'];

class Traductions extends ChangeNotifier {
  final String _prefixe; // the dictionaries: assets/i18n/<prefix>_<language>.json
  final SharedPreferences? _stockage;
  String _langue = 'fr';
  Map<String, Object?> _dictionnaire = {};

  Traductions(this._prefixe, [this._stockage]);

  String get langue => _langue;

   // the source language: the one stored on the device, otherwise the language of the
   // phone (if known), otherwise French
  Future<void> demarrer() async {
    final memorisee = _stockage?.getString('$_prefixe.langue');
    final appareil = WidgetsBinding.instance.platformDispatcher.locale.languageCode;
    await changerLangue(memorisee ?? (langues.contains(appareil) ? appareil : 'fr'));
  }

  Future<void> changerLangue(String langue) async {
     // rootBundle: files included with the app (the "assets" section of the pubspec)
    final json = await rootBundle.loadString('assets/i18n/${_prefixe}_$langue.json');
    _dictionnaire = jsonDecode(json) as Map<String, Object?>;
    _langue = langue;
    await _stockage?.setString('$_prefixe.langue', langue);
    notifyListeners();
  }

   // "ACCUEIL.BONJOUR" -> dictionaryQZXW2HTMLBWydBQ0NVRUlMJ10ZQXQZXW2HTMLBWydCT05KT1VSJ10ZQX; null if absent
  String? _chercher(String cle) {
    Object? noeud = _dictionnaire;
    for (final partie in cle.split('.')) {
      noeud = noeud is Map<String, Object?> ? noeud[partie] : null;
    }
    return noeud is String ? noeud : null;
  }

  String t(String cle, [Map<String, Object?> params = const {}]) {
    String? texte;
    final count = params['count'];
    if (count is int) {
       // Intl.pluralLogic: the plural form, according to the rules of the language
      texte = Intl.pluralLogic(
        count,
        locale: _langue,
        zero: _chercher('${cle}_zero'),
        one: _chercher('${cle}_one'),
        other: _chercher('${cle}_other'),
      );
    }
    texte ??= _chercher(cle);
     // an unknown key is displayed as-is: you can immediately see what’s missing
    if (texte == null) return cle;
     // {{name}} -> the value of the “name” parameter
    return texte.replaceAllMapped(RegExp(r'\{\{(\w+)\}\}'), (m) => '${params[m[1]] ?? m[0]}');
  }
}
  • lines 30–34: the translations: a [ChangeNotifier] (the screens will be rebuilt when the language changes), which retains the current language and its dictionary;
  • lines 42–45: the source language: the one stored on the device, otherwise the phone’s language (if known), otherwise French;
  • lines 48–54: change language: load the dictionary, a JSON file included with the application ([rootBundle.loadString] reads a file from the [assets] section of [pubspec.yaml]), decode it ([jsonDecode]), save the selection, and update the screens;
  • lines 58–63: search for a key “ACCUEIL.BONJOUR” in the dictionary: it traverses, section by section, the nested JSON objects. [noeud is Map<String, Object?> ? ... : null]: a type check, which “promotes” the variable in the branch where it is true;
  • Lines 66–83: the translation. For a plural (an integer parameter [count]), [Intl.pluralLogic] chooses the form according to the language rules: in French, 0 and 1 are singular; in English, only 1. An unknown key is displayed as-is: you can immediately see what’s missing. Finally, each [{{nom}}] is replaced by the parameter’s value.

Why not use the official [Flutter] tool? [Flutter] offers a generator ([flutter gen-l10n]) that creates, from [.arb] files, a class with one method per text ([AppLocalizations.of(context).bonjour('Marie')]): The keys are validated at compile time. This is the best solution for an application where all texts are known in advance. But our server returns keys (“ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN”) that need to be translated at runtime: a dictionary, which is queried by the key, is much better suited for this purpose and allows us to share dictionaries with other clients.

docs.title: 7.1.3. The translated page
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex21_i18n/main.dart - a bilingual application
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
//    - the application’s TEXTES files: the dictionaries (traductions.dart),
//      provided to all screens by the provider (see example 20);
//    - dates and amounts: the intl package, in the current language
//      (see example 09);
//    - Flutter texts LUI-MÊME (the calendar, its buttons, etc.): the
//      localization "delegates" of the flutter_localizations package, which
//      follow the locale property of MaterialApp.
// Changing the language re-renders the entire screen without restarting.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:flutter_localizations/flutter_localizations.dart';
import 'package:intl/date_symbol_data_local.dart';
import 'package:intl/intl.dart';
import 'package:provider/provider.dart';
import 'package:shared_preferences/shared_preferences.dart';

import 'traductions.dart';

// what the server RdvMedecins would return (see the chapter on the black box)
const reponsesServeur = [
  (statusCode: 409, cle: 'ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN', params: <String, String>{}),
  (statusCode: 429, cle: 'ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS', params: {'minutes': '15'}),
];

// context.t('CLE'): a shortcut, via an extension of BuildContext
extension Traduire on BuildContext {
  String t(String cle, [Map<String, Object?> params = const {}]) => watch<Traductions>().t(cle, params);
}

Future<void> main() async {
  WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized();
  await initializeDateFormatting();
  final traductions = Traductions('ex21', await SharedPreferences.getInstance());
  await traductions.demarrer();
  runApp(ChangeNotifierProvider.value(value: traductions, child: const Application()));
}

class Application extends StatelessWidget {
  const Application({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return MaterialApp(
      debugShowCheckedModeBanner: false,
       // onGenerateTitle: the application title, translated
      onGenerateTitle: (context) => context.t('APP.TITRE'),
      theme: ThemeData(colorSchemeSeed: Colors.indigo),
      locale: Locale(context.watch<Traductions>().langue),
      supportedLocales: [for (final l in langues) Locale(l)],
      localizationsDelegates: GlobalMaterialLocalizations.delegates,
      home: const PageTraduite(),
    );
  }
}

class PageTraduite extends StatefulWidget {
  const PageTraduite({super.key});

  @override
  State<PageTraduite> createState() => _PageTraduiteState();
}

class _PageTraduiteState extends State<PageTraduite> {
  int _nombre = 2;
  final _aujourdhui = DateTime.now();

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final traductions = context.watch<Traductions>();
    final langue = traductions.langue;
     // instructors in the language COURANTE
    final date = DateFormat.yMMMMEEEEd(langue).format(_aujourdhui);
    final prix = NumberFormat.currency(locale: langue, name: 'EUR', symbol: '€').format(1234.5);

    return Scaffold(
      appBar: AppBar(
        title: Text(context.t('APP.TITRE')),

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
The document’s PDF is HERE.

The document’s codes are HERE.

This document is a product of Anthropic’s IA Claude. It follows the course “Step-by-Step Introduction to the React Web Framework,” from which it borrows the outline, examples, and case study, while changing the target:

  • In the courses [React], [Vue.js], and [Angular], the application runs in a browser; it is built using HTML, CSS, and [JavaScript];
  • In this course, the application is a mobile app, written using the [Flutter] framework and the [Dart] language, which runs on a [Android] phone. The same code, without any changes, also generates a web application (and a [Windows], [macOS], or [Linux] application).

The server, however, remains the same: it is the JSON [RdvMedecins] server from previous lessons, written using [NestJS]. And the application screens are the ones that readers of the other lessons are already familiar with (login with CAPTCHA, doctor’s schedule, appointment window, patient portal, doctor and client management, account creation, French and English), adapted for a phone screen.

The document follows the same structure as its predecessors: first, numerous short examples, each focusing on a concept from [Flutter], followed by a complete case study—the [Flutter] client for the [RdvMedecins] application—with all files fully commented. The 25 examples have the same numbers as those in the [React] course: Readers familiar with [React], [Vue.js], or [Angular] will find the same examples, written in the style of [Flutter].

A course on this topic already exists: An Example of a Flutter Client/Server / NestJS (2026), which presents a complete client right from the start. This document differs in its approach: we learn [Flutter] step by step, through small examples, before tackling the complete client; and the server is treated as a black box, of which only the API and JSON are of interest to us.

A basic understanding of the [Dart] language is assumed: these fundamentals are covered in the course “Introduction to the Dart Language Through Examples” (2026). However, language features specific to [Flutter] (named parameters, classes, [async] / [await], collections, etc.) are reviewed throughout the examples as they are used.

docs.title: 1.1. The Role of Flutter in a Client/Server Application
docs.text:
The application has two parts, which communicate with each other only through HTTP requests:

  • 1: The [Flutter] application, running on the phone, sends a HTTP request to the server, for example, [GET /api/agenda?idMedecin=1&jour=2026-10-05];
  • 2: The server responds with data JSON: this doctor’s schedule for that day. It does not generate any pages;
  • 3: Using this data, [Flutter] updates the phone’s screen.

This is exactly the architecture of the clients [React], [Vue.js], and [Angular]: the only difference is what generates the display. Whereas a browser builds a page from HTML and CSS, [Flutter] draws every pixel on the screen itself, using its own graphics engine. It does not use the system’s components (the buttons from [Android] or [iOS]): it mimics them or provides its own. This is what allows it to display the same application, down to the pixel, on a [Android] phone, a [iPhone], in a browser, or on a computer.

[Flutter] is a framework created by [Google] and released in 2018. It is currently the most widely used framework for writing mobile apps for [Android] and [iOS] using a single codebase. It is based on three core concepts:

  • everything is a widget: the screen is described by a tree of widgets, objects that each represent a part of the interface—such as text, a button, a margin, a column, or an entire screen. You create your own widgets by assembling those provided by [Flutter];
  • the interface is a function of state: a widget has a method [build()] that describes what to display based on its data. When the data changes ([setState()]), [Flutter] calls [build()], compares the new tree to the old one, and redraws what has changed. We never write code that modifies the screen: we describe the screen based on its state. Readers of the [React] course will recognize this principle: it is the same as that of components and [useState];
  • a language, [Dart], compiled into machine code for the phone (resulting in fast applications), or into [JavaScript] or [WebAssembly] for the browser. During development, [Dart] enables hot reloading: a code change is applied to the running application in one second, without losing its state.

Like [React], [Flutter] is not an “all-in-one” framework for communicating with a server: the HTTP client, the router, shared state, and translations are provided by packages (libraries) published on the pub.dev website. This course uses the packages recommended in the [Flutter] documentation and maintained, for the most part, by the [Flutter] team itself: [http] (HTTP requests), [go_router] (the router), [provider] (shared state), [shared_preferences] (on-device storage), [intl] (dates and numbers in each language), [flutter_svg] (images SVG).

docs.title: 1.2. Tools Used
docs.text:
The examples were written and tested using the following tools (their installation is described in the appendix):

  • SDK [Flutter] 3.44, which includes SDK [Dart] 3.12;
  • the [Visual Studio Code] editor and its extension [Flutter] (which also installs the [Dart] extension);
  • [Android Studio], only for its emulator manager, and SDK [Android]: an emulator [Android] (a simulated phone on the computer), or a real phone [Android] connected to the computer;
  • the [Chrome] browser, for the web version of the applications;
  • the SGBD [MySQL] (or [MariaDB]), for example, the one for [Laragon] under [Windows] and [Node.js]: these are required by the JSON server, as described in the chapter introducing it;
  • the command-line tool [curl], which displays the raw HTTP responses.

The packages used are those from the [pubspec.yaml] files: [go_router] 16, [provider] 6, [http] 1.5, [shared_preferences] 2.5, [flutter_svg] 2, [intl], and the packages [flutter_localizations] and [flutter_test] included with [Flutter].

docs.title: 1.3. Screenshots
docs.text: The screenshots in this document were generated automatically by [Flutter] tests ([test/captures] project folders): Each test launches an example, interacts with it as a user would (entering text, tapping buttons), and then instructs the [Flutter] engine to render the screen as an image file at the resolution of a [Android] phone (1080 x 2340 pixels). These are therefore actual screens from the app, rendered by the same engine as on the phone; the only elements missing are the phone’s status bar (time, battery) and the on-screen keyboard. The chapter on the first example shows the same app running on a [Android] emulator.

docs.title: 1.4. The Examples
docs.text:
The code in this document is organized into three folders:

flutter-etape-par-etape-sept-2026/
├── exemples_flutter/          les 25 petits exemples de Flutter (un seul projet)
├── rdvmedecins-nestjs-json/   le serveur JSON RdvMedecins (la « boîte noire »)
└── rdvmedecins_flutter/       le client Flutter de l'étude de cas

The examples make up a single project, [Flutter], with each example located in a folder within [lib/]:

exemples_flutter/
├── android/                    le projet Android (généré par Flutter)
├── web/                        le projet web (généré par Flutter)
├── windows/                    le projet Windows (généré par Flutter)
├── assets/                     les fichiers livrés avec l'application (images, dictionnaires)
├── lib/
│   ├── main.dart               le point d'entrée par défaut (il lance l'exemple 01)
│   ├── ex01_premiere_application/
│   │   └── main.dart           le point d'entrée de l'exemple 01
│   ├── ex02_etat/
│   ├── ...
│   ├── ex25_erreurs_serveur/
│   └── commun/                 du code partagé par les exemples 22 à 25
├── test/                       les tests (et la fabrication des copies d'écran)
├── analysis_options.yaml       les règles de l'analyseur de code
├── pubspec.yaml                la description du projet et de ses paquets
└── web_dev_config.yaml         le serveur de développement web (exemples 22 à 25)

The platform-specific folders ([android/], [web/], [windows/]) are not provided in their entirety: these are small projects—[Android] (web) and [Windows]—that [Flutter] can generate, and which depend on the version of [Flutter] installed. You build them once, then download the packages in a console opened to the [exemples_flutter] folder (in [VS Code]: Terminal menu / New Terminal):

flutter create --platforms=android,web,windows --org fr.stahe --project-name exemples_flutter .
flutter pub get

[flutter create .] (the period indicates the current folder) completes the project without modifying existing files: the provided [android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml] file (see Example 22) is preserved. If you skip this step, [flutter run] fails on a phone with a misleading message: “Build failed due to use of deleted Android v1 embedding” ([Flutter] cannot find the [Android] project and assumes it is very old).

Then run an example by specifying the [main.dart] file with the [-t] option (for “target”):

flutter run -t lib/ex01_premiere_application/main.dart

[flutter run] asks which device to run the application on if it finds multiple devices (an emulator [Android], [Chrome], [Windows]...). You can specify this using the [-d] option (for “device”):

flutter run -d emulator-5554 -t lib/ex01_premiere_application/main.dart
flutter run -d chrome -t lib/ex01_premiere_application/main.dart

While the application is running, the console accepts a few single-letter commands: r (hot reload: code changes are applied, and the state is preserved), R (hot restart: the application restarts from scratch), q (stop). In [VS Code], you can also open the example file [main.dart] and press F5; the device is then selected in the status bar at the bottom right of the window.

Examples 22 through 25 query the JSON and [RdvMedecins] servers: you will need to have them installed and running, as explained in the chapter dedicated to them.
