docs.title: 5. Routing
docs.text: An application has multiple screens. [Flutter] manages them using [Navigator]: a stack of screens, where a new screen ([Navigator.push]) is pushed onto the stack and from which it is popped ([Navigator.pop], or the phone’s Back button). This is sufficient for a small mobile app. But as soon as you want URLs (/doctors/2)—that is, screens that can be referenced, opened from a link, reloaded on the web, and protected by guards—you use a router. The [go_router] package, maintained by the [Flutter] team and recommended in its documentation, is the most widely used.

docs.title: 5.1.1. The data
docs.text:
// "hard-coded" data, so as not to depend on a server in this example
typedef Medecin = ({int id, String titre, String prenom, String nom, String specialite});

const medecins = <Medecin>[
  (id: 1, titre: 'Mme', prenom: 'Marie', nom: 'PELISSIER', specialite: 'généraliste'),
  (id: 2, titre: 'Mr', prenom: 'Paul', nom: 'TATOU', specialite: 'pédiatre'),
  (id: 3, titre: 'Melle', prenom: 'Sophie', nom: 'DUPONT', specialite: 'généraliste'),
];

"Hard-coded" data, to avoid relying on a server in this example: a list of records.

docs.title: 5.1.2. The routes
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex17_routeur/routes.dart - the application's ROUTES files
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// An application has multiple screens ("pages"). The ROUTEUR associates a
// ADRESSE (a path, like on the web: /doctors/2) to a screen. Flutter
// provides the Navigator (a PILE of screens: you stack them, you unstack them); the
// go_router package, maintained by the Flutter team, adds the
// addresses: links, parameters, the browser’s Back button
// and URLs typed manually on the web, the Android Back button.
//    '/doctors/:id'  :id is a parameter (/doctors/2 -> id = "2");
//    ShellRout      e a common “shell” (top bar, bottom
//                     bottom navigation bar) surrounding the route screens;
//    redirec        t a redirect: the old address leads to the new one;
//    errorBuilde    r the screen for an address that does not correspond to any route.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:go_router/go_router.dart';

import 'coquille.dart';
import 'pages/accueil.dart';
// loading DIFFÉRÉ: on the web, the code for this page is downloaded
// until the first visit (Flutter Build Web creates a separate file for it)
import 'pages/a_propos.dart' deferred as a_propos;
import 'pages/chargement_differe.dart';
import 'pages/detail_medecin.dart';
import 'pages/liste_medecins.dart';
import 'pages/page_introuvable.dart';
import 'pages/recherche.dart';

final routeur = GoRouter(
   // the starting address (on a phone: there is no address bar)
  initialLocation: '/',
  routes: [
    ShellRoute(
       // child: the screen for the current child route, placed DANS in the shell
      builder: (context, state, child) => Coquille(child: child),
      routes: [
        GoRoute(path: '/', builder: (context, state) => const Accueil()),
        GoRoute(
          path: '/medecins',
          builder: (context, state) => const ListeMedecins(),
           // a route IMBRIQUÉE: /doctors/2
          routes: [
            GoRoute(
              path: ':id',
               // pathParameters: path parameters, always CHAÎNES
              builder: (context, state) => DetailMedecin(id: state.pathParameters['id']!),
            ),
          ],
        ),
        GoRoute(
          path: '/recherche',
           // uri.queryParameters: parameters after the “?” (/search?q=pediatrician)
          builder: (context, state) => Recherche(q: state.uri.queryParameters['q'] ?? ''),
        ),
        GoRoute(
          path: '/a-propos',
          builder: (context, state) =>
              ChargementDiffere(charger: a_propos.loadLibrary, construire: () => a_propos.APropos()),
        ),
         // a redirect: the URL has no page; it returns another address
        GoRoute(path: '/docteurs', redirect: (context, state) => '/medecins'),
      ],
    ),
  ],
  errorBuilder: (context, state) => PageIntrouvable(adresse: state.uri.toString()),
);

A route associates a path with a screen.

  • Line 23: a deferred import ([deferred]). On the web, this page’s code is compiled into a separate file, which is downloaded only on the first visit to the page ([a_propos.loadLibrary()]). On a phone, all the code is already in the app: [loadLibrary()] terminates immediately;
  • lines 30–32: the router, an object named [GoRouter], is created once, outside of any widget. [initialLocation]: the starting address (on a phone, there is no address bar to display it);
  • lines 34–36: a [ShellRoute] is a common container for several screens: the top bar and the bottom navigation bar. Its [builder] receives [child]—the current route screen—and places it within the shell. This is equivalent to nested routes and the [<Outlet />] of [React Router];
  • line 38: a route—its path—and a function that generates its screen. [state] ([GoRouterState]) describes the current navigation: the address and its parameters;
  • lines 40–47: the list of doctors, and a nested route: [':id'] under ['/medecins'] provides the path [/medecins/:id], where [:id] is a parameter ([/medecins/2]: [id] equals ["2"]). [state.pathParameters] provides the path parameters, which are always strings;
  • lines 52–54: [state.uri] is the full address; [queryParameters] contains the parameters following [?] ([/recherche?q=pédiatre]);
  • lines 57–59: the page loaded on demand by the [ChargementDiffere] widget (discussed later);
  • line 62: a redirect—the route has no screen; its function [redirect] returns another address, to which navigation is redirected;
  • line 66: the screen for an address that does not correspond to any route.

docs.title: 5.1.3. Startup
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex17_routeur/main.dart
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// MaterialApp.router: the application no longer has a home screen (UN),
// The router determines which screen to display based on the address.
// usePathUrlStrategy() : On the web, “clean” URLs (/doctors/2)
// rather than the default format (/#/doctors/2). Has no effect elsewhere.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:flutter_web_plugins/url_strategy.dart';

import 'routes.dart';

void main() {
  usePathUrlStrategy();
  runApp(
    MaterialApp.router(
      debugShowCheckedModeBanner: false,
      theme: ThemeData(colorSchemeSeed: Colors.indigo),
      routerConfig: routeur,
    ),
  );
}
  • line 16: on the web, “clean” addresses ([/medecins/2]) rather than the default form ([/#/medecins/2]). Has no effect on a phone;
  • Lines 17–21: [MaterialApp.router]: the app no longer displays the UN home screen ([home]); the router determines the screen based on the address.

docs.title: 5.1.4. The app's shell
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex17_routeur/coquille.dart - the application’s “shell”
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The top bar, the bottom navigation bar, and, between them,
// the current route screen (child).
//    - GoRouterState.of(context).uri: the current URL;
//    - context.go('/doctors')       : go to an address. The stack of
//      screens is REMPLACÉE, replaced by that of this address (a tab);
//    - context.push('/doctors/2')   : EMPILER one screen above
//      the current screen; the Back button (or context.pop()) collapses it.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:go_router/go_router.dart';

// the tabs: (path, label, icon)
const onglets = [
  ('/', 'Accueil', Icons.home),
  ('/medecins', 'Médecins', Icons.people),
  ('/recherche?q=généraliste', 'Recherche', Icons.search),
  ('/a-propos', 'À propos', Icons.info),
];

class Coquille extends StatelessWidget {
  final Widget child;

  const Coquille({super.key, required this.child});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final adresse = GoRouterState.of(context).uri;
     // the active tab: the one whose path is the beginning of the current address
    int actif = 0;
    for (final (i, (chemin, _, _)) in onglets.indexed) {
      final debut = Uri.parse(chemin).path;
      if (debut != '/' && adresse.path.startsWith(debut)) actif = i;
    }

    return Scaffold(
      appBar: AppBar(title: const Text('Exemple 17 - le routeur')),
      body: Column(
        crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.stretch,
        children: [
          Container(
            color: Colors.grey.shade100,
            padding: const EdgeInsets.all(8),
             // Uri.decodeFull: %C3%A9 becomes active again
            child: Text(
              'adresse courante : ${Uri.decodeFull(adresse.toString())}',
              style: const TextStyle(fontFamily: 'RobotoMono', fontSize: 12),
            ),
          ),
          Expanded(
            child: Padding(padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16), child: child),
          ),
        ],
      ),
       // NavigationBar: the bottom tab bar, typical of a mobile device
      bottomNavigationBar: NavigationBar(
        selectedIndex: actif,
        onDestinationSelected: (i) => context.go(onglets[i].$1),
        destinations: [
          for (final (_, libelle, icone) in onglets) NavigationDestination(icon: Icon(icone), label: libelle),
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}
  • Lines 17–21: the tabs: records (path, label, icon);
  • line 31: the current address. [GoRouterState.of(context)] is a legacy data read (see Example 14): the shell is reconstructed with each navigation;
  • lines 33–36: the active tab: the one whose path is the beginning of the current address. [for (final (i, (chemin, _, _)) in onglets.indexed)] parses both the (rank, tab) pair and the tab record, retaining only the path ([_]: “ignored”);
  • lines 48–49: the current address, displayed ([Uri.decodeFull]: [%C3%A9] reverts to [é]);
  • lines 53–54: the current route screen;
  • lines 59–63: the bottom tab bar ([NavigationBar]), typical of a mobile app. [onDestinationSelected] receives the index of the tapped tab; [context.go(chemin)] leads to its address. [onglets[i].$1]: the first field of a positional record.

Two ways to navigate, using [go_router]:

  • [context.go('/medecins')]: Go to an address. The screen stack is replaced by the one described by this address. This is what you do to switch tabs;
  • [context.push('/medecins/2')]: Push the screen at this address onto the top of the current screen. The phone’s Back button (or [context.pop()]) pops it off the stack, and you return to where you were. This is how you “enter” a detail view.

docs.title: 5.1.5. The pages
docs.text:
// lib/ex17_routeur/pages/accueil.dart
// Title: the title of the browser (web) tab or the app in
// the list of recent apps (Android), as long as the page is displayed
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:go_router/go_router.dart';

class Accueil extends StatelessWidget {
  const Accueil({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Title(
      title: 'Accueil',
      color: Colors.indigo,
      child: ListView(
        children: [
          const Text(
            "Bienvenue. Touchez les onglets : l'écran change, et son adresse aussi. Sur le web, "
            "l'adresse s'affiche dans la barre du navigateur, les boutons Précédent et Suivant "
            "fonctionnent, ainsi que le rechargement (F5) de n'importe quelle page.",
          ),
          const SizedBox(height: 16),
           // links to specific addresses
          Wrap(
            spacing: 8,
            children: [
              OutlinedButton(onPressed: () => context.go('/docteurs'), child: const Text('/docteurs (redirection)')),
              OutlinedButton(onPressed: () => context.go('/page-inconnue'), child: const Text('Lien cassé')),
            ],
          ),
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}

Each page places a [Title] widget: its title is that of the browser tab (on the web) or of the app in the list of recent apps (on [Android]), as long as the page is displayed. Two buttons lead to specific URLs: the redirect [/docteurs], and a URL that does not exist.

// lib/ex17_routeur/pages/liste_medecins.dart - links with parameters
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:go_router/go_router.dart';

import '../donnees.dart';

class ListeMedecins extends StatelessWidget {

// lib/ex17_routeur/pages/recherche.dart - a page driven by the URL
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// /search?q=pediatrician: the page is fully described by its URL.
// On the web, you can bookmark it, reload it, or go back to
// back. Searching is done at the address ALLER /search?q=<input>:
// The page displays what the URL says, and nothing else.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:go_router/go_router.dart';

import '../donnees.dart';

class Recherche extends StatelessWidget {
  final String q;

  const Recherche({super.key, required this.q});

  void _rechercher(BuildContext context, String saisie) {
     // URI: constructs the URL by encoding the necessary parts (é -> %C3%A9)
    context.go(Uri(path: '/recherche', queryParameters: {'q': saisie.trim()}).toString());
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final resultats = medecins
        .where((m) => '${m.prenom} ${m.nom} ${m.specialite}'.toLowerCase().contains(q.toLowerCase()))
        .toList();
    return Title(
      title: 'Recherche',
      color: Colors.indigo,
      child: ListView(
        children: [
           // a controlled NON field, which starts with the value of the URL;
           // key: ValueKey(q): if the address changes (Back button), Flutter
           // recreates the field, which then takes on the new value
          TextFormField(
            key: ValueKey(q),
            initialValue: q,
            decoration: const InputDecoration(hintText: 'nom ou spécialité', suffixIcon: Icon(Icons.search)),
            textInputAction: TextInputAction.search,
            onFieldSubmitted: (saisie) => _rechercher(context, saisie),
          ),
          const SizedBox(height: 8),
          for (final m in resultats) ListTile(title: Text('${m.prenom} ${m.nom} (${m.specialite})')),
          if (resultats.isEmpty)
            const ListTile(
              title: Text('Aucun résultat.', style: TextStyle(color: Colors.grey)),
            ),
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}
  • Lines 20–22: Search for ALLER at the address [/recherche?q=<saisie>]. [Uri] generates the address by encoding the necessary information ([é] becomes [%C3%A9]). The page is fully described by its address: on the web, you can bookmark it, reload it, or go back;
  • lines 38–43: an unvalidated field that starts with the value of the URL. [key: ValueKey(q)]: if the URL changes (browser’s Back button), the key changes; [Flutter] recreates the field, which takes on the new value. [textInputAction: TextInputAction.search]: The Enter key on the phone’s keyboard acts as a magnifying glass.

// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A screen whose code is loaded on demand (deferred import):
// load() downloads the code (a Future), build() constructs the screen
// once the code arrives. In the meantime: a loading indicator.
// FutureBuilder rebuilds its content when the Future completes
// (see Example 19).
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

class ChargementDiffere extends StatefulWidget {
  final Future<void> Function() charger;
  final Widget Function() construire;

  const ChargementDiffere({super.key, required this.charger, required this.construire});

  @override
  State<ChargementDiffere> createState() => _ChargementDiffereState();
}

class _ChargementDiffereState extends State<ChargementDiffere> {
   // The Future is created UNE times (not with every build)
  late final Future<void> _chargement = widget.charger();

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return FutureBuilder(
      future: _chargement,
      builder: (context, etat) => etat.connectionState == ConnectionState.done
          ? widget.construire()
          : const Center(child: CircularProgressIndicator()),
    );
  }
}
  • line 25: the code is loaded, initiated UNE times (a [late] field initialized on its first read): if it were initiated in [build], each reconstruction would trigger it again;
  • Lines 29–33: [FutureBuilder] rebuilds its content when [Future] terminates: in the meantime, a loading indicator; then, the screen (see Example 19).

// =========================================================================
// lib/ex18_gardes/session.dart - a session SIMULÉE (without a server)
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The logged-in user must be recognized by ÉCRANS (the top bar,
// the calendar) and the router’s GARDES (features that are not
// widgets). It is stored in a single object, a ChangeNotifier:
//    - a private field, the state;
//    - methods to read and modify it;
//    - notifyListeners(): notifies its subscribers (the router, the screens)
//      when it changes.
// (Example 23 will do the same thing with a real server.)
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';

enum Role { admin, doctor, user }

typedef Utilisateur = ({String login, Role role});

// three "hard-coded" accounts (password = login)
const _comptes = {'admin': Role.admin, 'pelissier': Role.doctor, 'martin': Role.user};

class Session extends ChangeNotifier {
  Utilisateur? _utilisateur; // status: null, no one is logged in

  Utilisateur? get utilisateur => _utilisateur;

  bool connecter(String login, String password) {
    final role = _comptes[login];
    if (role == null || password != login) {
      return false;
    }
    _utilisateur = (login: login, role: role);
    notifyListeners();
    return true;
  }

  void deconnecter() {
    _utilisateur = null;
    notifyListeners();
  }
}

// the application’s single session
final session = Session();

The logged-in user must be recognized by the screens (the top bar, the calendar) and the router’s controls—features that are not widgets. It is stored in a single object, a [ChangeNotifier] (see Example 14):

  • line 24: the status: a user, or [null];
  • lines 28–35: the connection, simulated: three “hard-coded” accounts (password = login). It notifies its subscribers ([notifyListeners()]);
  • line 45: the application’s single session, a global variable. (Example 23 will do the same thing with a real server.)

docs.title: 5.2.2. Guards and Protected Paths
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex18_gardes/routes.dart - PROTÉGÉES routes protected by guards
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// redirect: a function that go_router calls AVANT on every navigation
// (that of GoRouter: for all routes; that of a GoRoute:
// for that route alone). It receives the navigation status (state.uri:
// the requested address) and returns:
//    - null: navigation continues;
//    - an address: navigation is replaced by navigation to
//      that address.
// refreshListenable: an object at ÉCOUTER; when it signals a
// change (session: login, logout), the router reevaluates
// its guards for the current screen.
//
// This is the client-side equivalent of the guards NestJS (JwtAuthGuard,
// RolesGuard) — with one difference, FONDAMENTALE: a client guard is
// merely a convenience. The application is in the hands of the user, who
// can modify it at will. True data protection remains that
// provided by the SERVEUR (see the chapter on the black box).
// =========================================================================

import 'package:go_router/go_router.dart';

import 'coquille.dart';
import 'pages/accueil.dart';
import 'pages/administration.dart' deferred as administration;
import 'pages/agenda.dart';
import 'pages/connexion.dart';
import '../ex17_routeur/pages/chargement_differe.dart';
import 'session.dart';

// the “login required” prompt: not logged in -> to the login page,
// remembering where you wanted to go
String? connexionRequise(GoRouterState state) {
  if (session.utilisateur == null) {
    return Uri(path: '/connexion', queryParameters: {'redirect': state.uri.toString()}).toString();
  }
  return null;
}

// the “role required” guard: a function that triggers FABRIQUE a guard
String? Function(GoRouterState) roleRequis(Set<Role> roles) {
  return (state) {
    final u = session.utilisateur;
    if (u == null || !roles.contains(u.role)) {
       // is logged in, but not with the correct role: returns to the home page, with a reason
      return Uri(path: '/', queryParameters: {'refus': state.uri.path}).toString();
    }
    return null;
  };
}

final routeur = GoRouter(
  refreshListenable: session,
  routes: [
    ShellRoute(
      builder: (context, state, child) => Coquille(child: child),
      routes: [
        GoRoute(
          path: '/',
          builder: (context, state) => Accueil(refus: state.uri.queryParameters['refus']),
        ),
        GoRoute(
          path: '/connexion',
          builder: (context, state) => Connexion(redirection: state.uri.queryParameters['redirect']),
        ),
        GoRoute(
          path: '/agenda',
          redirect: (context, state) => connexionRequise(state),
          builder: (context, state) => const Agenda(),
        ),
        GoRoute(
          path: '/administration',
           // the guards, in order: the first one that returns an address wins
          redirect: (context, state) => connexionRequise(state) ?? roleRequis({Role.admin})(state),
           // the page code is loaded only after the guards have been passed
          builder: (context, state) =>
              ChargementDiffere(charger: administration.loadLibrary, construire: () => administration.Administration()),
        ),
      ],
    ),
  ],
   // any other address (no matching route): return to the home page
  onException: (context, state, routeur) => routeur.go('/'),
);

With [go_router], a guard is a redirect function, called before each navigation (the one for [GoRouter]: for all routes; the one for [GoRoute]: for that route alone). It receives the navigation state and returns:

  • [null]: the navigation continues;
  • an address: the navigation is replaced by a navigation to that address.

The code:

  • lines 34–38: the “connection required” guard: not connected? Redirects to the login page, while retaining the intended destination (parameter [redirect]);
  • lines 42–47: the “role required” guard is generated by a function that receives the permitted roles and returns the guard. Logged in, but without the correct role: redirect to the home page, with a reason (parameter [refus]);
  • line 54: the router monitors the session: when it detects a change (login, logout), it reevaluates the guards for the current screen. If you log out from the calendar, you are immediately redirected to the login page;
  • line 69: the calendar requires the user to be logged in;
  • line 75: the administration page requires the user to be logged in (ET) and to have the role (ADMIN): the checks are chained with [??]; the first one that returns an address takes precedence;
  • Lines 77–78: The code for the administration page is loaded only after the guards have been passed;
  • line 84: any other address redirects to the home page.

This is the client-side equivalent of the server checks [NestJS] ([JwtAuthGuard], [RolesGuard]), with one difference: FONDAMENTALE—a client-side guard is merely a convenience (to avoid displaying an unnecessary screen). The application is in the user’s hands, who can modify it as they wish; true data protection remains on the server, which re-verifies everything with every request (see the chapter on the black box).

// =========================================================================
// lib/ex18_gardes/coquille.dart - links, and the logged-in user
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// ListenableBuilder: rebuilds its content every time the object
// being monitored (the session) signals a change. The top bar follows
// the logged-in user.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:go_router/go_router.dart';

import 'session.dart';

class Coquille extends StatelessWidget {
  final Widget child;

  const Coquille({super.key, required this.child});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final chemin = GoRouterState.of(context).uri.path;

     // A link: bold if it points to the currently displayed page
    Widget lien(String cible, String libelle) => TextButton(
      onPressed: () => context.go(cible),
      child: Text(libelle, style: TextStyle(fontWeight: chemin == cible ? FontWeight.bold : FontWeight.normal)),
    );

    return Scaffold(
      appBar: AppBar(
        title: const Text('Exemple 18 - les gardes'),
        actions: [
          ListenableBuilder(
            listenable: session,
            builder: (context, _) {
              final u = session.utilisateur;
              if (u == null) {
                return TextButton(onPressed: () => context.go('/connexion'), child: const Text('connexion'));
              }
              return Row(
                children: [
                  Chip(label: Text('${u.login} ${u.role.name.toUpperCase()}')),
                  IconButton(
                    tooltip: 'déconnexion',
                    icon: const Icon(Icons.logout),
                    onPressed: () {
                      session.deconnecter();
                      context.go('/');
                    },
                  ),
                ],
              );
            },
          ),
        ],
      ),
      body: Column(
        crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
        children: [
          Wrap(
            children: [
              lien('/', 'Accueil'),
              lien('/agenda', 'Agenda (connecté)'),
              lien('/administration', 'Administration (ADMIN)'),
            ],
          ),
          const Divider(),
          Expanded(
            child: Padding(padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16), child: child),
          ),
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}
  • lines 24–26: a local function that creates a link: in bold if it refers to the currently displayed page;
  • lines 33–37: [ListenableBuilder] rebuilds its content every time the monitored object (the session) signals a change: the top bar follows the logged-in user;
  • lines 46–48: logout, then the welcome page. 
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex18_gardes/pages/connexion.dart
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// After logging in, the user is redirected to the page they wanted
// (the ?redirect=... parameter set by the guard), or to the home page.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:go_router/go_router.dart';

import '../session.dart';

class Connexion extends StatefulWidget {
  final String? redirection;

  const Connexion({super.key, this.redirection});

  @override
  State<Connexion> createState() => _ConnexionState();
}

class _ConnexionState extends State<Connexion> {
  final _login = TextEditingController();
  final _password = TextEditingController();
  bool _erreur = false;

  @override
  void dispose() {
    _login.dispose();
    _password.dispose();
    super.dispose();
  }

  void _valider() {
    if (!session.connecter(_login.text.trim(), _password.text)) {
      setState(() => _erreur = true);
      return;
    }
     // Only a path like INTERNE is accepted: it starts with /, but not with //
     // (//site.com/... refers to a AUTRE site) - no redirection to another site
    final r = widget.redirection;
    final interne = r != null && r.startsWith('/') && !r.startsWith('//');
    context.go(interne ? r : '/');
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return ListView(
      children: [
        if (widget.redirection != null)
          Card(
            color: Colors.amber.shade50,
            child: Padding(
              padding: const EdgeInsets.all(12),
              child: Text('Connectez-vous pour ouvrir ${widget.redirection}.'),
            ),
          ),
        TextField(
          controller: _login,
          decoration: const InputDecoration(labelText: 'login'),
        ),
        TextField(
          controller: _password,
          obscureText: true,
          decoration: const InputDecoration(labelText: 'mot de passe'),
          onSubmitted: (_) => _valider(),
        ),
        const SizedBox(height: 16),
        Align(
          alignment: Alignment.centerLeft,
          child: FilledButton(onPressed: _valider, child: const Text('Se connecter')),
        ),
        if (_erreur)
          const Padding(
            padding: EdgeInsets.only(top: 8),
            child: Text('Login ou mot de passe incorrect.', style: TextStyle(color: Colors.red)),
          ),
      ],
    );
  }
}
  • lines 41–43: After login, the user is redirected to the page they wanted to open (parameter [redirect] set by the guard), or to the home page. Only an internal path is accepted: it begins with [/], but not with [//] ([//site.com/...] refers to a AUTRE site). On the web, a login URL generated by a third party ([/connexion?redirect=//site-pirate.com]) will therefore never lead anywhere else.

docs.title: 2.1. Installing the Tools
docs.text:
1. Node.js: Download and install version 22 (or later) from nodejs.org. Verify the installation in a terminal:

    node --version
npm --version

  2. Visual Studio Code (VSCode): available for free download at code.visualstudio.com. Install the “TypeScript and JavaScript Language Features” extension (usually already included).

  3. [MySQL] 8: Install, for example, via XAMPP, Laragon (on Windows), or directly via [MySQL] Community Server. A graphical administration tool (phpMyAdmin, [MySQL] Workbench, DBeaver, HeidiSQL…) simplifies the process. Subsequently, the Laragon tool is used.

docs.title: 2.2. Installing the Flutter client
docs.text:
Launch VSCode without specifying a project:

  • In [1-2], open the command palette;

  • In [3], create a new Flutter project;

  • in [4], create an app;

  • In [5-6], specify a folder where the project subfolder will be created;

  • in [6], name the project. This will also be the name of the folder created for the project;

  • In [1-3], specify the project targets in [1 – application Android, 2- application de bureau 3 – application web];

  • to [4], the created project. VSCode automatically downloads SDK from Flutter;

The [flutter doctor] command verifies that everything [Flutter] needs is in place, target by target. Run VSCode in a terminal for the newly created Flutter project:

flutter doctor

When everything is correct, you’ll get a result like this (version numbers may vary):

docs.title: 2.3. Android Studio and Android command-line tools
docs.text:
The target device for this course is a [Android] phone. To compile the application and install it on this phone, [Flutter] requires SDK and [Android], which are installed along with [Android Studio], Google's development environment. [Android Studio] is not used for writing code—the editor remains [VSCode]—it is used here solely to install and update SDK and [Android].

  1. [Android Studio]: Download it for free from [https://developer.android.com/studio] and then install it. When you launch it for the first time, the wizard will offer a standard installation: accept it, and it will download SDK and [Android].

  1. Open [SDK Manager] from [Android Studio] (the [Tools / SDK Manager] menu when a project is open, or [More Actions / SDK Manager] from the home screen): This is the file that installs and updates the components of SDK and [Android].
  1. [SDK Platforms] tab: Verify that a recent [Android] platform is installed (the [Flutter] documentation specifies version 36 at the time of writing).

  1. [SDK Tools] tab: Check [Android SDK Command-line Tools (latest)], [Android SDK Build-Tools], and [Android SDK Platform-Tools] (as well as [Android Emulator] if you want to test on an emulator), then click [Apply]. The documentation for [Flutter] also recommends [CMake] and [NDK (Side by side)]. It is the [Android SDK Command-line Tools] packages that are missing when [flutter doctor] displays “cmdline-tools component is missing.”
  2. Accept the licenses for SDK and [Android] by entering the following command in a terminal within the Flutter project, then answering “[y]” to each question until you see the message “All SDK package licenses accepted.”: 
flutter doctor –android-licenses

[Remarque]: With version 23.0 of [Android SDK Command-line Tools], the command above may complete immediately, without prompting for anything, displaying “The --licenses option is no longer needed.” This is a known issue in [Flutter] (issues 191558 and 191487 on github.com/flutter/flutter). Workaround: In [SDK Manager], [SDK Tools] tab, check [Show Package Details], replace version 23.0 of [Android SDK Command-line Tools] with version 22.0, click on [Apply], and then rerun the command.

docs.title: 2.4. Set up an Android emulator
docs.text:
If you don’t have a phone, you can test the app on a [Android] emulator: a virtual phone that runs in a window on your computer. [Android Studio] installs the [Android Emulator] program (if it was checked in the [SDK Manager], see above) but does not provide a ready-to-use virtual device: you must create one.

  1. [Prérequis]: Virtualization must be enabled in the computer’s [BIOS], and under [Windows], the [Plateforme de l'hyperviseur Windows] feature must be checked ([Panneau de configuration / Programmes / Activer ou désactiver des fonctionnalités Windows]), which requires a restart. Otherwise, the emulator will not start or will remain very slow.
  2. Open [Device Manager] from [Android Studio]: [More Actions / Virtual Device Manager] from the home screen, or [Tools / Device Manager] when a project is open (depending on the version: [View / Tool Windows / Device Manager]).

  1. Click on [Create Device], select a template (for example, [Pixel 8]), then [Next]. Select a recent [Android] system image for the [x86_64] processor and download it using the [Download] link located next to it, then [Next] and [Finish].

  1. Start the emulator using the [Play] button on the [Device Manager]:

  1. Wait until the [Android] home screen appears in the emulator window: the first startup may take several minutes. Then verify that [Flutter] recognizes the emulator, which should appear in the list (for example, [emulator-5554], platform [android-x64]): 
flutter devices


PS C:\Data\st-2026\dev\flutter-nestjs-sept-2026\rdvmedecins_flutter_client> flutter devices
Found 4 connected devices:
  sdk gphone16k x86 64 (mobile) • emulator-5554 • android-x64    • Android 17 (API 37) (emulator)
  Windows (desktop)             • windows       • windows-x64    • Microsoft Windows [version
  10.0.26200.9457]
  Chrome (web)                  • chrome        • web-javascript • Google Chrome 153.0.8010.48
  Edge (web)                    • edge          • web-javascript • Microsoft Edge 153.0.4234.48

[Remarque]: if [flutter devices] does not display the emulator but instead shows the message “Device emulator-5554 is offline,” the emulator has not finished starting up, or [adb] (the tool that connects the computer to the device, installed along with [Android SDK Platform-Tools]) is in an inconsistent state. Try the following in order: (1) wait for the welcome screen to appear, then rerun the command; (2) restart [adb] using the following three commands (in [Windows], within [PowerShell]), with the last one displaying “device” rather than “offline”; (3) In the device’s [Device Manager] menu ([⋮]), select [Cold Boot Now], or even [Wipe Data] as a last resort.

& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Android\Sdk\platform-tools\adb.exe" kill-server
& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Android\Sdk\platform-tools\adb.exe" start-server
& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Android\Sdk\platform-tools\adb.exe" devices

If the problem persists, use [where.exe adb] to verify that no other [adb], of a different version, is present in the [PATH]: Two versions of [adb] competing for the connection cause this issue.

Once the emulator is recognized, the application launches on it with the following command (see the “Installation and Execution” section): 

flutter run -d emulator-5554

Preparing the Android phone

To run the application on a real [Android] phone, the phone must be set to allow control from the computer:

  1. Enable developer options: open [Paramètres / À propos du téléphone], then tap [Numéro de build] several times (usually 7) until the phone indicates that you are a developer. The exact labels vary by manufacturer.
  2. Enable [Débogage USB] in the [Options pour les développeurs] menu (added in the previous step).
  3. Connect the phone to the computer using a USB cable that transfers data (not just charges the phone), and accept the USB debugging authorization request on the phone. On Windows, if the phone is not recognized, install the manufacturer’s driver USB (“OEM USB drivers,” see [https://developer.android.com/studio/run/oem-usb]).
  4. Verify that [Flutter] can detect the phone: it should appear in the list displayed by the following command, along with the [android] platform: 
flutter devices

The phone will access the [NestJS] server via the computer’s IP address on the local network (not via [localhost]): this configuration is described in Chapter 5.

docs.title: 8. The RdvMedecins server, a black box
docs.text:
Examples 22 through 25, followed by the case study, interact with a server: the JSON server of the [RdvMedecins] application. This is the [NestJS] server for courses [React], [Vue.js], and [Angular]: the server for course [NestJS], whose controllers no longer generate HTML pages but instead produce JSON responses. Readers of these lectures are already familiar with this chapter, which is reproduced here almost unchanged; they need only focus on the section on authentication, which explains what changes for a mobile application.

In this course, this server is a black box: you don’t need to know how it’s written. All that matters is its API—that is, the list of HTTP requests it accepts and the responses it returns. This is the typical situation for a client developer: the API is a contract, and the server team can change whatever they want behind that contract. Its source code is provided ([rdvmedecins-nestjs-json] folder) and extensively commented, for the curious reader.

This chapter explains how to install the server, describes its API, and queries it using [curl].

docs.title: 8.1. The RdvMedecins Application
docs.text:
The application manages appointments for a medical practice. It has three roles:

RoleWhoWhat they can do[ADMIN]The administrator ([admin])Schedule and cancel appointments for all patients; manage doctors and clients[DOCTOR]Doctors ([pelissier], [tatou], [dupont])Schedule and cancel appointments for all patients; view all names in the calendars[USER]Patients ([martin], [durand], [bistrou], [german])book appointments for themselves; cancel their appointments; manage their accounts. In a calendar, they cannot see the names of other patients

Demo accounts use their login as the password. The management rules are verified by the server, regardless of the client:

  • no appointments in the past;
  • only one upcoming appointment per patient;
  • a time slot can only be booked once per day;
  • two doctors (or two clients) cannot have the same first and last names; a login belongs to only one account;
  • a doctor with appointments cannot be deleted;
  • A record that has been modified in the meantime by someone else cannot be overwritten (optimistic lock);
  • a patient is never assigned the name of another patient.

docs.title: 8.2. Installation
docs.text:
You need [Node.js] and a [MySQL] (or [MariaDB]) server: their installation is described in the appendix.

  1. The database. The script [database/dbrdvmedecins2.sql] creates the database [dbrdvmedecins2], its tables, and its sample data. Using [Laragon], run it from within [HeidiSQL] (File menu / Run a SQL file); at the command line:
mysql -u root -p < database/dbrdvmedecins2.sql

The script always starts with an empty database: you can rerun it to restore the initial data.

  1. Libraries. In a console window open to the [rdvmedecins-nestjs-json] folder:
npm install
  1. Configuration. Copy the file [.env.example] to [.env] (under [Windows]: [copy .env.example .env]), then modify it:
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Sample configuration file.
# Copy this file to [.env], then adjust the values for your machine.
# The file [.env] must never be shared or committed (passwords).
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------

# JSON server listening port
PORT=8080

# Database connection settings MySQL [dbrdvmedecins2]
# (script: database/dbrdvmedecins2.sql)
DB_HOST=localhost
DB_PORT=3306
DB_USERNAME=root
DB_PASSWORD=
DB_DATABASE=dbrdvmedecins2
# true: displays in the console the SQL queries sent to MySQL
DB_LOGGING=false

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# authentication
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# secret key used to sign/verify JWT tokens—must be changed
# mandatory in production (a long random string, never committed).
JWT_SECRET=change-moi-en-une-longue-chaine-aleatoire
# validity period of a JWT token, in seconds (7200 s = 2 h). The cookie
# that carries the token has the same lifetime.
JWT_EXPIRES_IN_SECONDS=7200
# Set to true in production (site served as HTTPS): the
# will then never be sent over an unencrypted connection.
COOKIE_SECURE=false

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# bot protection
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# login: number of failed attempts (incorrect CAPTCHA or password) allowed for
# the same login from the same IP address, before this combination is blocked...
LOGIN_MAX_ECHECS=5
# ... during this period (an address IP is also blocked if it accumulates
# 5 times as many failed attempts, across all logins)
LOGIN_BLOCAGE_MINUTES=15
# customer account creation: maximum number of accounts created per hour
# from the same IP address. In a classroom, all workstations log out
# from the same IP address: increase if necessary.
INSCRIPTION_MAX_PAR_HEURE=10

# MODE TEST from the CAPTCHA: if this variable has a value, that value is
# accepted as the answer to the N'IMPORTE QUEL CAPTCHA. Useful for querying
# the API using curl (you can’t “read” the image in a console).
# Leave VIDE in production.
CAPTCHA_TEST=

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# production
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# compiled web client directory, served by this server (default: client/)
# DOSSIER_CLIENT=client
# set to true if the server is behind a proxy (nginx...)
TRUST_PROXY=false
  • line 8: the server listens on port 8080;
  • lines 12–16: the connection to [MySQL]. With [Laragon], the user [root] has no password: the default values are fine;
  • line 25: the secret key that signs the authentication tokens;
  • lines 38–45: anti-bot measures (lockout after multiple failed login attempts, number of accounts created per hour);
  • Line 51: Captcha test mode. The login page requires you to type the characters from an image, which is impossible from a console. If this variable has a value, that value is accepted as the answer to any CAPTCHA, similar to the “test keys” that [Google] provides for its [reCAPTCHA]. For the tests with [curl] in this chapter, enter [CAPTCHA_TEST=test]. The automated tests that generated the screenshots for this course also use this value. Leave it as VIDE in production;
  • lines 57–59: two settings for production (see the “Deployment” chapter).
  1. Launch.
npm run start:dev

The console displays (excerpt):

[Nest] LOG [NestFactory] Starting Nest application...
[Nest] LOG [RoutesResolver] AgendaController {/api/agenda}:
[Nest] LOG [RouterExplorer] Mapped {/api/agenda, GET} route
[Nest] LOG [RoutesResolver] RendezVousController {/api/rendez-vous}:
...
[Nest] WARN [RdvMedecins] MODE TEST du captcha actif (CAPTCHA_TEST dans .env) : à ne jamais utiliser en production
[Nest] LOG [NestApplication] Nest application successfully started
[Nest] LOG [RdvMedecins] serveur JSON démarré : http://localhost:8080/api

If the database is inaccessible ([MySQL] server stopped, incorrect password), the server stops immediately with a connection error message.

docs.title: 8.3. Response Format
docs.text:
All URLs begin with [/api]. A successful request receives a 2xx status code and, in its body, the requested data in the format JSON. A rejected request receives a 4xx or 5xx code and, in the body, TOUJOURS, which has the same format:

{
  "statusCode": 400,
  "cle": "ERRORS.INVALID_FORM",
  "params": { "min": "6" },
  "champs": { "nom": "ERRORS.LASTNAME_REQUIRED", "password": "ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT" }
}
  • [statusCode]: the code HTTP, repeated in the body;
  • [cle]: the message translation key. The server never returns text to be displayed: it no longer knows the user’s language. It is the client that translates the key using its dictionaries (see Example 21);
  • [params] (optional): the message parameters ([Au moins {min} caractères], [Réessayez dans {minutes} minute(s)]);
  • [champs] (optional): for a rejected form, the error for each field.

Codes used:

CodeMeaningExamples of keys400Invalid request[ERRORS.INVALID_FORM] (+ fields), [ERRORS.INVALID_DATE], [ERRORS.WRONG_CAPTCHA], [ERRORS.CHOOSE_PATIENT], [ERRORS.WRONG_CURRENT_PASSWORD], [ERRORS.BAD_REQUEST]...401not authenticated[ERRORS.AUTH_REQUIRED] (no token), [ERRORS.SESSION_EXPIRED] (invalid or expired token), [LOGIN.ERROR]403Access Denied[ERRORS.FORBIDDEN] (insufficient role), [ERRORS.CAPTCHA_BEFORE_ACCOUNT] (no pass)404Not found[ERRORS.NOT_FOUND], [ERRORS.DOCTOR_NOT_FOUND], [ERRORS.APPOINTMENT_NOT_FOUND]...409Business rule violation[ERRORS.PAST_DATE], [ERRORS.SLOT_ALREADY_BOOKED], [ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN], [ERRORS.CONCURRENT_UPDATE]...415POST, which is not in JSON[ERRORS.JSON_REQUIRED]429Too many attempts[ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS], [ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ACCOUNTS] (+ params.minutes)500server error[ERRORS.SERVER_ERROR]

docs.title: 8.4. Authentication
docs.text:
The client authenticates using [POST /api/auth/login], with a username, password, and CAPTCHA response. In return, the server sends, in the [Set-Cookie] header of its response, a cookie containing a signed token JWT:

Set-Cookie: rdvmedecins_jwt=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs...; Max-Age=7200; Path=/api; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict

The client must then include this cookie, in the [Cookie] header, with every request to [/api]: this is how the server knows who is making the request.

This server was designed for web clients, and its design choices are driven by the risks specific to web browsers:

  • [HttpOnly]: The page’s code ([JavaScript]) cannot read this cookie (PAS). A malicious script injected into the page would therefore be unable to steal the token. Consequence for the client: it cannot determine on its own whether it is logged in. It asks the server ([GET /api/auth/moi]);
  • [Path=/api]: The cookie is only included in requests to API;
  • [SameSite=Strict]: The browser attaches the cookie only to requests sent to a page on this site. A malicious page on another site cannot cause the browser to act on the user’s behalf (a so-called CSRF attack);
  • [Max-Age=7200]: It expires after two hours, at the same time the token expires.

A second safeguard against CSRF attacks: the server rejects (415) any POST request whose body is not in JSON. A compromised HTML form on another site cannot send JSON.

What about a mobile app? There is no browser: no one stores the cookie or sends it back on its own. The app will take on this role by reading the [Set-Cookie] header in the responses and writing the [Cookie] header in the requests (example 23). The attributes [HttpOnly] and [SameSite] apply only to browsers: they have no effect on the app, just as [curl] does not. The same [Flutter] application, when compiled for the web, will, however, function as browsers do: the cookie is managed by the browser, provided that the application and API share the same origin (see Example 22 and the “Deployment” chapter).

docs.title: 8.5. The API
docs.text:
MethodAddressRolesSent/Response BodyGET[/api/captcha]publicResponse: [{ id, svg }]POST[/api/auth/login]public[{ login, password, captchaId, captcha }]; response: [{ login, nom, role }] + cookiePOST[/api/auth/logout]public[{}] ; deletes the cookieGET[/api/auth/moi]logged inresponse: [{ login, nom, role }]GET[/api/agenda?idMedecin=&jour=]allAnswer: the calendar (excluding idMedecin: for a DOCTOR, his own)POST[/api/rendez-vous]all[{ jour, idCreneau, idClient }] (idClient ignored for a USER); 201DELETE[/api/rendez-vous/:id]allA USER cancels only its ownGET[/api/medecins]allthe list (with login for ADMIN)GET[/api/clients]ADMIN, DOCTORthe list (with login for ADMIN)GET[/api/medecins/:id], [/api/clients/:id]ADMINa recordPOST[/api/medecins], [/api/clients]ADMIN[{ titre, prenom, nom, login?, password? }]; 201PUT[/api/medecins/:id], [/api/clients/:id]ADMIN[{ titre, prenom, nom, login?, password?, version }]DELETE[/api/medecins/:id], [/api/clients/:id]ADMINAnswer: [{}]POST[/api/inscription/acces]public[{ captchaId, captcha }]; issues a token (cookie)GET[/api/inscription/acces]publicresponse: [{ valide }]POST[/api/inscription]public + pass[{ titre, prenom, nom, login, password, confirmation }]; 201GET[/api/mon-espace]USERresponse: [{ patient, rendezVous }]GET[/api/mon-compte]USERResponse: [{ titre, prenom, nom, login, version }]PUT[/api/mon-compte]USER[{ titre, prenom, nom, login, password?, confirmation?, motDePasseActuel, version }]DELETE[/api/mon-compte]USER[{ motDePasseActuel }]; deletes the account and its appointments

A calendar entry ([GET /api/agenda]) describes a time slot (ET) and what the logged-in user is authorized to do with it:

{ "id": 3, "hdebut": 8, "mdebut": 40, "hfin": 9, "mfin": 0,
  "libre": false,
  "patient": { "titre": "Mme", "prenom": "Alice", "nom": "DURAND" },
  "moi": false, "reservable": false, "idRv": 2 }
  • [libre]: Is the time slot available on that day?
  • [patient]: the patient for the appointment. For a logged-in patient, this is equal to [null], except for SON (appointment): the names of other patients are never sent;
  • [moi]: This is the logged-in patient’s appointment;
  • [reservable]: Can the user book this time slot (available, not in the past, and, for a patient, no upcoming appointments)?
  • [idRv]: filled in if the user can cancel this appointment.

The server handles DÉCIDE; the client displays it. And even if a client were to cheat (by displaying a “Book” button when it shouldn’t), the server would double-check everything at the time of booking.

docs.title: 8.6. Query the API using curl
docs.text:
The [curl] folder on the server contains the JSON request bodies from this chapter, with one file per request. For example, [curl/login-admin.json]:

{ "login": "admin", "password": "admin", "captchaId": "-", "captcha": "test" }

Commands are entered in a console opened on the [rdvmedecins-nestjs-json] directory. Some options for [curl]:

  • [-i]: also display the response headers; [-s]: without a progress bar;
  • [--json @fichier]: send the contents of the file in POST, with the header [Content-Type: application/json] (curl 7.82 and later; with an older version, use [-H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @fichier]);
  • [-X PUT], [-X DELETE]: the HTTP method;
  • [-c cookies.txt]: save the received cookies to this file; [-b cookies.txt]: send them back. This is how [curl] “stays logged in” from one command to the next, just as a browser would.

Under [PowerShell], you must enter [curl.exe] and not [curl] (which refers to a different command there). The somewhat lengthy responses for JSON have been formatted for this document, and the headers for [Date], [ETag], [Connection], and [Keep-Alive] have been removed.

docs.title: 8.6.1. Login
docs.text:
First, the CAPTCHA (the image is cropped):

$ curl -i http://localhost:8080/api/captcha
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Cache-Control: no-store
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 11397

{"id": "9931064f-dcc3-45f7-a35c-3057d208a1d4", "svg": "<svg xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\" width=\"150..."}

Without a token, a protected URL returns a 401 response:

$ curl -i http://localhost:8080/api/doctors
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 47

{"statusCode": 401, "cle": "ERRORS.AUTH_REQUIRED"}

An incorrect CAPTCHA, followed by an incorrect password:

$ curl -i --json @curl/login-mauvais-captcha.json http://localhost:8080/api/auth/login
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 91

{"statusCode": 400, "cle": "ERRORS.WRONG_CAPTCHA", "champs": {"captcha": "ERRORS.WRONG_CAPTCHA"}}

$ curl -i --json @curl/login-mauvais-mdp.json http://localhost:8080/api/auth/login
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 38

{"statusCode": 401, "cle": "LOGIN.ERROR"}

A successful login sets the cookie, which [curl] stores in [cookies.txt]:

$ curl -i -c cookies.txt --json @curl/login-admin.json http://localhost:8080/api/auth/login
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Set-Cookie: rdvmedecins_jwt=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs...; Max-Age=7200; Path=/api; Expires=Mon, 28 Sep 2026 12:49:12 GMT; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 55

{"login": "admin", "nom": "Administrateur", "role": "ADMIN"}

With this cookie, the server knows who we are:

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt http://localhost:8080/api/auth/me
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 55

{"login": "admin", "nom": "Administrateur", "role": "ADMIN"}

A forged (or expired) token results in an expired session, and the server instructs the browser to delete the cookie:

$ curl -i -b "rdvmedecins_jwt=abc.def.ghi" http://localhost:8080/api/auth/me
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Set-Cookie: rdvmedecins_jwt=; Path=/api; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 49

{"statusCode": 401, "cle": "ERRORS.SESSION_EXPIRED"}

docs.title: 8.6.2. Doctors, clients, calendar
docs.text:
The list of doctors, as seen by ADMIN (with logins):

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt http://localhost:8080/api/doctors
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 258

[
  {"id": 3, "version": 0, "titre": "Melle", "prenom": "Sophie", "nom": "DUPONT", "login": "dupont"},
  {"id": 1, "version": 0, "titre": "Mme", "prenom": "Marie", "nom": "PELISSIER", "login": "pelissier"},
  {"id": 2, "version": 0, "titre": "Mr", "prenom": "Paul", "nom": "TATOU", "login": "tatou"}
]

Dr. PELISSIER’s schedule for January 15, 2030:

$ curl -s -b cookies.txt "http://localhost:8080/api/agenda?idMedecin=1&jour=2030-01-15"
{
  "medecin": {"id": 1, "version": 0, "titre": "Mme", "prenom": "Marie", "nom": "PELISSIER"},
  "jour": "2030-01-15",
  "creneaux": [
    {"id": 1, "hdebut": 8, "mdebut": 0, "hfin": 8, "mfin": 20, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 2, "hdebut": 8, "mdebut": 20, "hfin": 8, "mfin": 40, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 3, "hdebut": 8, "mdebut": 40, "hfin": 9, "mfin": 0, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 4, "hdebut": 9, "mdebut": 0, "hfin": 9, "mfin": 20, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 5, "hdebut": 9, "mdebut": 20, "hfin": 9, "mfin": 40, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 6, "hdebut": 9, "mdebut": 40, "hfin": 10, "mfin": 0, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 7, "hdebut": 10, "mdebut": 0, "hfin": 10, "mfin": 20, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 8, "hdebut": 10, "mdebut": 20, "hfin": 10, "mfin": 40, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 9, "hdebut": 10, "mdebut": 40, "hfin": 11, "mfin": 0, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 10, "hdebut": 11, "mdebut": 0, "hfin": 11, "mfin": 20, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 11, "hdebut": 11, "mdebut": 20, "hfin": 11, "mfin": 40, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 12, "hdebut": 11, "mdebut": 40, "hfin": 12, "mfin": 0, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null}
  ],
  "info": null
}

A date that does not exist:

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt "http://localhost:8080/api/agenda?idMedecin=1&jour=2030-02-30"
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 46

{"statusCode": 400, "cle": "ERRORS.INVALID_DATE"}

docs.title: 8.6.3. Appointments
docs.text:
ADMIN reserves slot 3 for patient No. 2 (Alice DURAND). The body of the request:

{ "jour": "2030-01-15", "idCreneau": 3, "idClient": 2 }

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt --json @curl/rv-admin.json http://localhost:8080/api/appointments
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 55

{"id": 2, "jour": "2030-01-15", "idCreneau": 3, "idClient": 2}

The calendar now displays this appointment, along with the patient’s name and instructions on how to cancel it ([idRv]):

$ curl -s -b cookies.txt "http://localhost:8080/api/agenda?idMedecin=1&jour=2030-01-15"
{
  "medecin": {"id": 1, "version": 0, "titre": "Mme", "prenom": "Marie", "nom": "PELISSIER"},
  "jour": "2030-01-15",
  "creneaux": [
    {"id": 1, "hdebut": 8, "mdebut": 0, "hfin": 8, "mfin": 20, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 2, "hdebut": 8, "mdebut": 20, "hfin": 8, "mfin": 40, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 3, "hdebut": 8, "mdebut": 40, "hfin": 9, "mfin": 0, "libre": false, "patient": {"titre": "Mme", "prenom": "Alice", "nom": "DURAND"}, "moi": false, "reservable": false, "idRv": 2},
    {"id": 4, "hdebut": 9, "mdebut": 0, "hfin": 9, "mfin": 20, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 5, "hdebut": 9, "mdebut": 20, "hfin": 9, "mfin": 40, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 6, "hdebut": 9, "mdebut": 40, "hfin": 10, "mfin": 0, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 7, "hdebut": 10, "mdebut": 0, "hfin": 10, "mfin": 20, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 8, "hdebut": 10, "mdebut": 20, "hfin": 10, "mfin": 40, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 9, "hdebut": 10, "mdebut": 40, "hfin": 11, "mfin": 0, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 10, "hdebut": 11, "mdebut": 0, "hfin": 11, "mfin": 20, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 11, "hdebut": 11, "mdebut": 20, "hfin": 11, "mfin": 40, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 12, "hdebut": 11, "mdebut": 40, "hfin": 12, "mfin": 0, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null}
  ],
  "info": null
}

Try again: the patient already has an upcoming appointment. An appointment in the past is also rejected:

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt --json @curl/rv-admin.json http://localhost:8080/api/appointments
HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 66

{"statusCode": 409, "cle": "ERRORS.PATIENT_HAS_UPCOMING_APPOINTMENT"}

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt --json @curl/rv-passe.json http://localhost:8080/api/appointments
HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 43

{"statusCode": 409, "cle": "ERRORS.PAST_DATE"}

A standard HTML form (simulated here by [-d], which sends [application/x-www-form-urlencoded]) is rejected:

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt -d "jour=2030-01-15&idCreneau=4&idClient=2" http://localhost:8080/api/appointments
HTTP/1.1 415 Unsupported Media Type
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 47

{"statusCode": 415, "cle": "ERRORS.JSON_REQUIRED"}

docs.title: 8.6.4. A patient’s perspective
docs.text:
You log out, then log in as [martin]:

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt -c cookies.txt --json @curl/vide.json http://localhost:8080/api/auth/logout
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Set-Cookie: rdvmedecins_jwt=; Path=/api; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 2

{}

$ curl -s -c cookies-martin.txt --json @curl/login-martin.json http://localhost:8080/api/auth/login
{"login": "martin", "nom": "Jean MARTIN", "role": "USER"}

The same schedule, as seen by a patient: slot 3 is occupied (["libre": false]), but ["patient"] is equivalent to [null]: Alice’s name, DURAND, was not sent:

$ curl -s -b cookies-martin.txt "http://localhost:8080/api/agenda?idMedecin=1&jour=2030-01-15"
{
  "medecin": {"id": 1, "version": 0, "titre": "Mme", "prenom": "Marie", "nom": "PELISSIER"},
  "jour": "2030-01-15",
  "creneaux": [
    {"id": 1, "hdebut": 8, "mdebut": 0, "hfin": 8, "mfin": 20, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 2, "hdebut": 8, "mdebut": 20, "hfin": 8, "mfin": 40, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 3, "hdebut": 8, "mdebut": 40, "hfin": 9, "mfin": 0, "libre": false, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": false, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 4, "hdebut": 9, "mdebut": 0, "hfin": 9, "mfin": 20, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 5, "hdebut": 9, "mdebut": 20, "hfin": 9, "mfin": 40, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 6, "hdebut": 9, "mdebut": 40, "hfin": 10, "mfin": 0, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 7, "hdebut": 10, "mdebut": 0, "hfin": 10, "mfin": 20, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 8, "hdebut": 10, "mdebut": 20, "hfin": 10, "mfin": 40, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 9, "hdebut": 10, "mdebut": 40, "hfin": 11, "mfin": 0, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 10, "hdebut": 11, "mdebut": 0, "hfin": 11, "mfin": 20, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 11, "hdebut": 11, "mdebut": 20, "hfin": 11, "mfin": 40, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 12, "hdebut": 11, "mdebut": 40, "hfin": 12, "mfin": 0, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null}
  ],
  "info": null
}

A patient does not have access to the client list:

$ curl -i -b cookies-martin.txt http://localhost:8080/api/clients
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 43

{"statusCode": 403, "cle": "ERRORS.FORBIDDEN"}

They are making a reservation for themselves (the body does not contain [idClient]), once, not twice:

{ "jour": "2030-01-15", "idCreneau": 5 }

$ curl -i -b cookies-martin.txt --json @curl/rv-martin.json http://localhost:8080/api/appointments
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 55

{"id": 3, "jour": "2030-01-15", "idCreneau": 5, "idClient": 1}

$ curl -i -b cookies-martin.txt --json @curl/rv-martin-2.json http://localhost:8080/api/appointments
HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 53

{"statusCode": 409, "cle": "AGENDA.ALREADY_BOOKED_INFO"}

His space:

$ curl -s -b cookies-martin.txt http://localhost:8080/api/my-space
{
  "patient": {"titre": "Mr", "prenom": "Jean", "nom": "MARTIN"},
  "rendezVous": [
    {
      "id": 3,
      "jour": "2030-01-15",
      "creneau": {"id": 5, "hdebut": 9, "mdebut": 20, "hfin": 9, "mfin": 40},
      "medecin": {"id": 1, "version": 0, "titre": "Mme", "prenom": "Marie", "nom": "PELISSIER"}
    }
  ]
}

He cannot cancel another patient’s appointment. The server responds with “not found,” just as it would for an appointment that does not exist: it reveals nothing about other patients’ appointments:

$ curl -i -b cookies-martin.txt -X DELETE http://localhost:8080/api/appointments/2
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 55

{"statusCode": 404, "cle": "ERRORS.APPOINTMENT_NOT_FOUND"}

His own, yes:

$ curl -i -b cookies-martin.txt -X DELETE http://localhost:8080/api/appointments/3
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 2

{}

docs.title: 8.6.5. A doctor’s perspective
docs.text:
Without [idMedecin], a logged-in doctor receives the SON calendar, with all the names:

$ curl -s -b cookies-pelissier.txt "http://localhost:8080/api/agenda?jour=2030-01-15"
{
  "medecin": {"id": 1, "version": 0, "titre": "Mme", "prenom": "Marie", "nom": "PELISSIER"},
  "jour": "2030-01-15",
  "creneaux": [
    {"id": 1, "hdebut": 8, "mdebut": 0, "hfin": 8, "mfin": 20, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 2, "hdebut": 8, "mdebut": 20, "hfin": 8, "mfin": 40, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 3, "hdebut": 8, "mdebut": 40, "hfin": 9, "mfin": 0, "libre": false, "patient": {"titre": "Mme", "prenom": "Alice", "nom": "DURAND"}, "moi": false, "reservable": false, "idRv": 2},
    {"id": 4, "hdebut": 9, "mdebut": 0, "hfin": 9, "mfin": 20, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 5, "hdebut": 9, "mdebut": 20, "hfin": 9, "mfin": 40, "libre": false, "patient": {"titre": "Mr", "prenom": "Jean", "nom": "MARTIN"}, "moi": false, "reservable": false, "idRv": 3},
    {"id": 6, "hdebut": 9, "mdebut": 40, "hfin": 10, "mfin": 0, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 7, "hdebut": 10, "mdebut": 0, "hfin": 10, "mfin": 20, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 8, "hdebut": 10, "mdebut": 20, "hfin": 10, "mfin": 40, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 9, "hdebut": 10, "mdebut": 40, "hfin": 11, "mfin": 0, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 10, "hdebut": 11, "mdebut": 0, "hfin": 11, "mfin": 20, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 11, "hdebut": 11, "mdebut": 20, "hfin": 11, "mfin": 40, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 12, "hdebut": 11, "mdebut": 40, "hfin": 12, "mfin": 0, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null}
  ],
  "info": null
}

It does not manage doctors:

$ curl -i -b cookies-pelissier.txt --json @curl/medecin-ajout.json http://localhost:8080/api/doctors
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 43

{"statusCode": 403, "cle": "ERRORS.FORBIDDEN"}

docs.title: 8.6.6. Managing doctors and clients (ADMIN)
docs.text:
An addition. If the username is missing, the default is the name in lowercase; the password is the username:

{ "titre": "Mme", "prenom": "Claire", "nom": "LEROY" }

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt --json @curl/medecin-ajout.json http://localhost:8080/api/doctors
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 82

{"id": 4, "version": 1, "titre": "Mme", "prenom": "Claire", "nom": "LEROY", "login": "leroy"}

Invalid body: the response lists the error for each field:

{ "titre": "Dr", "prenom": "", "nom": "UN-NOM-BIEN-TROP-LONG-POUR-LA-BASE", "login": "Claire L" }

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt --json @curl/medecin-invalide.json http://localhost:8080/api/doctors
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 210

{
  "statusCode": 400,
  "cle": "ERRORS.INVALID_FORM",
  "params": {"min": "6"},
  "champs": {"login": "ERRORS.INVALID_LOGIN", "titre": "ERRORS.INVALID_TITLE", "prenom": "ERRORS.FIRSTNAME_REQUIRED", "nom": "ERRORS.LASTNAME_TOO_LONG"}
}

A homonym: both affected fields are flagged:

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt --json @curl/medecin-doublon.json http://localhost:8080/api/doctors
HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 143

{"statusCode": 409, "cle": "ERRORS.DOCTOR_ALREADY_EXISTS", "champs": {"prenom": "ERRORS.DOCTOR_ALREADY_EXISTS", "nom": "ERRORS.DOCTOR_ALREADY_EXISTS"}}

A modification. The [version] is the one read from the record (here, 1):

{ "titre": "Mme", "prenom": "Claire", "nom": "LEROY-MARTIN", "version": 1 }

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt -X PUT --json @curl/medecin-modif.json http://localhost:8080/api/doctors/4
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 89

{"id": 4, "version": 2, "titre": "Mme", "prenom": "Claire", "nom": "LEROY-MARTIN", "login": "leroy"}

The record is now at version 2. Resubmitting the same change (with version 1) would overwrite a record that has since been modified by someone else: the optimistic lock prevents this:

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt -X PUT --json @curl/medecin-modif.json http://localhost:8080/api/medecins/4
HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 51

{"statusCode": 409, "cle": "ERRORS.CONCURRENT_UPDATE"}

A doctor with appointments cannot be deleted; the others can:

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt -X DELETE http://localhost:8080/api/doctors/1
HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 57

{"statusCode": 409, "cle": "ERRORS.DOCTOR_HAS_APPOINTMENTS"}

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt -X DELETE http://localhost:8080/api/doctors/4
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 2

{}

docs.title: 8.6.7. Creating an account
docs.text:
Without a pass, it’s impossible:

$ curl -i --json @curl/inscription.json http://localhost:8080/api/registration
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 56

{"statusCode": 403, "cle": "ERRORS.CAPTCHA_BEFORE_ACCOUNT"}

First, you solve a CAPTCHA; the server issues a token, valid for 15 minutes, in a cookie:

$ curl -i -c cookies-inscription.txt --json @curl/captcha-test.json http://localhost:8080/api/registration/access
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Set-Cookie: rdvmedecins_inscription=1c3352aa-26ba-4f85-9f61-ed2c6a731d84; Max-Age=900; Path=/api/inscription; Expires=Mon, 28 Sep 2026 11:04:12 GMT; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 2

{}

$ curl -s -b cookies-inscription.txt http://localhost:8080/api/registration/access
{"valide": true}

The password confirmation must be identical:

$ curl -i -b cookies-inscription.txt --json @curl/inscription-confirmation.json http://localhost:8080/api/registration
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 98

{"statusCode": 400, "cle": "ERRORS.INVALID_FORM", "champs": {"confirmation": "ERRORS.PASSWORDS_DIFFER"}}

{ "titre": "Mme", "prenom": "Julie", "nom": "BERNARD", "login": "jbernard", "password": "secret1", "confirmation": "secret1" }

$ curl -i -b cookies-inscription.txt -c cookies-inscription.txt --json @curl/inscription.json http://localhost:8080/api/registration
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
Set-Cookie: rdvmedecins_inscription=; Path=/api/inscription; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 20

{"login": "jbernard"}

The passcode has been used: it cannot be used to create a second account:

$ curl -i -b cookies-inscription.txt --json @curl/inscription.json http://localhost:8080/api/registration
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 56

{"statusCode": 403, "cle": "ERRORS.CAPTCHA_BEFORE_ACCOUNT"}

docs.title: 8.6.8. Manage Your Account
docs.text:
The new patient logs in and reads her medical record:

$ curl -s -b cookies-jbernard.txt http://localhost:8080/api/my-account
{"titre": "Mme", "prenom": "Julie", "nom": "BERNARD", "login": "jbernard", "version": 1}

Making a change requires the current password. The server issues a new token, which contains the new name:

{ "titre": "Mme", "prenom": "Julie", "nom": "BERNARD-DUVAL", "login": "jbernard", "motDePasseActuel": "secret1", "version": 1 }

$ curl -i -b cookies-jbernard.txt -c cookies-jbernard.txt -X PUT --json @curl/mon-compte.json http://localhost:8080/api/my-account
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Set-Cookie: rdvmedecins_jwt=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs...; Max-Age=7200; Path=/api; Expires=Mon, 28 Sep 2026 12:49:13 GMT; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 62

{"login": "jbernard", "nom": "Julie BERNARD-DUVAL", "role": "USER"}

Deleting the account also deletes the cookie:

$ curl -i -b cookies-jbernard.txt -c cookies-jbernard.txt -X DELETE --json @curl/mon-compte-suppression.json http://localhost:8080/api/my-account
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Set-Cookie: rdvmedecins_jwt=; Path=/api; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 2

{}

$ curl -i -b cookies-jbernard.txt http://localhost:8080/api/auth/me
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 47

{"statusCode": 401, "cle": "ERRORS.AUTH_REQUIRED"}

docs.title: 8.6.9. Some errors
docs.text:
An unknown route, a body that is not a valid JSON:

$ curl -i -b cookies-martin.txt http://localhost:8080/api/does-not-exist
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 43

{"statusCode": 404, "cle": "ERRORS.NOT_FOUND"}

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{pas du json" http://localhost:8080/api/appointment
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 45
