docs.title: 4. Widgets
docs.text: Writing your own widgets is at the heart of working with [Flutter]: a well-written screen is made up of small widgets, each with its own parameters, its [build], and, if necessary, its state. This chapter shows how they communicate with each other (parameters, functions), how they are assembled (composition), how they function (lifecycle), how they share data without passing it from one to another (inherited data), and how to reuse behavior.

docs.title: 4.1.1. Data Type
docs.text:
The parent and child share a class, defined in its own file:

// The data type is shared by the parent (PageMedecins) and the child (CarteMedecin)
class Medecin {
  final int id;
  final String titre;
  final String prenom;
  final String nom;
  final String specialite;
  final bool disponible;

  const Medecin({
    required this.id,
    required this.titre,
    required this.prenom,
    required this.nom,
    required this.specialite,
    required this.disponible,
  });

   // A copy where only the availability changes
  Medecin avecDisponibilite(bool d) =>
      Medecin(id: id, titre: titre, prenom: prenom, nom: nom, specialite: specialite, disponible: d);
}
  • lines 10–16: a constructor with named parameters, all of which are required: [Medecin(id: 1, titre: 'Mme', ...)]. Named parameters make the call readable, and their order does not matter;
  • lines 20–21: a copy where only the availability changes (the object itself never changes).

docs.title: 4.1.2. The child
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex10_widgets_parametres/carte_medecin.dart - a widget ENFANT
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// It receives its data from its parent via the PARAMÈTRES fields of its
// constructor, stored in final fields. Their type is verified during
// compilation stage: CarteMedecin (doctor: 42) would be rejected.
//    - required: the parent DOIT must provide this parameter;
//    - this.compact = false: an optional parameter with its default value.
//
// Golden rule: a widget does not inherit its parameters (they are final).
// Data flows from the parent to the child; to request a
// change, the child calls a function passed to it by the parent
// (see Example 11). When the parent changes its data, it RECONSTRUIT its
// children with new parameters.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

import 'medecin.dart';

// the map’s “style”: constants PRIVÉES in this file (the “_”).
// No other widgets can see them or be affected by them
const _couleurInitiales = Color(0xFF087EA4);
const _styleInitiales = TextStyle(color: Colors.white, fontWeight: FontWeight.bold);

class CarteMedecin extends StatelessWidget {
  final Medecin medecin;
  final int rang;
  final bool compact;

   // const: if all parameters are constant, the widget is also constant
   // (Flutter doesn’t even need to rebuild it)
  const CarteMedecin({super.key, required this.medecin, required this.rang, this.compact = false});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
     // a value calculated from the parameters
    final initiales = '${medecin.prenom[0]}${medecin.nom[0]}';

    return Card(
       // a green border for an available doctor
      shape: RoundedRectangleBorder(
        borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(12),
        side: medecin.disponible ? const BorderSide(color: Colors.green, width: 2) : BorderSide.none,
      ),
      child: Padding(
        padding: const EdgeInsets.all(12),
        child: Row(
          children: [
            CircleAvatar(
              backgroundColor: _couleurInitiales,
              child: Text(initiales, style: _styleInitiales),
            ),
            const SizedBox(width: 12),
             // Expanded: the text takes up the entire remaining width
            Expanded(
              child: Column(
                crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
                children: [
                  Text(
                     '$rang. ${medecin.titre} ${medecin.prenom} ${medecin.nom}',
                    style: Theme.of(context).textTheme.titleMedium,
                  ),
                  if (!compact) Text(medecin.specialite, style: const TextStyle(color: Colors.grey)),
                ],
              ),
            ),
          ],
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}
  • lines 23–24: the map’s “style”: constants private to this file (the underlined ones). No other file can see them or be affected by them. This is the equivalent, in [Flutter], of the “CSS modules” in [React]: there is no global stylesheet; a widget’s style is embedded in its code;
  • lines 27–29: the widget’s parameters, stored in [final] fields;
  • line 33: the constructor. [required this.medecin]: a required parameter, stored directly in the field; [this.compact = false]: an optional parameter, with its default value. The constructor is [const]: if all arguments are constant, the map is also constant;
  • line 38: a value calculated from the parameters;
  • lines 42–44: the card’s shape ([Card]): rounded corners and a green border if a doctor is available ([BorderSide.none] otherwise);
  • lines 50–52: a colored disc with the initials;
  • line 64: the specialty is only displayed in non-compact view.

Golden rule: a widget never modifies its own parameters (they are [final]; the compiler prohibits this, by the way). Data flows from the parent to the child; to request a change, the child calls a function passed to it by the parent (Example 11). When the parent changes its data, it reconstructs its children with new parameters.

docs.title: 4.1.3. The parent
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex10_widgets_parametres/main.dart - the PARENT widget
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// It imports the CarteMedecin widget and uses it as many times as
// as needed, just like any other Flutter widget: a widget is a piece
// of the user interface RÉUTILISABLE, with its own parameters, its `build()` method, and
// style. Writing your own widgets is at the heart of working with
// Flutter: a well-written screen is made up of small widgets.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

import 'carte_medecin.dart';
import 'medecin.dart';

void main() {
  runApp(
    MaterialApp(
      debugShowCheckedModeBanner: false,
      theme: ThemeData(colorSchemeSeed: Colors.indigo),
      home: const PageMedecins(),
    ),
  );
}

class PageMedecins extends StatefulWidget {
  const PageMedecins({super.key});

  @override
  State<PageMedecins> createState() => _PageMedecinsState();
}

class _PageMedecinsState extends State<PageMedecins> {
  List<Medecin> _medecins = const [
    Medecin(id: 1, titre: 'Mme', prenom: 'Marie', nom: 'PELISSIER', specialite: 'généraliste', disponible: true),
    Medecin(id: 2, titre: 'Mr', prenom: 'Paul', nom: 'TATOU', specialite: 'pédiatre', disponible: false),
    Medecin(id: 3, titre: 'Melle', prenom: 'Sophie', nom: 'DUPONT', specialite: 'généraliste', disponible: true),
  ];
  bool _compact = false;

   // the parent changes SES data: Flutter calls its build() method, which
   // rebuilds the children with their new parameters
  void _inverserDisponibilite() {
    setState(() {
      _medecins = [for (final m in _medecins) m.avecDisponibilite(!m.disponible)];
    });
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Scaffold(
      appBar: AppBar(title: const Text('Exemple 10 - les widgets et leurs paramètres')),
      body: ListView(
        padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16),
        children: [
          SwitchListTile(
            contentPadding: EdgeInsets.zero,
            title: const Text('affichage compact'),
            value: _compact,
            onChanged: (v) => setState(() => _compact = v),
          ),
          Align(
            alignment: Alignment.centerLeft,
            child: OutlinedButton(onPressed: _inverserDisponibilite, child: const Text('Inverser les disponibilités')),
          ),
          const SizedBox(height: 8),
          for (final (i, m) in _medecins.indexed)
             // Each card receives SES parameters
            CarteMedecin(key: ValueKey(m.id), medecin: m, rang: i + 1, compact: _compact),
          const SizedBox(height: 16),
          const Text(
            'La même carte, en version compacte, en fixant le paramètre :',
            style: TextStyle(color: Colors.grey),
          ),
          SizedBox(width: 260, child: CarteMedecin(medecin: _medecins[0], rang: 1, compact: true)),
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}
  • lines 34–39: the parent’s state: the list of doctors (a constant list, which will be replaced by another) and the compact display;
  • lines 43–45: the parent changes its SES data to a new list consisting of copies of the doctors. [Flutter] calls its [build], which rebuilds the cards with their new parameters;
  • line 69: one map per doctor, with SES parameters. The [CarteMedecin] widget is used exactly like a [Flutter] widget;
  • line 75: the same map, in a compact version, in a box 260 points wide.

Initially, then in compact view, availability is reversed:

A method that creates widgets (like [_ligne] from Example 02) or a real widget ([CarteMedecin])? The actual widget is almost always preferable: it has a name, its parameters are typed and documented, it can be reused elsewhere, and [Flutter] can avoid rebuilding it (if it is [const], or if its parameters haven’t changed).

docs.title: 4.2. Example 11: The child notifies its parent
docs.text: Data flows down through parameters; information flows back up through functions passed as parameters.

docs.title: 4.2.1. "Events" from the child
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex11_remonter_l_information/compteur.dart
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A child who PRÉVIENT their parent: the parent passes them FONCTIONS in
// parameters (by convention, their names begin with "on"), and the child
// calls them when something happens:
//      Counter(label: 'Coffees', max: 3, onIncremente: ..., onLimite: ...)
// These function types have predefined names in Flutter:
//    - ValueChanged<int>: a function that takes an int and returns nothing;
//    - VoidCallbac     k : a function with no parameters that returns nothing.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

class Compteur extends StatefulWidget {
  final String libelle;
  final int max;
  final ValueChanged<int> onIncremente; // with the new value
  final VoidCallback onLimite; // with no data

  const Compteur({
    super.key,
    required this.libelle,
    required this.max,
    required this.onIncremente,
    required this.onLimite,
  });

  @override
  State<Compteur> createState() => _CompteurState();
}

class _CompteurState extends State<Compteur> {
   // the state PROPRE for this counter: each counter has its own
  int _valeur = 0;

  void _plus() {
     // widget: within the State object, provides access to the widget’s parameters
    if (_valeur >= widget.max) {
      widget.onLimite();
      return;
    }
    setState(() => _valeur++);
     // on the parent PRÉVIENT, passing the new value to it
    widget.onIncremente(_valeur);
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Row(
      children: [
        SizedBox(width: 110, child: Text(widget.libelle)),
        OutlinedButton(onPressed: _plus, child: const Text('+1')),
        const SizedBox(width: 12),
        Chip(label: Text('$_valeur / ${widget.max}')),
      ],
    );
  }
}
  • lines 18–19: two parameters that are functions, which the counter will call. [ValueChanged<int>] is the type of a function that takes a [int] and returns nothing; [VoidCallback] is the type of a function with no parameters. By convention, their names begin with “on,” such as [onPressed] or [onChanged] for the widgets of [Flutter];
  • line 35: the state PROPRE for this counter: each [Compteur] has its own;
  • lines 37–45: within the [State] object, [widget] provides access to the widget’s settings: [widget.max], [widget.onLimite]... If the maximum is exceeded, the counter notifies its parent ([widget.onLimite()]); otherwise, it changes its state and then notifies its parent by transmitting the new value. Unlike [React], the state is updated immediately: [_valeur] already has its new value when it is transmitted.

docs.title: 4.2.2. A controlled widget
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex11_remonter_l_information/champ_texte.dart - a widget CONTRÔLÉ
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A "custom" form field (label + field + tooltip + character counter
// ) that is used as a controlled field:
//      ChampTexte(value: _nom, onChanged: (v) => setState(() => _nom = v), ...)
// The value belongs to PARENT, which passes it (the value) to it and which
// notifies of every keystroke (onChanged). The parent decides.
//
// A challenge specific to Flutter: a TextField stores its text in a
// controller, which must survive rebuilds. The widget therefore has a
// state (the controller)... which it must maintain at JOUR when the parent changes
// its value (the “Clear” button): this is the role of didUpdateWidget.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

class ChampTexte extends StatefulWidget {
  final String valeur;
  final ValueChanged<String> onChanged;
  final String libelle;
  final int max;
  final String aide;

  const ChampTexte({
    super.key,
    required this.valeur,
    required this.onChanged,
    required this.libelle,
    required this.max,
    this.aide = '',
  });

  @override
  State<ChampTexte> createState() => _ChampTexteState();
}

class _ChampTexteState extends State<ChampTexte> {
   // late: the field will be initialized later (in initState), before it is used
  late final TextEditingController _controleur;

  @override
  void initState() {
    super.initState();
    _controleur = TextEditingController(text: widget.valeur);
  }

   // called when PARENT rebuilds this widget with new parameters;
   // old: the previous widget, for comparison
  @override
  void didUpdateWidget(ChampTexte ancien) {
    super.didUpdateWidget(ancien);
    if (widget.valeur != _controleur.text) {
      _controleur.text = widget.valeur; // the parent changed the value itself
    }
  }

  @override
  void dispose() {
    _controleur.dispose();
    super.dispose();
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final plein = widget.valeur.length == widget.max;
    return TextField(
      controller: _controleur,
      maxLength: widget.max, // the field rejects excess characters
      decoration: InputDecoration(
        labelText: widget.libelle,
        helperText: widget.aide,
         // the border turns red when the field is full
        errorText: plein ? 'Longueur maximale atteinte' : null,
      ),
      onChanged: widget.onChanged, // the parent's function, passed as-is
    );
  }
}

A “custom” form field (label + field + tooltip + character counter) that functions as a controlled field: the value belongs to the parent, which passes it to the field ([valeur]) and notifies the parent of each keystroke ([onChanged]).

  • Line 40: [late]: This field will be initialized later (in [initState]), but before it is used. [Dart] checks it at runtime;
  • Lines 43–45: The controller starts with the parent’s value;
  • lines 51–54: This is the specific challenge with [Flutter]: a [TextField] stores its text in a controller, which must survive page rebuilds. The widget therefore has a state (the controller)... which it must keep up to date when the parent changes the value itself (Clear button). [didUpdateWidget] is called every time the parent rebuilds this widget with new parameters; it receives the old widget for comparison. If the parent’s value differs from the field’s text, it is copied over;
  • line 69: the field rejects excess characters and displays a counter (“12/20”);
  • line 72: a tooltip appears below the field;
  • line 74: the border turns red when the field is full;
  • line 76: the parent’s function, passed as-is to [TextField].

docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex11_remonter_l_information/main.dart - the parent listens to its children
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Data flows down (parameters); information flows back up via
// functions passed as parameters:
//    1. "events" from the child: onIncremente, onLimite;
//    2. a controlled widget: value + onChanged, such as a checkbox. The state
//       remains the property of the parent, which can modify it itself (Clear).
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

import 'champ_texte.dart';
import 'compteur.dart';

void main() {
  runApp(
    MaterialApp(
      debugShowCheckedModeBanner: false,
      theme: ThemeData(colorSchemeSeed: Colors.indigo),
      home: const PageParent(),

}

}

  int _total = 0;
  String _message = '';
  String _prenom = 'Marie';
  String _nom = 'PELISSIER';

   // the function called by a counter: it receives the value that the counter passes
  void _surIncremente(String libelle, int valeur) {
    setState(() {
      _total++;
      _message = '$libelle vaut maintenant $valeur';
    });
  }

  void _vider() {
    setState(() {
      _prenom = '';
      _nom = '';

  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final styleTitre = Theme.of(context).textTheme.titleSmall;
    return Scaffold(
      appBar: AppBar(title: const Text("Exemple 11 - l'enfant prévient son parent")),
      body: ListView(

        children: [
          Card(
            child: Padding(
              padding: const EdgeInsets.all(12),
              child: Column(
                crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
                children: [

                  Compteur(
                    libelle: 'Cafés',
                    max: 3,
                    onIncremente: (v) => _surIncremente('Cafés', v),
                    onLimite: () => setState(() => _message = 'Pas plus de 3 cafés !'),
                  ),

                  ),

  • lines 69–73: a counter and the functions it will call. [(v) => _surIncremente('Cafés', v)]: an anonymous function that adds its own argument (the label);
  • lines 94–99: a controlled field: its value, and the function that changes the parent’s state;
  • line 114: the parent’s data, which follows the entry;

docs.title: 4.3.1. A map
docs.text:
A widget’s parameters transmit data… but also content: a widget is a value like any other, which can be passed to another widget. [Flutter] uses it everywhere: the [child] of a [Padding], the [title] of a [AppBar], the [body] of a [Scaffold].

// =========================================================================
// lib/ex12_composition/carte.dart - a reusable GABARIT
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A widget’s parameters pass DONNÉES... but also
// CONTENU: a widget is just another value that can be passed to
// another widget, which places it wherever it wants. Flutter uses it everywhere:
// the child of a Padding, the title of a AppBar, the body of a Scaffold...
//    - child: by convention, the “main” content;
//    - header, footer: other locations (“slots”) provided by the
//      parent; the header has default content, the footer is optional.
// The card defines the frame (border, header, footer); the parent provides the
// content inside it.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

class Carte extends StatelessWidget {
  final Color? couleur; // "?": optional (default is null)
  final Widget entete;
  final Widget? pied;
  final Widget child;

  const Carte({super.key, this.couleur, this.entete = const Text('Sans titre'), this.pied, required this.child});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final fond = couleur ?? Colors.grey.shade300;
    return Card(
       // clipBehavior: The colored header follows the card’s rounded corners
      clipBehavior: Clip.antiAlias,
      shape: RoundedRectangleBorder(
        borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(8),
        side: BorderSide(color: fond),
      ),
      child: Column(
        crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.stretch,
        children: [
          Container(
            color: fond,
            padding: const EdgeInsets.all(10),
             // DefaultTextStyle: the style of TOUS applies to the header text,
             // regardless of the widget provided by the parent
            child: DefaultTextStyle.merge(
              style: TextStyle(color: couleur == null ? Colors.black : Colors.white, fontWeight: FontWeight.bold),
              child: entete,
            ),
          ),
          Padding(padding: const EdgeInsets.all(10), child: child),
           // no footer provided: no footer at all
          if (pied != null)
            Container(
              color: Colors.grey.shade100,
              padding: const EdgeInsets.all(8),
              child: DefaultTextStyle.merge(
                style: const TextStyle(color: Colors.grey, fontSize: 12),
                child: pied!,
              ),
            ),
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}
  • lines 18–21: Parameters: an optional color ([Color?]), and three slots for content: [entete], [pied] (optional), and [child], the main content;
  • line 23: the header has default content: a constant widget;
  • line 27: the header color: the one provided, or light gray;
  • line 30: the colored header is cropped to match the map’s rounded corners;
  • lines 43–45: [DefaultTextStyle] sets the style of TOUS for the text in its subtree, regardless of the widget provided by the parent: the header is bold, white on a colored background;
  • line 48: the main content, provided by the parent;
  • lines 50–58: no footer provided; no footer at all. [pied!]: in this branch, [pied] is not [null] (the compiler cannot infer this for a field, hence the [!]).

docs.title: 4.3.2. A generic array
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex12_composition/tableau.dart - a table GÉNÉRIQUE
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Array<T> is a generic widget: it displays rows of any
// type T. It knows how to iterate over the rows, but not how to display UNE
// row: the parent tells it how, by passing it a FONCTION,
// cells(row, index), which returns the cell widgets.
// This is the principle behind Flutter’s “builders” (ListView.builder,
// FutureBuilder...): the content provided by the parent uses data
// that belong to the child (the row, its index).
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

// the type of a function that creates the cells in a row
typedef ConstructeurCellules<T> = List<Widget> Function(T ligne, int index);

class Tableau<T> extends StatelessWidget {
  final List<T> lignes;
  final List<String> colonnes;
  final ConstructeurCellules<T> cellules;
  final Widget vide; // displayed when there are no rows

  const Tableau({
    super.key,
    required this.lignes,
    required this.colonnes,
    required this.cellules,
    this.vide = const Text('Aucune donnée.'),
  });

   // a cell: a small margin around its content
  static Widget _cellule(Widget contenu) => Padding(padding: const EdgeInsets.all(6), child: contenu);

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    if (lignes.isEmpty) {
      return Column(
        crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
        children: [
          Text(colonnes.join('   '), style: const TextStyle(fontWeight: FontWeight.bold)),
          const Divider(),
          DefaultTextStyle.merge(
            style: const TextStyle(color: Colors.grey),
            child: vide,
          ),
        ],
      );
    }
    return Table(
      defaultVerticalAlignment: TableCellVerticalAlignment.middle,
      border: TableBorder(horizontalInside: BorderSide(color: Colors.grey.shade300)),
      children: [
        TableRow(
          children: [for (final c in colonnes) _cellule(Text(c, style: const TextStyle(fontWeight: FontWeight.bold)))],
        ),
        for (final (i, ligne) in lignes.indexed)
           // the cells in the CETTE row, created by the parent function
          TableRow(children: [for (final c in cellules(ligne, i)) _cellule(c)]),
      ],
    );
  }
}
  • line 16: the type of a function that takes a row (of type [T]) and its index, and returns the widgets of its cells;
  • line 18: a generic widget: it displays rows of any type ([T]). It knows how to iterate through the rows, but not how to display a row (UNE); the parent tells it how by passing it the function [cellules]. This is the principle behind [Flutter] “builders” ([ListView.builder], [FutureBuilder]...): the content is provided by the parent, but it uses data that belongs to the child (the line, its index). [React] calls this a “render prop”;
  • line 33: a [static] method, which does not use any fields from the widget;
  • lines 37–45: no row: the column headers and the [vide] content, provided by the parent;
  • lines 50–59: the table: a row of headers, followed by one row per line, whose cells are generated by the parent’s function.

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

import 'carte.dart';
import 'tableau.dart';

// a slot: a named record (no need to write a class)
typedef Creneau = ({int id, String horaire, String? patient});

const creneaux = <Creneau>[
  (id: 1, horaire: '8:00 - 8:20', patient: null),
  (id: 2, horaire: '8:20 - 8:40', patient: 'Mme Alice DURAND'),
  (id: 3, horaire: '8:40 - 9:00', patient: null),
];

void main() {
  runApp(
    MaterialApp(
      debugShowCheckedModeBanner: false,
      theme: ThemeData(colorSchemeSeed: Colors.indigo),
      home: const PageComposition(),
    ),
  );
}

class PageComposition extends StatelessWidget {
  const PageComposition({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final libres = creneaux.where((c) => c.patient == null).length;

    return Scaffold(
      appBar: AppBar(title: const Text('Exemple 12 - la composition')),
      body: ListView(
        padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16),
        children: [
           // header and footer: widgets passed as parameters; child: the content
          Carte(
            couleur: Colors.indigo,
            entete: const Row(
              children: [
                Icon(Icons.event, color: Colors.white),
                SizedBox(width: 8),

                Expanded(child: Text('Agenda de Mme PELISSIER')),
              ],
            ),
            pied: Text('$libres créneau(x) libre(s)'),
             // Array<Slot>: T is inferred from the row type
            child: Tableau(
              lignes: creneaux,
              colonnes: const ['#', 'Time Slot', 'Status'],
               // the function that creates the cells for the UNE row;
               // c receives the row, i its index
              cellules: (c, i) => [
                Text('${i + 1}'),
                Text(c.horaire),
                c.patient != null
                    ? Chip(label: Text(c.patient!), visualDensity: VisualDensity.compact)
                    : Chip(
                        label: const Text('Libre'),
                        backgroundColor: Colors.green.shade100,
                        visualDensity: VisualDensity.compact,
                      ),
              ],
            ),
          ),
          const Carte(
            couleur: Colors.green,
            entete: Text('Une carte sans pied'),
            child: Text("Le pied n'est pas fourni : la carte ne l'affiche pas."),
          ),
           // no header provided: default content, “Untitled”
          Carte(
            child: Tableau<({int id, String nom})>(
              lignes: const [],
              colonnes: const ['Nom'],
              cellules: (p, _) => [Text(p.nom)],
              vide: const Text("Personne pour l'instant."),
            ),
          ),
        ],
      ),

  • line 11: a slot, in the form of a named record;
  • lines 42–52: a map: its color, a header (one line: an icon and text), a footer;
  • lines 54–66: its content: a table of slots. [T] is derived from the type [lignes]: it is a [Tableau<Creneau>]. The [cellules] function takes a time slot ([c]) and its rank ([i]), and returns three widgets;
  • lines 72–75: a card without a footer;
  • lines 79–83: a map without a footer (the default content, “Untitled”); its array is empty. [Tableau<({int id, String nom})>]: the type [T] is specified explicitly, because [lignes: const []] does not allow it to be inferred.

The card defines the framework (border, header, footer); the parent provides the content inside it. This is how the [Flutter] widgets themselves are built: [Scaffold] defines the structure of a screen and receives the top bar, the body, and the floating button.

docs.title: 4.4. Example 13: The Lifecycle of a Widget
4.4.1. A clock
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex13_cycle_de_vie/horloge.dart - a widget that starts and stops
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The lifecycle of a StatefulWidget State object:
//    1. initState(             ) : It has just been created; the widget will
//                                  appear. The necessary processes are started;
//    2. didChangeDependencies( ) : immediately afterward, and then every time the
//                                  inherited data it reads changes (see Example 14);
//    3. build(                 ) : as many times as necessary;
//    4. didUpdateWidget (old)   : the parent has rebuilt it with new
//                                  parameters;
//    5. dispose(               ) : the widget disappears permanently. We
//                                  what was started.
// A clock starts a timer (Timer.periodic) when it appears...
// and must stop it when it disappears: otherwise, the
// timer would continue to run for no reason, and would call setState()
// on a dead object (an error).
// =========================================================================

import 'dart:async';

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

String heureCourante() => DateTime.now().toString().substring(11, 19); // "12:05:09"

class Horloge extends StatefulWidget {
  final ValueChanged<String> onJournal;
  final Color couleur;

  const Horloge({super.key, required this.onJournal, this.couleur = Colors.indigo});

  @override
  State<Horloge> createState() => _HorlogeState();
}

class _HorlogeState extends State<Horloge> {
  String _heure = heureCourante();
   // late: initialized in initState
  late final Timer _minuterie;

   // notify the parent... APRÈS screen construction in progress: we do not
   // modify the state of a widget (the parent) while it is being built
  void _journaliser(String message) {
    WidgetsBinding.instance.addPostFrameCallback((_) => widget.onJournal(message));
  }

  @override
  void initState() {
    super.initState(); // always first
    _journaliser('Horloge : initState - démarrage de la minuterie');
    _minuterie = Timer.periodic(const Duration(seconds: 1), (_) {
      setState(() => _heure = heureCourante());
    });
  }

  @override
  void didUpdateWidget(Horloge ancien) {
    super.didUpdateWidget(ancien);
    if (ancien.couleur != widget.couleur) {
      _journaliser('Horloge : didUpdateWidget - nouvelle couleur');
    }
  }

  @override
  void dispose() {
    _minuterie.cancel(); // NETTOYAGE
    _journaliser('Horloge : dispose - minuterie arrêtée');
    super.dispose(); // always last
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Text(
      _heure,
      style: TextStyle(fontSize: 40, fontFamily: 'RobotoMono', color: widget.couleur),
    );
  }
}

The lifecycle of the [State] object within a [StatefulWidget]:

MethodWhen?initState()The object has just been created; the widget will appear. This is where you start whatever needs to be started (timer, subscription, etc.)didChangeDependencies()Immediately after initState, then whenever any inherited data it reads changes (see Example 14)build()as many times as necessarydidUpdateWidget(old)the parent has rebuilt it with new parametersdispose()the widget disappears permanently. Anything that was started there is stopped
  • lines 37–39: the state: the displayed time, and a timer ([Timer], from the [dart:async] library);
  • lines 43–44: the clock notifies its parent of each stage of its lifecycle. But it does so during [initState] or [dispose]—that is, while [Flutter] is building the screen: the parent cannot modify its state at that moment ([setState] would cause an error). [addPostFrameCallback] defers the call until after the current image has finished rendering;
  • lines 48–52: [super.initState()] first, always. Then a periodic timer is started: its function is called every second and updates the time;
  • lines 57–60: The parent has redrawn the clock with a different color: this is noted;
  • lines 65–68: cleanup: we stop the timer. Otherwise, it would continue to run needlessly and call [setState] on a dead object, resulting in an error (“setState() called after dispose()”) and a memory leak. [super.dispose()] always comes last.

docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex13_cycle_de_vie/main.dart
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
//    - if (_avecHorloge) Clock(...): checking/unchecking the box causes
//      the widget to appear / disappear (initState, then arrange, see
//      horloge.dart); changing its color rebuilds it (didUpdateWidget);
//    - autofocus: an input field that gains focus as soon as it appears
//      (the phone's keyboard opens);
//    - the app title updates as you type (Title widget);
//    - AppLifecycleListener: the life of the APPLICATION itself. On a
//      phone, it goes into the background (when you open another app,
//      the screen turns off), then comes back: you can interact with it (save,
//      stop a timer...).
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

import 'horloge.dart';

void main() {
  runApp(
    MaterialApp(
      debugShowCheckedModeBanner: false,
      theme: ThemeData(colorSchemeSeed: Colors.indigo),
      home: const PageCycleDeVie(),
    ),
  );
}

class PageCycleDeVie extends StatefulWidget {
  const PageCycleDeVie({super.key});

  @override
  State<PageCycleDeVie> createState() => _PageCycleDeVieState();
}

class _PageCycleDeVieState extends State<PageCycleDeVie> {
  bool _avecHorloge = true;
  bool _rouge = false;
  final List<String> _journal = [];
  String _recherche = '';
  bool _afficherRecherche = false;
  late final AppLifecycleListener _ecouteur;

  void _tracer(String message) {
     // The clock can warn of APRÈS the screen going dark (app closing)
    if (!mounted) return;
    setState(() => _journal.add('${heureCourante()} $message'));
  }

  @override
  void initState() {
    super.initState();
     // the app changes state: resumed (in the foreground), inactive,
     // hidden, paused (in the background)...
    _ecouteur = AppLifecycleListener(onStateChange: (etat) => _tracer('Application : ${etat.name}'));
  }

  @override
  void dispose() {
    _ecouteur.dispose();
    super.dispose();
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Title(
      title: _recherche.isEmpty ? 'Exemple 13' : 'Recherche : $_recherche',
      color: Colors.indigo,
      child: Scaffold(
        appBar: AppBar(title: const Text('Exemple 13 - le cycle de vie')),
        body: ListView(
          padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16),
          children: [
            Card(
              child: Padding(
                padding: const EdgeInsets.all(12),
                child: Column(
                  crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
                  children: [
                    CheckboxListTile(
                      contentPadding: EdgeInsets.zero,
                      controlAffinity: ListTileControlAffinity.leading,
                      title: const Text("afficher l'horloge"),
                      value: _avecHorloge,
                      onChanged: (v) => setState(() => _avecHorloge = v!),
                    ),
                    CheckboxListTile(
                      contentPadding: EdgeInsets.zero,
                      controlAffinity: ListTileControlAffinity.leading,
                      title: const Text('en rouge'),
                      value: _rouge,
                      onChanged: (v) => setState(() => _rouge = v!),
                    ),
                    if (_avecHorloge) Horloge(onJournal: _tracer, couleur: _rouge ? Colors.red : Colors.indigo),
                  ],
                ),
              ),
            ),
            Card(
              child: Padding(
                padding: const EdgeInsets.all(12),
                child: !_afficherRecherche
                    ? Align(
                        alignment: Alignment.centerLeft,
                        child: OutlinedButton(
                          onPressed: () => setState(() => _afficherRecherche = true),
                          child: const Text('Rechercher...'),
                        ),
                      )
                     // autofocus: focus as soon as the field appears
                    : TextField(
                        autofocus: true,
                        decoration: const InputDecoration(hintText: 'le titre suit la saisie'),
                        onChanged: (v) => setState(() => _recherche = v),
                      ),
              ),
            ),
            Text('Journal', style: Theme.of(context).textTheme.titleSmall),
            for (final (i, ligne) in _journal.indexed) Text('${i + 1}. $ligne', style: const TextStyle(fontSize: 12)),
          ],
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}
  • lines 56–61: the life of the application itself. On a phone, it goes into the background (you open another app, the screen turns off) and then returns: [AppLifecycleListener] notifies of each change ([resumed]: in the foreground; [inactive], [hidden], [paused]: switching to the background...). You would respond to these notifications to save a draft or stop a timer. The listener is created in [initState] and released in [dispose]: the same pattern as the clock timer;
  • line 95: checking the box displays the clock ([initState]); unchecking it hides it ([dispose]); changing its color redraws it ([didUpdateWidget]);
  • lines 112–115: a field that appears only after tapping “Search...”. [autofocus: true]: it gains focus as soon as it appears, and the phone’s keyboard opens;
  • line 68: the app title updates as you type.

We change the color, remove and then re-add the clock, open the search, and type a name:

The log shows the clock’s activity: start, color change, stop, start.

Students taking the [React] course will compare it with [useEffect]: what [React] writes to an effect and its cleanup function; [Flutter] distributes it between [initState] and [dispose]; what [React] obtains from an effect’s dependency table, [Flutter] obtains it using [didUpdateWidget], by comparing the old widget to the new one.

docs.title: 4.5. Example 14: Inherited Data
docs.text: How can you share data and functions between distant widgets without passing them from parameter to parameter through all the intermediaries? With inherited data, such as [InheritedWidget]. This is the mechanism that [Flutter] itself uses: [Theme.of(context)], [MediaQuery.of(context)], [Navigator.of(context)]... are inherited data reads. [React] calls this a context; [Angular] would refer to it as a service.

docs.title: 4.5.1. One data set for the entire application
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex14_donnees_heritees/suppliers/journal.dart - Data for the TOUTE application
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// How to share data and functions between widgets
// remote widgets, without passing them from parameter to parameter through all the
// intermediate ones? With a InheritedWidget, “inherited” data:
//    1. a FOURNISSEUR widget, located high in the tree, carries the data;
//    2. any descendant, at any depth, such as LIT
//       via context.dependOnInheritedWidgetOfExactType<Supplier>();
//    3. The descendant that read it is then ABONNÉ: it is reconstructed
//       when the data changes.
// This is the mechanism that Flutter itself uses: Theme.of(context),
// MediaQuery.of(context), Navigator.of(context)... are reads of
// legacy data.
//
// InheritedNotifier is a ready-made variant: the data is an object
// that PRÉVIENT tracks its changes (a ChangeNotifier, which calls
// notifyListeners()), and the provider then reconstructs its readers.
// Usage: a static method `of(context)` to read the data.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

// The data: a ChangeNotifier. notifyListeners() notifies its subscribers
class Journal extends ChangeNotifier {
  final List<String> lignes = [];

  void tracer(String message) {
    lignes.insert(0, '${DateTime.now().toString().substring(11, 19)} $message');
    if (lignes.length > 6) lignes.removeLast();
    notifyListeners();
  }
}

// The provider: it carries the newspaper and rebuilds its readers when
// the newspaper notifies of a change
class JournalFournisseur extends InheritedNotifier<Journal> {
  const JournalFournisseur({super.key, required Journal journal, required super.child}) : super(notifier: journal);

   // Reading: the provider most PROCHE above context
  static Journal of(BuildContext context) {
    final fournisseur = context.dependOnInheritedWidgetOfExactType<JournalFournisseur>();
    if (fournisseur == null) {
      throw FlutterError('JournalFournisseur.of : aucun JournalFournisseur au-dessus de ce widget');
    }
    return fournisseur.notifier!;
  }
}
  • lines 25–31: the shared data: a log. It is a [ChangeNotifier], an object that notifies its listeners of changes: every method that modifies it calls [notifyListeners()];
  • lines 37–38: the provider: a widget, located high in the tree, that holds the log. [InheritedNotifier] is a [InheritedWidget] ready for a [ChangeNotifier]: when the log notifies of a change, the provider rebuilds all the widgets that have read it;
  • Lines 41–46: Reading, via a static method [of(context)], as used by [Flutter]. [context.dependOnInheritedWidgetOfExactType<JournalFournisseur>()] traverses the tree from [context] up to the nearest provider and subscribes the widget that reads the data: it will be rebuilt when the data changes. If there is no provider above it, this is a programming error: it is clearly flagged.

docs.title: 4.5.2. Data provided by a widget
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex14_donnees_heritees/providers/panier.dart - Data provided by the UN widget
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The shopping cart is only provided to a portion of the tree: the widgets
// encompassed by PanierFournisseur (see main.dart). Two providers placed at
// two different locations on the screen would result in two independent shopping carts.
// The supplier here is a StatefulWidget: it is this supplier that CRÉE creates the shopping cart
// (didChangeDependencies) and releases it (disposes of it). The supplier uses the log itself.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

import 'journal.dart';

typedef Article = ({String libelle, double prix});

class Panier extends ChangeNotifier {
  final Journal _journal;
  final List<Article> articles = [];

  Panier(this._journal);

   // a calculated value: fold “folds” the list into a single value
  double get total => articles.fold(0, (somme, a) => somme + a.prix);

  void ajouter(Article article) {
    articles.add(article);
    _journal.tracer('panier : + ${article.libelle}');
    notifyListeners();
  }

  void retirer(int index) {
    _journal.tracer('panier : - ${articles[index].libelle}');
    articles.removeAt(index);
    notifyListeners();
  }
}

class PanierFournisseur extends StatefulWidget {
  final Widget child;

  const PanierFournisseur({super.key, required this.child});

   // reading, via the private widget _PanierHerite placed in build()
  static Panier of(BuildContext context) {
    final herite = context.dependOnInheritedWidgetOfExactType<_PanierHerite>();
    if (herite == null) {
      throw FlutterError('PanierFournisseur.of : aucun PanierFournisseur au-dessus de ce widget');
    }
    return herite.notifier!;
  }

  @override
  State<PanierFournisseur> createState() => _PanierFournisseurState();
}

class _PanierFournisseurState extends State<PanierFournisseur> {
  Panier? _panier; // null until it is created

   // called immediately after initState: the widget can then LIRE the data
   // inherited. getInheritedWidgetOfExactType: read the log SANS subscribe
   // to its changes (the shopping cart provider does not need to be rebuilt
   // every time the log changes)
  @override
  void didChangeDependencies() {
    super.didChangeDependencies();
     // ??=: the shopping cart is created only the first time
    _panier ??= Panier(context.getInheritedWidgetOfExactType<JournalFournisseur>()!.notifier!);
  }

  @override
  void dispose() {
    _panier?.dispose();
    super.dispose();
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) => _PanierHerite(notifier: _panier!, child: widget.child);
}

class _PanierHerite extends InheritedNotifier<Panier> {
  const _PanierHerite({required super.notifier, required super.child});
}
  • lines 17–24: the shopping cart, another [ChangeNotifier]. It receives the log upon creation to record every addition and removal. [fold] “collapses” the list into a single value: the sum of the prices;
  • lines 39–40: This time, the provider is a [StatefulWidget]: it is the one that creates the shopping cart and releases it. It is provided only to the widgets it encompasses ([child]);
  • lines 45–50: the private widget [_PanierHerite], which the provider places above its child, reads the data;
  • lines 65–68: the basket is created in [didChangeDependencies], which is called immediately after [initState], and from which a widget can read the inherited data. [??=]: this is created only the first time. [getInheritedWidgetOfExactType] reads the log SANS and subscribes to its changes: the shopping cart provider does not need to be rebuilt every time the log changes;
  • line 78: the provider places the inherited data above its child;
  • lines 81–82: the inherited data itself, which is private.

docs.title: 4.5.3. A configured provider
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex14_donnees_heritees/suppliers/horloge.dart - a supplier PARAMÉTRÉ
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A clock, whose refresh period is a parameter of the
// provider: HorlogeFournisseur(period: Duration(seconds: 5), ...).
// Two nested providers: a widget reads the one that is closest to it. PROCHE
// of it. This time, we write a InheritedWidget “by hand”: it is
// updateShouldNotify that determines whether the readers need to be rebuilt.
// The clock stops when its provider disappears (is unavailable).
// =========================================================================

import 'dart:async';

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

class HorlogeFournisseur extends StatefulWidget {
  final Duration periode;
  final Widget child;

  const HorlogeFournisseur({super.key, this.periode = const Duration(seconds: 1), required this.child});

   // The default value: a fixed date, read by a widget without a provider
  static DateTime of(BuildContext context) =>
      context.dependOnInheritedWidgetOfExactType<_HorlogeHeritee>()?.maintenant ?? DateTime(2026);

  @override
  State<HorlogeFournisseur> createState() => _HorlogeFournisseurState();
}

class _HorlogeFournisseurState extends State<HorlogeFournisseur> {
  DateTime _maintenant = DateTime.now();
  Timer? _minuterie;

  void _demarrer() {
    _minuterie?.cancel();
    _minuterie = Timer.periodic(widget.periode, (_) => setState(() => _maintenant = DateTime.now()));
  }

  @override
  void initState() {
    super.initState();
    _demarrer();
  }

   // If the parent changes the time period, the timer is restarted
  @override
  void didUpdateWidget(HorlogeFournisseur ancien) {
    super.didUpdateWidget(ancien);
    if (ancien.periode != widget.periode) _demarrer();
  }

  @override
  void dispose() {
    _minuterie?.cancel();
    super.dispose();
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) => _HorlogeHeritee(maintenant: _maintenant, child: widget.child);
}

class _HorlogeHeritee extends InheritedWidget {
  final DateTime maintenant;

  const _HorlogeHeritee({required this.maintenant, required super.child});

   // Called when the provider is rebuilt: should the
   // readers? Yes, if the time has changed
  @override
  bool updateShouldNotify(_HorlogeHeritee ancien) => ancien.maintenant != maintenant;
}
  • line 23: the read operation; without a provider, a default value (a fixed date). [?.]: if no provider is found, the result is [null], and [??] then takes the default value;
  • lines 34–36: a timer, with the period specified as a parameter;
  • lines 47–49: if the parent changes the period, the timer is restarted;
  • lines 62–70: this time, a [InheritedWidget] written “by hand.” It carries a piece of data (the time). Every time the provider is rebuilt (every second), [Flutter] calls [updateShouldNotify] with the old widget: if it returns [true], the widgets that read the data are rebuilt.

// =========================================================================
// lib/ex14_donnees_heritees/resume_panier.dart
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Another descendant: the MÊME shopping cart, but SA PROPRE
// clock, refreshed every 5 seconds. A widget only reads the
// feeds placed by AU-DESSUS: ResumePanier therefore places a second
// HorlogeFournisseur around its content, which it entrusts to a small
// widget, _Contenu (whose context is, in turn, SOUS this provider).
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

import 'fournisseurs/horloge.dart';
import 'fournisseurs/panier.dart';

class ResumePanier extends StatelessWidget {
  const ResumePanier({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return const HorlogeFournisseur(periode: Duration(seconds: 5), child: _Contenu());
  }
}

class _Contenu extends StatelessWidget {
  const _Contenu();

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final panier = PanierFournisseur.of(context);
    final maintenant = HorlogeFournisseur.of(context); // the nearest one: 5 seconds
    return Card(
      child: Padding(
        padding: const EdgeInsets.all(12),
        child: Column(
          crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
          children: [
            Text(
              'Panier (${panier.articles.length} article(s)) - ${maintenant.toString().substring(11, 19)}',
              style: Theme.of(context).textTheme.titleSmall,
            ),
            for (final (i, a) in panier.articles.indexed)
              Row(
                children: [
                  Text(a.libelle),
                  TextButton(onPressed: () => panier.retirer(i), child: const Text('retirer')),
                ],
              ),
            Text('Total : ${panier.total} €', style: const TextStyle(fontWeight: FontWeight.bold)),
          ],
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}
  • Line 21: The summary places a second clock provider, with a 5-second period, around its content. A widget only reads the providers placed above it: that is why the content is a separate widget, [_Contenu], whose [context] is SOUS—this provider (the [context] of [ResumePanier], meanwhile, is above it);
  • Lines 30–31: The MÊME is in the same basket as the catalog, but the closest clock is the 5-second one.

We add three items, then remove one:

docs.title: 4.6. Example 15: Reusing Behaviors
docs.text: A widget reuses a view. How do you reuse a behavior, along with its state (highlighting what’s tapped, triggering an action after a long press, giving focus on startup)? [React] has “custom hooks”; [Flutter] and [Dart] have three tools.

docs.title: 4.6.1. An “envelope” widget
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex15_comportements/surligneur.dart - behavior within a widget
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The first way to reuse a COMPORTEMENT (along with its state): a
// "wrapper" widget, which adds this behavior to any child.
//      Highlighter(color: ..., child: ListTile(...))
// This one highlights its child while you TOUCHE (with your finger on
// the screen), and, with a mouse (web, computer), while you SURVOLE.
// Each Highlighter has its own state: two lines do not interfere with each other.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

class Surligneur extends StatefulWidget {
  final Color couleur;
  final Widget child;

  const Surligneur({super.key, this.couleur = const Color(0xFFFFF3CD), required this.child});

  @override
  State<Surligneur> createState() => _SurligneurState();
}

class _SurligneurState extends State<Surligneur> {
  bool _touche = false;
  bool _survole = false;

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
     // MouseRegion: mouse movements; Listener: finger touches
     // (or clicks) at the lowest level
    return MouseRegion(
      onEnter: (_) => setState(() => _survole = true),
      onExit: (_) => setState(() => _survole = false),
      child: Listener(
        onPointerDown: (_) => setState(() => _touche = true),
        onPointerUp: (_) => setState(() => _touche = false),
        onPointerCancel: (_) => setState(() => _touche = false),
         // AnimatedContainer: a color change ANIMÉ (200 ms)
        child: AnimatedContainer(
          duration: const Duration(milliseconds: 200),
          color: _touche || _survole ? widget.couleur : Colors.transparent,
          child: widget.child,
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}
  • lines 32–34: [MouseRegion] notifies when the mouse enters or exits the widget (on the web or a computer; a phone does not have a mouse);
  • lines 35–38: [Listener] notifies, at the lowest level, of every finger touch (or every click): down, up, canceled;
  • lines 40–42: an animated [Container]: when its color changes, it transitions from the old color to the new one in 200 milliseconds, without requiring any additional code. [Flutter] has a whole family of these “implicitly animated” widgets: [AnimatedOpacity], [AnimatedPadding], [AnimatedAlign]...

[Surligneur] applies its behavior to any child: [Surligneur(child: ListTile(...))].

docs.title: 4.6.2. A widget that contains an animation
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex15_comportements/appui_long.dart - a long-press button
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
//      BoutonAppuiLong (duration: Duration(seconds: 1), onAction: delete, child: ...)
// The action is executed only if the button is held down for
// the entire duration: protection against accidental presses. A ring
// fills up while the button is pressed.
// The fill is a ANIMATION: a AnimationController produces a
// value ranging from 0 to 1 for the given duration, for each frame of
// screen. It requires a “ticker” (the frame rate): the mixin
// SingleTickerProviderStateMixin adds it to the State object. A MIXIN is
// is Dart’s way of reusing code across multiple classes (see
// autofocus.dart).
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

class BoutonAppuiLong extends StatefulWidget {
  final Duration duree;
  final VoidCallback onAction;
  final Widget child;

  const BoutonAppuiLong({
    super.key,
    this.duree = const Duration(seconds: 1),
    required this.onAction,
    required this.child,
  });

  @override
  State<BoutonAppuiLong> createState() => _BoutonAppuiLongState();
}

// "with": the State object also receives the code from the mixin
class _BoutonAppuiLongState extends State<BoutonAppuiLong> with SingleTickerProviderStateMixin {
  late final AnimationController _animation;

  @override
  void initState() {
    super.initState();
     // vsync: this: the ticker provided by the mixin
    _animation = AnimationController(vsync: this, duration: widget.duree)
       // end of the animation: the press lasted long enough
      ..addStatusListener((etat) {
        if (etat == AnimationStatus.completed) {
          _animation.reset();
          widget.onAction();
        }
      });
  }

   // when the widget is removed: no orphaned animation
  @override
  void dispose() {
    _animation.dispose();
    super.dispose();
  }

  void _commencer() => _animation.forward(from: 0);

   // the finger lifts too early: the ring empties
  void _arreter() {
    if (_animation.isAnimating) _animation.reverse();
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return GestureDetector(
      onTapDown: (_) => _commencer(),
      onTapUp: (_) => _arreter(),
      onTapCancel: _arreter,
       // AnimatedBuilder: reconstructs SEULEMENT this segment for each frame
      child: AnimatedBuilder(
        animation: _animation,
        builder: (context, child) => Row(
          mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,
          children: [
            SizedBox(
              width: 22,
              height: 22,
              child: CircularProgressIndicator(value: _animation.value, strokeWidth: 3, color: Colors.red),
            ),
            const SizedBox(width: 8),
            child!, // the child, built once and for all
          ],
        ),
        child: widget.child,
      ),
    );
  }
}
  • line 35: [with]: the [State] object also receives the code from a mixin. A mixin is how [Dart] reuses code across multiple classes without inheritance. This mixin provides a “ticker”—the refresh rate of the screen (60 frames per second or more)—which an animation requires;
  • lines 42–47: a [AnimationController] generates a value ranging from 0 to 1 for the specified duration, for each frame. [vsync: this]: the ticker provided by the mixin. [..addStatusListener(...)]: when the animation reaches the end ([completed]), the press has lasted long enough: the animation is reset to zero and the action is executed;
  • lines 59–63: the finger touches the button: the animation starts from 0; if it lifts too early, the animation rewinds;
  • lines 69–71: gestures: press, release, cancel (the finger has slipped off the button);
  • lines 73–87: [AnimatedBuilder] reconstructs only this portion of the screen for each frame of the animation: a ring ([CircularProgressIndicator]) whose value corresponds to the animation. The fixed element (the button text) is constructed once and for all ([child]), and passed to [builder].

docs.title: 4.6.3. A behavior in a mixin
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex15_comportements/autofocus.dart - a behavior in a MIXIN
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The second way to reuse a behavior: a mixin on `State`.
//      class _MaPageState extends State<MaPage> with FocusAuDemarrage { ... }
// The State object receives a FocusNode (focusDemarrage), which takes focus
// as soon as the screen is displayed, and is released along with it: the mixin
// complements initState and is available to the class that uses it.
// "on State<T>": this mixin applies only to a State object, which
// therefore use its methods (initState, dispose, mounted...).
// (For a simple field, the `autofocus: true` parameter in TextField does the
// same thing: the mixin demonstrates the mechanism, which can be reused for other purposes.)
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/widgets.dart';

mixin FocusAuDemarrage<T extends StatefulWidget> on State<T> {
  final focusDemarrage = FocusNode();

  @override
  void initState() {
    super.initState(); // the initState from the class (or mixin) “above”
     // after the initial display: the field exists, so we give it focus
    WidgetsBinding.instance.addPostFrameCallback((_) {
      if (mounted) focusDemarrage.requestFocus();
    });
  }

  @override
  void dispose() {
    focusDemarrage.dispose();
    super.dispose();
  }
}
  • line 17: a mixin that is applied only to an object [State] ([on State<T>]): it can therefore use its methods;
  • line 18: the [State] object that uses the mixin receives this field;
  • Lines 21–25: The mixin [initState] is completed: [super.initState()] calls the one from the "parent" class (that of [State], or another mixin). After the initial display, the field exists: focus is given to it. [mounted]: Is the [State] object still in the tree?;
  • lines 30–32: it also completes [dispose], to free up [FocusNode].

// =========================================================================
// lib/ex15_comportements/main.dart - reusing behaviors
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Three Flutter and Dart tools for reusing a COMPORTEMENT (and
// its state), rather than just a simple display:
//    - an “envelope” widget (Highlighter);
//    - a widget that contains an animation (BoutonAppuiLong);
//    - a State mixin (FocusAuDemarrage).
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

import 'appui_long.dart';
import 'autofocus.dart';
import 'surligneur.dart';

void main() {
  runApp(
    MaterialApp(
      debugShowCheckedModeBanner: false,
      theme: ThemeData(colorSchemeSeed: Colors.indigo),
      home: const PageComportements(),
    ),
  );
}

class PageComportements extends StatefulWidget {
  const PageComportements({super.key});

  @override
  State<PageComportements> createState() => _PageComportementsState();
}

// the mixin FocusAuDemarrage: this State object receives focusDemarrage
class _PageComportementsState extends State<PageComportements> with FocusAuDemarrage {
  final List<String> _medecins = ['Mme Marie PELISSIER', 'Mr Paul TATOU', 'Melle Sophie DUPONT'];
  String _message = '';

  void _supprimer(String nom) {
    setState(() {
      _medecins.remove(nom);
      _message = '$nom a été supprimé.';
    });
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Scaffold(
      appBar: AppBar(title: const Text('Exemple 15 - réutiliser des comportements')),
      body: ListView(
        padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16),
        children: [
          TextField(
            focusNode: focusDemarrage, // the FocusNode provided by the mixin
            decoration: const InputDecoration(hintText: 'ce champ a reçu le focus tout seul'),
          ),
          const SizedBox(height: 12),
          const Text(
            'Touchez les lignes ; maintenez un bouton appuyé une seconde pour supprimer.',
            style: TextStyle(color: Colors.grey),
          ),
          for (final (i, m) in _medecins.indexed)
            Surligneur(
              key: ValueKey(m),
               // every other line: the default color; the rest, green
              couleur: i.isEven ? const Color(0xFFFFF3CD) : const Color(0xFFD1E7DD),
              child: ListTile(
                title: Text(m),
                trailing: BoutonAppuiLong(
                  onAction: () => _supprimer(m),
                  child: const Text('Supprimer', style: TextStyle(color: Colors.red)),
                ),
              ),
            ),
          const SizedBox(height: 12),
          if (_message.isNotEmpty) Text(_message, style: const TextStyle(color: Colors.indigo)),
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}

  • line 54: the [FocusNode] provided by the mixin;
  • lines 63–71: each line is highlighted when tapped; its “Delete” button only takes effect after being held down for one second.

docs.title: 4.7. Example 16: A Reusable Confirmation Window
docs.text: “Are you sure?”: [Flutter] provides everything you need. The [showDialog] function displays a modal window on top of the screen and returns a [Future], populated with the value the window transmits when it closes.

docs.title: 4.7.1. The window
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex16_confirmation/confirmation.dart - “Are you sure?”
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Flutter provides everything you need: showDialog() displays a window
// MODALE on top of the screen and returns a Future, resolved with the value
// which the window transmits when it closes: Navigator.pop(context, value).
// The calling code is therefore very simple:
//
//      if (await confirm(context, 'Delete this doctor?')) { ... }
//
// Closing the window SANS (by tapping outside the window, pressing the Back button on the
// phone, or the Esc key) resolves the Future to null: we treat it
// as a "no".
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

Future<bool> confirmer(BuildContext context, String message) async {
  final reponse = await showDialog<bool>(
    context: context,
     // AlertDialog: a Material window, with a title, content, and buttons
    builder: (context) => AlertDialog(
      title: const Text('Confirmation'),
      content: Text(message),
      actions: [
         // autofocus: the "No" button (the least risky choice) has focus
        TextButton(autofocus: true, onPressed: () => Navigator.pop(context, false), child: const Text('Non, revenir')),
        FilledButton(
          style: FilledButton.styleFrom(backgroundColor: Colors.red),
          onPressed: () => Navigator.pop(context, true),
          child: const Text('Oui, confirmer'),
        ),
      ],
    ),
  );
  return reponse ?? false; // null: window closed without a response
}
  • line 18: a standard function that can be used anywhere a [context] is available;
  • lines 19–22: [showDialog] opens the window created by [builder] and returns a [Future<bool?>]: the value passed when the window closes;
  • lines 23–25: [AlertDialog] is the dialog box for [Material Design]: a title, content, and buttons;
  • line 27: [Navigator.pop(context, false)] closes the window by transmitting [false]. [autofocus]: the “No” button—the least risky option—has focus (accidentally pressing Enter does not delete anything);
  • line 36: Closing the window (SANS) by responding (tapping outside the window, pressing the phone’s Back button, or pressing the Esc key) resolves [Future] to [null]: this is treated as a “no.”

The calling code is then just as simple to write as with the browser’s [window.confirm]: [if (await confirmer(context, 'Supprimer ce médecin ?')) { ... }]. The client [React] required a context, a hand-crafted promise, and a “portal” to achieve the same result; with [Flutter], this is how Windows normally works.

docs.title: 4.7.2. Using
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// lib/ex16_confirmation/main.dart - use the confirmation window
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A deletion, followed by a fleeting message at the bottom of the screen (SnackBar),
// with a "Cancel" button: the other method, very common on mobile devices, to
// protect the user from making a mistake.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

import 'confirmation.dart';

typedef Contact = ({int id, String nom});

void main() {
  runApp(
    MaterialApp(
      debugShowCheckedModeBanner: false,
      theme: ThemeData(colorSchemeSeed: Colors.indigo),
      home: const PageContacts(),
    ),
  );
}

class PageContacts extends StatefulWidget {
  const PageContacts({super.key});

  @override
  State<PageContacts> createState() => _PageContactsState();
}

class _PageContactsState extends State<PageContacts> {
  final List<Contact> _contacts = [
    (id: 1, nom: 'Jean MARTIN'),
    (id: 2, nom: 'Alice DURAND'),
    (id: 3, nom: 'Luc GERMAN'),
  ];
  String _message = '';

   // an async function: it “waits” for the user’s response
  Future<void> _supprimer(Contact c) async {
    final oui = await confirmer(context, 'Supprimer le contact ${c.nom} ?');
     // After an `await`, the screen may have disappeared: we check to make sure it’s still there
    if (!mounted) return;
    if (!oui) {
      setState(() => _message = 'Suppression abandonnée.');
      return;
    }
    final position = _contacts.indexOf(c);
    setState(() {
      _contacts.remove(c);
      _message = '${c.nom} a été supprimé.';
    });
     // ScaffoldMessenger: displays a temporary message at the bottom of the screen
    ScaffoldMessenger.of(context).showSnackBar(
      SnackBar(
        content: Text('${c.nom} supprimé'),
        action: SnackBarAction(
          label: 'Annuler',
          onPressed: () => setState(() {
            _contacts.insert(position, c);
            _message = '${c.nom} est revenu.';
          }),
        ),
      ),
    );
  }

  Future<void> _toutSupprimer() async {
    final oui = await confirmer(context, 'Supprimer les ${_contacts.length} contacts ?');
    if (oui && mounted) {
      setState(() {
        _contacts.clear();
        _message = 'Tous les contacts ont été supprimés.';
      });
    }
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Scaffold(
      appBar: AppBar(title: const Text('Exemple 16 - une fenêtre de confirmation')),
      body: ListView(
        padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16),
        children: [
          for (final c in _contacts)
            ListTile(
              leading: const Icon(Icons.person),
              title: Text(c.nom),
              trailing: IconButton(
                icon: const Icon(Icons.delete_outline, color: Colors.red),
                onPressed: () => _supprimer(c),
              ),
            ),
          if (_contacts.isEmpty)
            const ListTile(
              title: Text('Aucun contact.', style: TextStyle(color: Colors.grey)),
            ),
          const SizedBox(height: 12),
          Align(
            alignment: Alignment.centerLeft,
            child: FilledButton(
              style: FilledButton.styleFrom(backgroundColor: Colors.red),
               // null: button disabled when the list is empty
              onPressed: _contacts.isEmpty ? null : _toutSupprimer,
              child: const Text('Tout supprimer'),
            ),
          ),
          const SizedBox(height: 12),
          if (_message.isNotEmpty) Text(_message, style: const TextStyle(color: Colors.indigo)),
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}
  • lines 41–44: a [async] function: it waits for the user’s response. After a [await], the screen may have disappeared (the user has left): we check that the user is still there ([mounted]) before modifying the state or calling [context]. The analyzer flags that this check was omitted;
  • lines 55–62: After deletion, a temporary message appears at the bottom of the screen ([SnackBar]), with a “Cancel” button that restores the contact to its original position. This is another method, very common on mobile devices, to protect the user from making a mistake: take immediate action, but allow the user to undo it;
  • line 105: [null] disables the button when the list is empty.

The confirmation window; then the deletion is complete, with its fleeting message:
